श्रीललितासहस्रनाम

Śrī Lalitā Sahasranāma

The Thousand Names of the Divine Mother

Samāsa-vigraha, word-by-word meanings,
summary and esoteric notes

About this Edition

This edition presents all 1000 names of the Lalitā Sahasranāma. For every name it gives the Sanskrit name, the samāsa-vigraha (grammatical analysis of the compound), word-by-word meanings, a summary of the meaning, and an esoteric note based on the commentary Saubhāgya-bhāskara of Bhāskararāya.

The names are arranged in ten sections of one hundred names each. Use the Contents button to jump to a section, the page box to jump to a page, and A− / A+ to change the size of the text.

Section 1

Names 1–100

नामानि १–१००

Nāma 1

श्रीमाता

Samāsa-vigraha

श्रिया युता श्रीयुता। श्रीयुता माता।

श्रिया माता।

श्रियं (लक्ष्मीं) माति (परिच्छिनत्ति। तेन अनवधिकश्रीरूपः मोक्षः)।

श्रियं (विषं) माति (कण्ठे स्थापयति)।

Word by word

श्री / श्रिया - Lakshmi, wealth, auspiciousness, splendour, learning.

युता - endowed with, possessed of.

माता - mother.

श्रियं माति - She measures, limits, classifies, distributes, or contains Śrī.

विषं माति - She holds poison in the throat; the feminine counterpart of Śrīkaṇṭha.

Meaning

(i) The supreme mother.

When we are in deep trouble, the first word uttered by us involuntarily is Ma. Human beings are afflicted by three kinds of Tapas (difficulties), which cannot be solved by the mother in her human form. The possession of the power to resolve these difficulties makes Her the “Superior Mother”. Worshipping Her, who has given birth to the whole world, will prevent birth again in this world from the mother’s womb. (353rd name can be compared). The best of love is mother’s affection. Hence to contemplate and worship Her as the mother will give us proximity to Her.

(ii) Sree means Lakshmee (goddess of wealth). Hence Sreemata means Lakshmee’s mother. Sree also means Saraswathi (goddess of learning). She is mother of both Lakshmee and Saraswathi.

(iii) Ma means “to measure”. Sreemata therefore means that She is capable of measuring wealth. One that measures is superior to the one that is measured. Ma also be interpreted to mean one who “distributes” or “classifies”. She is the one who classified the Vedas. From this angle, Sreedevee can also be indicated as Brahma and/or Vyasa. “Richo Yajumshi Samani Sahi Srihi Amrta Sadam” - when interpreted in this manner this name is masculine.

(iv) Sree means venom. One who held the venom in her throat (Mathi). Lord Parameshwara is called Srikanta because he retained the Halahala venom in his throat. The feminine form which is part of Him is also called by this same name.

(v) The prefix Sree is used to refer respectable men or objects - for instance Sree Chakra, Sree Vidya, Sree Sailam, etc. Thus She is aptly called as Sreemata, as she is the mother of the whole world. Moreover, the word Sree is itself auspicious. Is it not, hence appropriate to commence this series of thousand names with Sree?

(vi) This hymn of thousand names was first recited by the eight Vagdevata’s led by Vasini. They appeared from the word power of Sreedevee herself. They were ordained to perform this holy task of reciting this hymn at her behest. They, in turn, selected and dedicated these thousand names out of millions of powerful names, and, by way of reminiscing the mother’s boundless love and compassion bestowed on them, start this series with the name Sreemata (Mother).

(vii) Merging the three letters of Bala Mantra to the six consonants ha, sa, ka, la, ra and ta, we derive a three-part Mantra, which is indicated as Matha. This is contained in this name. This secret Mantra has to be learnt through an appropriate teacher, in a proper way.

(viii) There is a poem (Sloka) called “Mata Kundalini Kriya Madhumathee” in the book “Laghustuthi” written by a great Devee Upasakar, “Laghu Bhattarakar”. The word Mata mentioned here also has a special cryptic meaning. This name is an indication of that special meaning.

(ix) Mother here also indicates that She has given birth to the entire universe. It indicates one of the three main functions of the Supreme Being viz. creation. Vedas also reflect the same sense in Yatho Vaimani Bhoothani Jayanthee.

Esoteric note

अर्थ (Meaning): She who is "endowed with श्री". Therefore, she is the माता who is eternally accompanied by divine splendor and auspiciousness.

अर्थ (Meaning): The Mother who is accompanied by or identified with श्री.

अर्थ (Meaning): श्रियं माति इति श्रीमाता. She who measures, limits, or controls material लक्ष्मी (wealth). By putting a limit on material existence, she bestows the limitless, boundless state of मोक्ष (liberation).

अर्थ (Meaning): She who contains the श्री (poison) in her throat. This derivation identifies the Divine Mother directly with the cosmic action of containing the poison during the churning of the ocean, establishing non-difference from नीलकण्ठ (Shiva).

Nāma 2

श्रीमहाराज्ञी

Samāsa-vigraha

महती च असौ राज्ञी च महाराज्ञी। श्रीयुता महाराज्ञी श्रीमहाराज्ञी।

Word by word

श्री - auspiciousness, splendour, divine wealth.

महती - great.

राज्ञी - queen, ruler.

महाराज्ञी - great empress.

श्रीयुता महाराज्ञी - the great empress endowed with Śrī.

Meaning

(i) The great empress (that is the protector of the whole world); the second of the three functions of the Supreme Being viz. Protection is indicated in this place. The Vedas state the same thought as Yena Jatanee Jeevantee.

(ii) Three secret syllables of Sree Vidya are hidden in this name. They are to be learnt through an appropriate teacher, in a proper way.

(iii) Any king’s wife is called queen. A queen is called as Rajnee in Sanskrit. The wife of an emperor is Empress - Sreemaharajnee. It is not that Sreedevee is honoured because Her consort is an emperor. She on her own carries out the function of governance and hence She is Maharajnee.

Esoteric note

When Bhāskararāya decodes महाराज्ञी, he moves past the conventional meaning of a royal monarch ruling an empire and elevates it to cosmic and mantric planes:

I. The Sovereign of Manifestation and Dissolution

The title राज्ञी comes from the verbal root राज् (rāj), meaning "to shine" or "to illuminate."

She is the महाराज्ञी because She shines supreme as the independent, self-luminous consciousness (स्वप्रकाश चिद्रूप) that illuminates the entire universe.

Unlike planetary rulers or cosmic deities (like Indra or Brahmā) whose domains are temporary and bounded by time, Her sovereignty spans across all three cosmic states: creation (Sṛṣṭi), preservation (Sthiti), and dissolution (Saṃhāra).

II. The Ruler of the Nine Enclosures (Śrī Cakra)

In the esoteric geography of the Śrī Cakra, the three outermost lines are called the Bhūpura. Within the entire citadel (Śrī Nagara), She sits at the absolute center at the बिन्दु (Bindu).

Esoteric Mapping: As the महाराज्ञी, She is the absolute commanding consciousness of the entire cosmic diagram. All the peripheral or enclosure deities (Āvaraṇa Devatās) act merely as Her structural expansions or rays of light.

III. Resolution into Non-Duality (Advaita)

Bhāskararāya asserts that true sovereignty lies in the absence of a second entity. If there is a rival or a separate object, dominion is limited.

Because She is the non-dual supreme reality (Ekam-eva-advitīyam), there is nothing outside of Her. Her rule is absolute because the universe is Her own self-projection (Vimarśa). Therefore, श्रीमहाराज्ञी signifies the supreme, unconditioned state of absolute autonomy (स्वातन्त्र्य शक्ति).

Nāma 3

श्रीमत्सिंहासनेश्वरी

Samāsa-vigraha

सिंहचिह्नितासनं सिंहासनम्। सिंहासनस्य ईश्वरी।

आसनेषु सिंहः (श्रेष्ठम्)। श्रीमच्च तत्सिंहासनं च श्रीमत्सिंहासनम्। तस्य ईश्वरी।

सिंहः आसनं यस्याः सा सिंहासना। सिंहासना च असौ ईश्वरी च।

सिंहेन (हिंसया) असनं (क्षेपणं) सिंहासनम्। तत्र ईश्वरी (समर्था)।

श्रीमती च असौ सिंहासनेश्वरी च।

Word by word

श्रीमत् - splendid, auspicious, endowed with wealth.

सिंह - lion; also connected with power and majesty.

आसन - seat, throne.

सिंहासन - lion-throne, the royal throne.

ईश्वरी - sovereign lady, ruler, controller.

श्रीमत्सिंहासनस्य ईश्वरी - the sovereign of the auspicious lion-throne.

Meaning

(i) She controls and rules the world seated on a great grand throne.

(ii) The seat of a king is a throne - Simhasana. The seat of kings is designed as if the ruler is seated on a lion, because the lion is the king of animals. By virtue of Her position as a controller and ruler of World Empire, She is the lord of Simhasan, symbolises the wealth (Lakshmee) of the empire of the Universe and seated in this throne.

(iii) She herself rides on a lion and uses it as a seat. It also means that She is Simhavahinee - one who rides on a lion. According to Devee Puranam, the demon Mahishan was killed by Sreedevee riding on a lion. She thus acquired the names of Mahishagni (killer of Mahishan) and Simhasaneshwari.

(iv) The word Simha is derived from the verb Himsa. Simha is the corrupted form of Himsa. Thus Himsasaneshwari means, one who has the power to destroy the whole world - the third function of the Supreme Being, viz. to destroy, is indicated here. The Vedas refer to this as Yath Prayantyapi Samvisanthi.

(v) The previous name was Sreemaharajnee - the empress; it is therefore appropriate that she is seated on a Simhasana and is called Sreematsimhasaneshwaree.

(vi) At the end of the Devee Navavarga Pooja, a throne (Simhasana) with five steps is contemplated on the Bindu. Five forms of Sreedevee are imagined on each of these five steps in the four directions north-west, north-east, south-west, and south-east and in the centre. This worship is called Pancha Panchika. In the first step are seated the five Lakshmees viz. Sree Vidya Lakshmee, Lakshmee-Lakshmee, Mahalakshmee-Lakshmee, Trisakthi Lakshmee, and Sarvasamrajya Lakshmee. Since the throne on which Sreedevee is seated has these five Lakshmees, She is referred to as Sreematsimhasaneshwari.

(vii) There are also Mantras which carry the name Simhasana. These are to be contemplated on the four sides and in the centre of the Bindu as described below: Three in the East viz. Bala, Chaitanya, Bhairavi and Sampathprada Bhairavi. Five in the South viz. Kameshwari, Rakthanetra, Shatkuta Bhairavi, Aghora Bhairavi and Sampathprada Bhairavi. Seven in the West viz. Sanjeevani, Mrithyunjaya, Amruta Sanjeevani Bhairavi, Vaireshwari, Tripura Bhairavi, Bhayahari, and Sampathprada Bhairavi. Four in the North viz. DamarEshwari, Bhayadvamsini Bhairavi, Aghora Bhairavi and Sampathprada Bhairavi. Five in the Centre viz. Prathama Sundaree, Dwitheeya Sundaree, Tritheeya Sundaree, Chaturtha Sundaree and Panchama Sundaree.

The Mantras of these 24 Devatas are called Simhasana Mantras. Sreedevee is the lord (Eshwari) of these Mantras.

Thus, by the first three names, the three functions of creation, protection and destruction are indicated. Sreedevee has the name Panchakrityaparayana (274th name) - one who carries out five functions. The remaining two functions viz. Thirodhana and Anugraha will be dealt with later.

Esoteric note

She is the supreme ruler and residing deity of the royal throne of consciousness. The lion denotes absolute dominion over the created universe.

Bhāskararāya aligns this with the Śrī Cakra, where Her seat is composed of the highest cosmic principles (the Sadāśiva-mahāpreta-padmāsana). It stands supreme above all other divine seats or states of yogic absorption.

This directly maps Her identity to the cosmic power that rides upon the lion (the vehicle of Durgā / Jagadambā), representing the absolute control and direction of the untamed, kinetic energy of the cosmos (Rajo-guṇa).

This addresses the Saṃhāra-krama (the dissolution phase of consciousness). She is the sovereign power that completely eliminates Samsāra, throwing away the limitations of names and forms to reveal the undifferentiated Self.

It confirms that Her absolute rule over the throne of the universe is not dry or purely destructive, but is eternally infused with श्रीमद्—the nectarine, auspicious, and blissful light of pure awareness (Cit-vilāsa).

Nāma 4

चिदग्निकुण्डसम्भूता

Samāsa-vigraha

अग्नेः कुण्डम् अग्निकुण्डम्। चिद् एव अग्निकुण्डं वा चिदरूपं अग्निकुण्डं वा चिदग्निकुण्डम्।

तस्मात् सम्भूता चिदाग्निकुण्डसम्भूता। अथवा तत्र सम्यक् (अभेदेन) भूता (स्थिता)।

Word by word

चित् - consciousness, knowledge, Brahman.

अग्नि - fire.

कुण्ड - fire-pit, sacrificial pit.

चिदग्निकुण्ड - the sacrificial fire-pit of consciousness or knowledge.

सम्भूता - born, arisen, emerged, fully manifested.

चिदग्निकुण्डसम्भूता - She who emerged from the fire-pit of consciousness.

Meaning

(i) One, who emerged from the sacrificial fire of knowledge.

(ii) The word Chit means flawless Brahmam. It is called Chidagni as it is the enemy of the darkness of ignorance. Sreedevee emerged from the fire of Chit that is knowledge. In other words, Sreedevee’s real form emerges from the sacrificial fire of knowledge for the purpose of annihilating ignorance.

(iii) That knowledge as fire is mentioned in several places in Vedic and other spiritual literatures. For instance Gnanagni: Sarvakarmani Bhasmasat kurute tatha (Sreemad Bhagavat Geeta IV-37).

(iv) The legend of Bhandasura occurs in the same Brahmanda Purana where this Sahasranamam is also recited. Indra and other Devas performed a sacrifice to propitiate Sreedevee in order to destroy Bhandasura, who was harassing them. The sacrificial fire raised by them was called Chidagnikunda. Once the Devas started offering organs of their own bodies in the sacrificial fire, Sreedevee emerged from that pit (Kunda). The illusory “I” related to the physical and causal bodies, which are the root cause of self-esteem and arrogance (the false notions of “I”) was thrown into the fire by the Devas and Sreedevee, who is the real “I” emerged.

(v) There is one method of worship of Sreedevee called Rahooyaga. The fire of knowledge, which burns on its own without any fuel, is enhanced by adding the fuel of Vasanas. Attributes arising out of previous thoughts and actions and when the fire is aglow, all the good deeds, sins, thoughts, actions and duties are offered therein and the soul assumes the form of pure light, which is Sreedevee. (Refer 381st name - Rahooyagakramaradya). Antar nirantara nirindana medamanee moohandhakara paribandhini samvidagnow - this is the Mantra chant and the special argya is poured in the Samayika pooja after Tatvasodanam. This is the meaning of this name.

Esoteric note

When Bhāskararāya decodes this pivotal name—which marks the literal manifestation narrative of Lalitā Tripura-sundarī out of the Mahā-yāga (the great cosmic sacrifice)—he bypasses the external mythological imagery to unveil a dynamic internal transformation:

I. The Alchemical Dissolution of Duality

In external rituals, objects are offered into a physical fire-pit to be consumed. Esoterically, the चिदग्निकुण्ड is the internal fire of pure awareness (Jñānāgni). The Sādhaka pours the entire manifest universe, along with their individual ego (Jīva-bhāva), into this fire as an oblation (Āhuti). When all sense of separation is completely burned away, what remains and emerges out of that absolute void of consciousness is the supreme deity Herself—चिदग्निकुण्डसम्भूता.

II. The Awakening of the Absolute Ego (Ahaṃtā)

Bhāskararāya emphasizes that Her emergence from the fire-pit signifies that She is not created; rather, She manifests when the limitations of the objective mind are dissolved. As the phrase "तत्र सम्यक् अभेदेन स्थिता" implies, She does not leave the fire; She is the very stability of that non-dual consciousness. She represents the pure, unconditioned cosmic I-consciousness (विमर्श / पूर्णांहता) that dawns when the dry intellect is consumed by spiritual fire.

Nāma 5

देवकार्यसमुद्यता

Samāsa-vigraha

देवानां कार्याणि देवकार्याणि।

देवकार्याणां समुद्यता (शेषषष्ठ्या तदर्थं समुद्यता)।

Word by word

देव - devas, divine beings.

कार्य - work, task, purpose.

देवकार्य - the task or purpose of the Devas.

समुद्यता - risen, come forward, prepared, engaged.

देवकार्यसमुद्यता - She who has come forward for the purpose of the Devas.

Meaning

(i) One, who came forward to service Devas.

(ii) Why should Sreedevee, who is of eternal existence incarnate or take a particular form? The purpose is to help the Devas achieve their objectives. Devanam Karyasidhyartham Avirbhavati Sa Yada Utpanneetitada Lookee Sa Nithyapyabhidheeyathee (Saptashatee). The objective of the Devas is to annihilate the demons like Bhandasura, Mahishasura, etc. Although She is eternal, She takes an incarnation every time to remove the grievances of the Devas.

(iii) Demons like Bhandasura are monsters bound by ignorance. Actions arising out of ignorance with selfish goals, take the form of Devils. Sreedevee takes different incarnations to release the Devas from the bondage of ignorance so that they can carry out their respective divine functions. The 4th and 5th names describe Sreedevee’s Chit (Prakasa) form. The description of the Vimarsa form follows.

Esoteric note

When Bhāskararāya parses देवकार्यसमुद्यता, he transitions the text from a mythological battle blueprint (the request of the gods to slay Bhandāsura) into an active metaphysical and structural process within consciousness:

I. The True Identity of the "Devas"

In the esoteric vocabulary of the Agamas and Upaniṣads, the word देव (Deva) is derived from the root दिव् (div - to shine). Bhāskararāya establishes that the true Devas are the internal sensory organs and faculties of perception (इन्द्रियाणि), which illuminate the external and internal worlds. The Devakārya (task of the gods) is the liberation of these faculties from the tyrannical grip of भण्डासुर (Bhaṇḍāsura, who represents cosmic limitation, ignorance, and the ego). She is Samudyatā because Her entire manifest nature is geared toward freeing the senses from bondage.

II. The Dynamic Architecture of Grace (Anugraha)

The term समुद्यता signifies absolute readiness and immediate, active expression. Bhāskararāya observes that while pure Shiva remains in an unmoving, transcendent state (Prakāśa), Shakti is inherently Samudyatā—creatively upraised. She represents the kinetic projection of divine grace (Anugraha-śakti) that actively intervenes in the cosmos to restore equilibrium whenever the individual soul cries out for liberation.

III. The Resolution of Śeṣa-ṣaṣṭhī

By utilizing Śeṣa-ṣaṣṭhī ("the remaining genitive relations"), the grammar implies that Her relationship to the divine work is not an external chore or an accidental duty. The work is not separate from Her essence; rather, the protection, evolution, and ultimate dissolution of the universe back into the absolute is Her natural, spontaneous play (Līlā).

Nāma 6

उद्यद्भानुसहस्राभा

Samāsa-vigraha

उद्यतां भानूनां सहस्रम् उद्यद्भानुसहस्रम्। तस्य आभया तुल्या आभा यस्याः सा।

Word by word

उद्यत् - rising.

भानु - sun.

सहस्र - thousand; also infinite or countless.

आभा - lustre, colour, splendour.

उद्यद्भानुसहस्राभा - She whose lustre is like that of thousands of rising suns.

Meaning

(i) Her lustre is equal to thousands of rising Suns. The word Sahasram also means infinite.

(ii) Her lustre is equal to Infinite (thousands) rays of rising Suns.

(iii) The word Sahasram can be attributed to “Sun” or its “rays”. In that case Her splendor can be equated to countless (thousands) number of rising Suns or countless number of rays of a rising Sun.

(iv) The word Abha can be interpreted as “lustre” or “colour”. Sreedevee is famous both for her lustre as well as her Crimson colour. In the morning, the rising Sun graciously reduces his intensity of the heat emanating from his light, just for us to see his cherry coloured rays. Similarly Sreedevee is also of Crimson colour. This colour itself is called Aruna colour, one of the names of the Sun himself.

(v) Every mood or character has a colour. The colour of kindness or graciousness is Crimson.

(vi) In most of the places the Supreme Being is referred to as a column of light in scriptures: Na Tatra Suryo Bhati Na Chandra Tarakam; Jyotirmayam (Sakthi Mahimna Stooram); Jyotirmayee (Laghustuti); Many a place in Bhagavat Geeta; Vidyutdhamasamaprabham (Dyana Sloka of Sapta Sathi).

The Prakasa and Vimarsa forms Sreedevee have been described so far. The forthcoming names seek to detail three more forms viz. the Stula, Sukshma and Param forms. The Stula form is the one with human physical organs like hands, feet, etc. The Sukshma is in the form of Mantras. The Param is in the form of Vasanas. The Stula form is taken up first.

Esoteric note

When Bhāskararāya evaluates this precise structural form, he focuses heavily on the dynamic tension implied by उद्यताम् (actively rising) and सहस्रम् (infinite multiplication):

I. The Dynamic Spanda of Consciousness

Unlike a static sun sitting at its zenith, उद्यताम् signifies the precise moment of dawning—the transition from darkness to absolute illumination. In Mantra-Śāstra, this represents स्पन्द (Spanda), the initial throb or kinetic leap of consciousness as it moves from the unmanifest (Prakāśa) to manifest awareness (Vimarśa). She is not merely light; She is the dynamic, active dawning of absolute reality within the practitioner's consciousness.

II. The Dissolution of Mental Obscurity

A single sun removes the darkness of the external world, but it leaves shadows. The imagery of a thousand rising suns shining simultaneously means there is no possibility of a shadow anywhere in the cosmos. Bhāskararāya notes that this represents the total, instantaneous destruction of मूलाविद्या (mūlāvidyā, root cosmic ignorance). When Her light dawns in the Dahara-ākāśa (the inner space of the heart), the illusion of division is instantly incinerated by the uniform red glow of non-dual awareness.

III. The Radiance of the Kāmakalā

The intense red luster of the rising suns specifically encrypts the red seed-potency of the Śrī Vidyā triad. Bhāskararāya frequently references that this specific shade of red (Aruṇa) represents unconditional compassion (Karuṇā) and absolute autonomy (Svātantrya). The infinite rays are the letters of the alphabet (Mātṛkās) spreading outward to construct the universe, all anchored in Her singular, self-luminous essence.

Nāma 7

चतुर्बाहुसमन्विता

Samāsa-vigraha

चतुर्भिः बाहुभिः समन्विता।

Word by word

चतुर्भिः - with four.

बाहुभिः - arms, hands.

समन्विता - endowed with, possessed of.

चतुर्बाहुसमन्विता - She who is endowed with four arms.

Meaning

(i) One with four hands.

(ii) Sreedevee has four hands - two from each shoulder in front and back. The four hands only have been indicated in the forms usually contemplated during meditation. Hands come first and foremost whenever we try to concentrate on the form mentioned in the Dhyana Sloka (meditation verse).

(iii) The four Devees who are the commandants of Sreedevee’s army viz. Ashwaruda, Sampatkaree, Mantreenee and Varahee, may be deemed to be the four hands of Sreedevee.

(iv) The Mantras pertaining to the above four Devees are indicated by this name.

(v) The Dhyana verse of this Sahasranamam mentions only two hands for Sreedevee. Preceding part may be referred for the meaning of the Dhyana Sloka (meditation verse). Mention was made about the four hands and followed by the weapons carried in these four hands.

Esoteric note

When Bhāskararāya parses चतुर्बाहुसमन्विता, he moves beyond the anthropomorphic visual representation to reveal the underlying cosmic architecture and internal psychological framework:

I. The Mastery Over the Antaḥkaraṇa (Internal Organs)

Bhāskararāya establishes that the four arms are the physical symbols of the four divisions of the internal psyche (अन्तःकरणचतुष्टय).

The Four Faculties: मनस् (Manas - the deliberating mind), बुद्धि (Buddhi - the decisive intellect), चित्त (Citta - the memory/retentive consciousness), and अहङ्कार (Ahaṅkāra - the ego-sense).

By being perfectly integrated with these four arms, She signifies that the individual human psyche is merely a limited reflection of Her four cosmic vectors of awareness. She holds absolute command over the psychological mechanism of every living being.

II. The Structural Anchors of the Śrī Cakra

In the ritual mapping of the Śrī Cakra, the four arms correspond directly to the weapons She wields, which occupy specific spatial directions in the central chamber (Bindu-cakra).

The arms represent the deployment of Her primordial cosmic energies: इच्छा (Icchā - Will), ज्ञान (Jñāna - Knowledge), and क्रिया (Kriyā - Action).

The four arms represent the four standard paths of Vedic revelation (the four Vedas) and the four absolute states of consciousness (Jāgrat, Svapna, Suṣupti, and Turīya), showing that She encompasses both the transactional states of experience and the transcendent reality.

III. The Resolution of Samanvitā

The prefix सम् (sam) implies perfection and absolute equilibrium, while अन्विता (anvitā) implies an inseparable, intrinsic connection (anvaya). Bhāskararāya notes that these four arms are not accidental appendages attached to Her form; they are the natural, spontaneous structural expansions of Her non-dual essence as She projects outward from the unmanifest point into cosmic play (Līlā).

Nāma 8

रागस्वरूपपाशाढ्या

Samāsa-vigraha

राग एव स्वं रूपः यस्य पाशस्य सः रागस्वरूपपाशः। तेन आढ्या।

Word by word

राग - attachment, desire, love.

स्वरूप - own form, essential nature.

पाश - noose, rope, bond.

आढ्या - endowed with, rich in, furnished with.

रागस्वरूपपाशाढ्या - She who is furnished with the noose whose very form is desire.

Meaning

(i) One who carries the weapon of desire in the form of a noose.

(ii) A noose is a rope thrown to tie and drag something. Sreedevee is holding both the ends of the noose in one hand. It is in the Stula form in her rear left arm. The presiding deity is Ashwaruda.

(iii) Raga and Anuraga are the two features of mind - wish and desire. This is the Vasana form of the weapon noose. This form has the twin opposite characters viz. love and hatred. Vasana is the effect of the deeds of previous births of Jeeva. In the hands of Sreedevee these take the form of Iccha Sakti and Gnana Sakti.

(iv) The noose helps us to round up and drag a distant object to oneself. We will be able to do this only if both the ends of the noose are under our control. Sreedevee holds both the ends of the noose in her hand. This indicates that “our wishes will get fulfilled automatically by Her grace.”

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya completely deconstructs the conventional concept of a weapon (pāśa) used to bind an enemy, transmuting it into a profound non-dual instrument of liberation:

I. The Transmutation of Rāga (Desire)

For ordinary bound souls (jīvas), rāga is an afflictive mental modification (kleśa) that binds them tightly to the objective wheel of births and deaths. However, Bhāskararāya explains that when this same power belongs to the Divine Mother, it is इच्छाशक्ति (Icchā-śakti—the primordial Will of the Absolute). It is the pure, cosmic desire to manifest, play, and ultimately reclaim all projected beings. By holding this noose, She demonstrates that She controls the very fabric of cosmic attraction.

II. The Noose as the Gravity of Grace

Linguistically, a noose catches, pulls, and restrains an object that is moving away. Bhāskararāya asserts that Her noose represents the inward-pulling gravity of Her divine grace (anugraha). When the practitioner's mind wanders outward into the multi-colored illusions of the world, Her pāśa catches the outward-bound consciousness and pulls it firmly back toward the silent center—the Bindu.

III. The Structural Placement in Worshipping the Śrī Cakra

Bhāskararāya notes that this weapon is held in Her lower-left hand and is structurally related to the element of space and sound. In the ritual meditation (dhyāna), the Sādhaka visualizes this noose not as a rope of bondage, but as a radiant, loop of absolute crimson light that represents the ultimate beauty and captivating power of the Self (Ātma-rati).

Nāma 9

क्रोधाकाराङ्कुशोज्ज्वला

Samāsa-vigraha

क्रोधस्य आकार इव आकारः यस्य अङ्कुशस्य सः क्रोधाकाराङ्कुशः। तेन उज्ज्वला।

Word by word

क्रोध - anger.

आकार - form, shape; also knowledge as the form taken by the mind.

अङ्कुश - goad, elephant-hook.

उज्ज्वला - shining, resplendent.

क्रोधाकाराङ्कुशोज्ज्वला - She who shines with the goad whose form is anger.

Meaning

(i) Her lustre is enhanced by holding the goad symbolising anger.

(ii) Goad is a pointed weapon used by a mahout to control an elephant. It has a sharp edge. Elephant is one of the biggest and strongest among all animals. It is extremely difficult to control a rogue elephant. Goad is the only weapon which can control it. In the hands of Sreedevee it is in a Stula form.

(iii) Its Vasana form is anger. If the mind is not able to get what it wants or does not derive the satisfaction expected out of it the mental reaction is anger. It is symbolised by the lustrous goad worn by Sreedevee.

(iv) Krodhakarankusham can be interpreted in two ways - (1) Goad in the form of anger or (2) Anger and Akara (knowledge). How is Akara interpreted as knowledge? When we see an object through our eyes, our mind recognises and takes the “form” (photo print) of that object - that is Akara. If we see a book, our mind recognises the form of the book and becomes that form (Akara) itself. Then only we understand that what we see is a book or have the knowledge that it is a book. Recognition of all the objects by the mind taking the form (Akara) of that object. Hence the word Akara gives the meaning as knowledge.

(v) Anger is a state of mind arising out of the knowledge of an object. Sreedevee adorns the goad that controls anger. Knowledge about an object is destroyed in order to annihilate anger.

(vi) A weapon will act as intended by the person who takes aim. Here these weapons will act as per the wish of Sreedevee. For worshippers of Sreedevee, She will make the “desire” and “hatred” act according to the wishes of the devotees and ultimately raise them to Her level.

Esoteric note

In the *Saubhāgyabhāskara*, Bhāskararāya decodes the goad (*aṅkuśa*) as **क्रोध** (aversion or anger)[cite: 1].

* **The Power of Restraint:** While anger in ordinary mortals is a binding mental modification, in Her hands, the goad represents the power of **ज्ञानशक्ति** (*Jñāna-śakti* — the power of pure discernment).

* **Cosmic Correction:** Just as a goad keeps an elephant on the right track, Her goad reins in the outward-bound senses, stopping the mental fluctuations and redirecting the mind toward inner absorption (*Samādhi*).

Nāma 10

मनोरूपेक्षुकोदण्डा

Samāsa-vigraha

मन एव रूपं यस्य इक्षोः सः मनोरूपेक्षुः। इक्षुमयं कोदण्डं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

मनस् - mind.

रूप - form.

इक्षु - sugarcane.

कोदण्ड - bow.

मनोरूपेक्षु - sugarcane whose form is mind.

मनोरूपेक्षुकोदण्डा - She who bears the sugarcane bow whose form is mind.

Meaning

(i) She dons a bow made of sugarcane - the physical form of “mind”.

(ii) Sreedevee has in her left forearm a bow made of sugarcane. Its symbolic form is the mind. Its presiding deity is Mantrini.

(iii) The action of the mind executed through the five organs is to take the form of the object seen and realise that “I see the object”, “This can give me pleasure”, “I desire to get this object”, “This gives me sorrow and hence I should avoid it” and the like. This is called Sankalpa. At the same time the thought “Is this object suitable for me or not”, “Should I try to get it or not”, and the like are called Vikalpa. The action of the mind is of these two types. This mind takes the form of sugarcane bow in the hands of Sreedevee.

(iv) In general a bow is made up of completely dry bamboo slats and is capable of being bent and unbent. Sugarcane is full of moisture; Sugarcane bow is a weapon, though it is sweet; again it is sweet though it is a weapon. It shows that Sreedevee’s mind is full of benignity. Is it not Her mind full of sweetness and graciousness?

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya notes that the sugarcane bow represents **मनस्** (*Manas*), the choosing and doubting mind.

* **The Sweetness of the Mind:** Sugarcane must be crushed and processed to yield its sweet juice; similarly, the mind must be systematically refined through spiritual discipline to experience its inherent, nectarine bliss (*Svātmānanda*).

* **The Seat of Kriyā-śakti:** Because She holds the mind as an instrument (*kodaṇḍa*), She proves that the cosmic mind is entirely under Her command as **क्रियाशक्ति** (*Kriyā-śakti* — the power of action).

Nāma 11

पञ्चतन्मात्रसायका

Samāsa-vigraha

पञ्च तन्मात्राणि एव सायकाः यस्याः सा।

Word by word

पञ्च - five.

तन्मात्राणि - subtle sense-elements; sound, touch, form/colour, taste, smell.

सायकाः - arrows.

पञ्चतन्मात्रसायका - She whose arrows are the five tanmatras.

Meaning

(i) One who has five characteristics as arrows.

(ii) In her physical form, Sreedevee has five flowers as arrows in her right forearm viz. Lotus, Red Lotus, Red Lily, Red Jasmine and Mango flower. The characteristics of these arrows are the effect they make on the objects attacked by them viz. to induce happiness, to give taste, to enthrall, to dry out and to kill. The presiding deity of these arrows is Varahi also known as Dandanatha.

(iii) The secret form of these arrows is the five self-characteristics (Tanmatras). These characteristics are the unique features of the five elements, which constitute the physical earth. Elements (Bhutas) and Self-Characteristics (Tanmatras): Space (Akasa) - Sound (Shabda); Wind / Air (Vayu) - Sense of touch (Sparsa); Fire (Agni) - Form / Colour (Rupa); Water (Jala) - Taste (Rasa); Earth (Prithvi) - Odour (Gandha). These characteristics stand alone only in the very intricate and atomic state of the elements. The Universe, we perceive is the composite form of these elements and hence each element cannot be perceived separately. Before the evolution of the universe, from the Absolute (Mulaprakriti), i.e. when matter and energy are in a state of indistinguishable union, the elements could be identified by their individual characteristics - space by sound, air by sense of touch and so on. In this state these are called Tanmatras.

(iv) The arrows hit their targets and give their desired effect, as intended by the person who aims them. A sincere devotee targeted by Sreedevee’s arrow will experience the good and pleasurable effects of these characteristics. If the devotee is insincere (bad in intention), the arrows also will give only undesirable effects such as agitation or disturbance, maddening or intoxication, etc.

(v) These arrows have three forms in three different states - in the physical (Stula) state, they take the form of flowers; in the secret (Sukshma) state, they are Mantras; and in the Vasana state they take the form of Para, a form of sound.

(vi) Sreedevee also has weapons - Sugarcane as bow and flowers as arrow, like Cupid (Manmatha). Hence She is called as Lalita or Kameshwari. As the emotion of love (Sringara rasa) is important to Her, She is endowed with beautiful things as weapons.

(vii) The presiding deity of sugarcane bow is Mantrini representing the power of intellect (Buddhi Sakti) and the presiding deity of arrows is Dandanatha - commander-in-chief representing the physical power. The Vag Devees symbolically emphasise that intellect and power should act in unison.

(viii) Mantras of the weapons described are encompassed in these names 8 to 11. These are so secret that they should be learnt through a proper teacher.

Esoteric note

The five floral arrows are the five *Tanmātras*: sound (*śabda*), touch (*sparśa*), form (*rūpa*), taste (*rasa*), and smell (*gandha*).

* **Dissolution of Sensory Leakage:** Usually, these five elements pull human attention outward into physical attachment. When She shoots these floral arrows into the practitioner's heart, they pierce the outer sensory layer and dissolve objective experience, returning the senses to their pure, uncompounded state within consciousness.

Nāma 12

निजारुणप्रभापूरमज्जद्ब्रह्माण्डमण्डला

Samāsa-vigraha

निजः (स्वकीयः) यः अरुणप्रभायाः पूरः निजारुणप्रभापूरः।

तस्मिन् मज्जन्तीति निजारुणप्रभापूरमज्जानि।

तेषामेव ब्रह्माण्डानां मण्डलानि यस्याः सा।

Word by word

निज - own, natural.

अरुण - red, crimson.

प्रभा - lustre, light.

पूर - flood, fullness, flow.

मज्जत् - sinking, immersed.

ब्रह्माण्ड - universe, cosmic egg, galaxy.

मण्डल - sphere, zone, circle.

निजारुणप्रभापूरमज्जद्ब्रह्माण्डमण्डला - She in whose own crimson lustre the spheres of universes are immersed.

Meaning

(i) One who immerses the zones of galaxy by the flow of her lustre.

(ii) Our Earth, space and the stellar zone constitute one galaxy (Brahmandam). Universe (Brahmandamandalam) consists of millions of such galaxies. Sreedevee sinks this entire universe in her red lustre. Again the red lustre alone shines immersing them all.

(iii) The physical form of Sreedevee’s red lustre is described in the ensuing names. This description starts from Her hair and ends in Her feet.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya uses this name to prove *Advaita-vāda* (non-duality) and the primacy of *Shakti*:

* **The Red Flood of Vimarśa:** The red glow represents **विमर्श** (*Vimarśa* — self-reflective consciousness). The universe is not a dry, external entity sitting apart from Her. It is entirely suspended, sustained, and dissolved (*majjat*) inside Her infinite, self-luminous red light of awareness.

Nāma 13

चम्पकाशोकपुन्नागसौगन्धिकलसत्कचा

Samāsa-vigraha

चम्पकानि च अशोकाश्च पुन्नागाश्च चम्पकाशोकपुन्नागाः।

तैः लसन्तः कचाः यस्याः सा।

Word by word

चम्पक - champaka / magnolia flower.

अशोक - ashoka flower.

पुन्नाग - punnaga flower.

सौगन्धिक - fragrant, red lotus / fragrant flower.

लसत् - shining, bedecked, adorned.

कचा - hair.

चम्पकाशोकपुन्नागसौगन्धिकलसत्कचा - She whose hair shines adorned with fragrant flowers such as Champaka, Ashoka, Punnaga and Red Lotus.

Meaning

(i) One who has beautiful hair studded with Magnolia, Asoka, Rhizophora mucronata (Punnaga) and Red Lotus flowers.

(ii) It is Sreedevee’s hair bedecked with flowers, which emerges first out of the sacrificial fire; hence the description of the Sreedevee’s physical form commences with the hair.

(iii) The first part of Her mantra is equated with Her face. Hence the description starts with the hair. (for instance 85th name - Sreemad Vagbhava Kootikaswarupa Mukapankaja).

Esoteric note

This name initiates the *Keśādi-pāda-varṇana* (head-to-toe description) of the Devi.

* **Esoteric Hair as Chidākāśa:** The dark, dense tresses (*kaca*) represent the unmanifest primordial cosmic space (*Chidākāśa*). The shining, fragrant flowers represent the active, manifest seeds of spiritual wisdom and virtue blossoming within the crown chakra (**सहस्रार** — *Sahasrāra*).

Nāma 14

कुरुविन्दमणिश्रेणीकनत्कोटीरमण्डिता

Samāsa-vigraha

कुरुविन्दमणीनां श्रेणी कुरुविन्दमणिश्रेणी।

तया कनत् (दीप्यमानः) कोटीरः (मुकुटः) कुरुविन्दमणिश्रेणीकनत्कोटीरः।

तेन मण्डिता।

Word by word

कुरुविन्दमणि - ruby gemstone.

श्रेणी - row, string, series.

कनत् - shining, glittering.

कोटीर - crown.

मण्डिता - adorned.

कुरुविन्दमणिश्रेणीकनत्कोटीरमण्डिता - She who is adorned with a crown glittering with rows of ruby stones.

Meaning

(i) Kuruvindamani is the precious stone Ruby. Sreedevee’s crown is studded with a string of Rubies.

(ii) Adorning of rubies will result in fulfillment of desires. Attachment will be created to good things; desire, affection, welfare and devotion to Sree Vishnu also.

(iii) Sreedevee’s crown is of Koteera model. This is a particular design, which does not hide beauty of the hair as well as the flowers adorned. The crowns worn by men will hide the hair and is called Makuta, Mukuta or Kireeta.

(iv) The red rubies match the red lustre of Sreedevee’s body.

(v) Meditation of Sreedevee’s face with the crown will increase the devotion.

Esoteric note

* **Sovereignty of the Unmanī:** *Kuruvinda* denotes a rare class of crimson ruby. The crown (*koṭīra*) sits above the head, symbolizing the transcendent state above the Sahasrāra—known as **उन्मनी** (*unmanī*) or the state of pure, non-dual sovereignty over all creation.

Nāma 15

अष्टमीचन्द्रविभ्राजदलिकस्थलशोभिता

Samāsa-vigraha

अष्टम्यां चन्द्रः अष्टमीचन्द्रः।

अलिकस्य (ललाटस्य) स्थलम् अलिकस्थलम्।

अष्टमीचन्द्रेण इव विभ्राजता अलिकस्थलेन शोभिता।

Word by word

अष्टमी - eighth lunar day.

चन्द्र - moon.

विभ्राजत् - shining brilliantly.

अलिकस्थल - forehead.

शोभिता - beautified, made splendid.

अष्टमीचन्द्रविभ्राजदलिकस्थलशोभिता - She whose forehead shines like the moon of the eighth lunar day.

Meaning

(i) One whose forehead shines like the Moon on the eighth day of lunar half month.

(ii) Of the fifteen phases of the moon, on the eighth day of bright lunar half month the eighth phase will be seen. Or reduced upto eight phases on the eighth day of the lunar dark half month and moon will be visible as a semicircle. In the emerging form of Sreedevee from the sacrificial fire, the crown, hair and flowers come out one after the other and the forehead emerges as an inverted semicircle resembling the eighth day moon, with flawless cool light.

(iii) This can be compared to 46th verse of Soundaryalaharee starting with Lalatam Lavanyadvithi Vimalamabhati.

Esoteric note

* **The Light of the Ājñā:** The eighth-day moon is a perfect, balanced semi-circle. The forehead represents the seat of the **आज्ञा चक्र** (*Ājñā Cakra*), the gateway of intuitive knowledge. It represents the *Kāmakaḷā* structure, wherein the crescent moon represents the upper dynamic arc holding the equilibrium of Shiva and Shakti.

Nāma 16

मुखचन्द्रकलङ्काभमृगनाभिविशेषका

Samāsa-vigraha

मुखम् एव चन्द्र इति रूपकं तत्कलङ्कत्वेन तुल्यः मृगनाभेः (कस्तूर्याः) विशेषकः (तिलकः) यस्याः सा।

Word by word

मुख - face.

चन्द्र - moon.

कलङ्क - dark mark, spot.

आभ - resembling.

मृगनाभि - musk.

विशेषक - tilaka, decorative mark.

मुखचन्द्रकलङ्काभमृगनाभिविशेषका - She whose musk tilaka resembles the dark mark on the moon-like face.

Meaning

(i) The bindi (musk dot) on the forehead of Sreedevee resembles the black spot on the surface of the Moon and it further beautifies the face.

(ii) It is a literary tradition to consider the black spot on the moon as a stain on the life of the Moon god. The Moon is sometimes described as Mruganka, as the stain looks like a deer and as Sasanka as the stain also looks like a rabbit. When Sreedevee’s forehead is described as a semicircular Moon (crescent), there is no stain, but the musk spot beautifies the face.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya offers a profound interpretation of the "blemish" (*kalaṅka*):

* **Māyā as an Ornament:** The dark spot on the moon is traditionally a flaw, but on the face of consciousness (the Devi), the black musk mark (*tilaka*) increases Her beauty. This represents **माया** (*Māyā*). To the bound soul, *Māyā* is a blemish of ignorance; but to the Devi, it is a mere decorative ornament of Her creative play (*Līlā*), entirely under Her sovereignty.

Nāma 17

वदनस्मरमाङ्गल्यगृहतोरणचिल्लिका

Samāsa-vigraha

वदनम् एव स्मरस्य माङ्गल्यगृहं तस्य तोरण एव चिल्लिका (भ्रूलता) यस्याः सा।

Word by word

वदन - face.

स्मर - Cupid, Manmatha.

माङ्गल्यगृह - auspicious house.

तोरण - festoon, arch at entrance.

चिल्लिका - eyebrow-creeper.

वदनस्मरमाङ्गल्यगृहतोरणचिल्लिका - She whose eyebrows are the festoons at the auspicious house of Cupid, which is Her face.

Meaning

(i) One whose eyebrows look like festoons in front of Cupid’s house which is Sreedevee’s face.

(ii) The roof at the entrance of the houses will be constructed in a raised manner so that the house is not affected by rain or Sunshine. This is called festoon. Sreedevee’s face is so beautiful as to infatuate Sree Kameshwara. Hence Cupid uses this face as an office for his auspicious activities. The eyebrows look like beautiful festoons in front of this house (office).

Esoteric note

* **The Primal Throb (Spanda):** *Smara* (Cupid) is the cosmic desire for manifestation. Her face is the palace where this auspicious creation begins. The curve of Her eyebrows (*cillikā*) represents the creative tension or vibration (**स्पन्द** — *Spanda*) that triggers the projection of space and time.

Nāma 18

वक्त्रलक्ष्मीपरीवाहचलन्मीनाभलोचना

Samāsa-vigraha

वक्त्रलक्ष्म्याः मुखकान्तेः परीवाहे चलद्भ्यां मीनाभ्यां तुल्ये लोचने यस्याः सा।

Word by word

वक्त्र - face.

लक्ष्मी - beauty, splendour.

परीवाह - stream, flow.

चलत् - moving.

मीन - fish.

आभ - resembling.

लोचना - eyes.

वक्त्रलक्ष्मीपरीवाहचलन्मीनाभलोचना - She whose eyes resemble fish moving in the stream of the beauty of Her face.

Meaning

(i) One whose eyes look like fish swimming in the stream of beauty of Sreedevee’s face.

(ii) The beauty of Sreedevee’s face undergoes momentary changes and this continuous change looks like a steady and slow stream. The motion of Sreedevee’s two eyes is compared to the fast movement of fish in this stream, which increases its beauty.

(iii) Fish are not mammals but lay eggs. It is believed that fish nurse their offspring just by affectionate looks. Similarly, Sreedevee’s eyes, which are compared to fish swimming in the stream of beauty uplifts Her devotees just by a gracious look. She is therefore called Meenakshi, here referred to as Meenabhalochana.

Esoteric note

* **Solar and Lunar Currents:** Fish animate the water in which they swim. Esoterically, the two eyes represent the cosmic tracks of the Sun and the Moon, or the twin subtle channels **इडा** (*Iḍā*) and **पिङ्गला** (*Piṅgalā*). Their movement (*calat*) governs the rhythmic cycles of cosmic time.

Nāma 19

नवचम्पकपुष्पाभनासादण्डविराजिता

Samāsa-vigraha

नवचम्पकस्य पुष्पं नवचम्पकपुष्पम्। तेन तुल्यः नासादण्डेन विराजिता।

नवचम्पकपुष्पाभनासादण्डविराजिता - She whose nose shines like a fresh Champaka flower.

Meaning

(i) One whose nose is like a fresh Champaka flower.

(ii) Nava can be interpreted as “new” or “partly blossomed”. A partly blossomed Champaka bud generates a pleasant aroma.

Esoteric note

* **The Path of Suṣumṇā:** The Campaka bud is perfectly linear and flawless. In *Kuṇdoṣṭi-yoga*, the straightness of the nose bridge is the physical external indicator of the straight alignment of the **सुषुम्णा नाडी** (*Suṣumṇā Nādī*). Its linear beauty represents the straight path of the ascending lifeforce (*Prāṇa*).

Samāsa-vigraha

तारायाः कान्तिं तिरस्करोतीति ताराकान्तितिरस्कारि। तदेव नासाभरणम्। तेन भासुरा (शोभमाना)।

Word by word

तारा - star; also name of a deity.

कान्ति - lustre, brilliance.

तिरस्कारि - surpassing, putting to shame.

नासाभरण - nose ornament, nose ring.

भासुरा - shining, brilliant.

ताराकान्तितिरस्कारिनासाभरणभासुरा - She who shines with a nose ornament that surpasses the brilliance of the stars.

Meaning

(i) One whose nose ring challenges the lustre of the stars.

(ii) Tara can also be interpreted to mean the two Devees - Mangala and Sukla or the Devata - Taraka.

(iii) Sreedevee’s nose rings are made of Ruby and Pearl.

Esoteric note

* **The Luminous Point of Self:** Stars represent distant, objective, finite points of light in the external sky. Her nose-pearl, which rests closest to the breath of life (*Prāṇa*), represents the singular, immediate point of pure subjective light (*Bindu*). It outshines the stars because inner self-awareness far eclipses any external cosmic object.

कदम्बमञ्जर्या क्लृप्तः (कल्पितः) कर्णपूरः कदम्बमञ्जरीक्लृप्तः। तेन मनोहरा (रमणीया)।

कॢप्त / क्लृप्त - arranged, made, fashioned.

मनोहरा - captivating, charming, stealing the mind.

Meaning

(i) One who wears a bunch of Kadamba flowers in Her ears and steals the heart with Her beauty.

(ii) Wearing a bunch of flowers in the earlobes increases the beauty. Kadamba flower is suitable for such adornment.

(iii) A garden of Kadamba trees is situated outside the Chintamani Graha, the abode of Sreedevee, in Sreepura. Sreedevee wears the flowers plucked from those trees to adorn Her ear.

Esoteric note

The Kadamba tree represents the dense forest of manifest existence. The ears are the receptors of sound (*śabda*), the primary quality of space (*ākāśa*) and the source of speech.

* **The Ornaments of Śruti:** By wearing Kadamba blossoms as ear ornaments, She shows that all sound, all Vedic revelation (*Śruti*), and all manifest languages are merely beautiful ornaments hanging upon Her listening consciousness.

तथा तपनस्य (सूर्यस्य) उडपस्य (चन्द्रस्य) च मण्डले यस्याः सा।

Word by word

युगलीभूत - becoming a pair.

तपन - sun.

ताटङ्कयुगलीभूततपनोडुपमण्डला - She whose ear-ornaments are the paired discs of the Sun and Moon.

Meaning

(i) One who wears the Sun and Moon as two large earrings.

(ii) One type of ornament worn by ladies in their ears is called Tatanka (palm-leaf). The Sun and the Moon take the form of these Tatankas to beautify Sreedevee’s face.

(iii) The Sun and the Moon have the fortune to become Sreedevee’s eyes, earrings and Her breasts.

(iv) Tatanka is considered to be an auspicious ornament for Sumangalis (ladies living with their husbands). Sree Adi Sankara, in his Soundaryalaharee, describes with awe that Sree Parameshwara could survive, even after consuming the Halahala (poison), only by the power of Sreedevee’s Tatankas (28th verse of Soundaryalaharee).

Esoteric note

The *Tāṭaṅka* (ear-ring) is the symbol of eternal auspiciousness (*Saumaṅgalya*), as She never undergoes widowhood.

* **Wielding Time:** The Sun and Moon are the twin cosmic measurers of time. By wearing them as mere ear-rings, She wears Time itself as an accessory. This also represents that the solar and lunar breaths (**इडा** and **पिङ्गला**) are anchored in Her cosmic hearing.

Word by word

पद्मरागशिला - ruby/sapphire-like red precious stone.

आदर्श - mirror, glass.

परिभावि / परिभू - surpassing, excelling.

कपोलभूः - cheek surface.

पद्मरागशिलादर्शपरिभाविकपोलभूः - She whose cheeks surpass a mirror made of Padmaraga stone.

Meaning

(i) One whose cheeks are most wonderful than a glass made of Padmaraga (Sapphire).

(ii) Sreedevee’s cheeks are smooth and reflect like a mirror. Since it also seems to be red on account of Her complexion, the cheeks seem to be superior to a glass made of Sapphire.

Esoteric note

* **Cheeks of Reflection:** A mirror reflects whatever stands before it but has no color of its own. Her cheeks, however, are like ruby mirrors—they are red with Her own internal bliss (*Vimarśa*) and reflect the entire universe back to itself. Bhāskararāya implies that the entire cosmos is merely a reflection appearing upon the clean, luminous cheek-mirrors of the Mother's consciousness.

नवानां विद्रुमबिम्बानां श्रियं न्यक्कुरुतः (अधःकुरुतः) रदनच्छदौ यस्याः सा।

Word by word

नव - fresh, new.

विद्रुम - coral.

बिम्ब - bimba fruit.

श्री - beauty, lustre.

न्यक्कारि - putting down, surpassing, outshining.

नवविद्रुमबिम्बश्रीन्यक्कारिरदनच्छदा - She whose lips surpass the beauty of fresh coral and bimba fruit.

Meaning

(i) One whose (gorgeous) lips challenge the lustre of fresh Corals and the Bimba fruit (a fruit of a creeper, which when ripe is Red).

(ii) Sreedevee’s lips are Red in colour, by nature. Coral and the Bimba fruit are the two usually referred to for comparing lustrous Red objects. Sreedevee’s Rosy lips surpass these two objects.

(iii) Radanacchada is another version and the meaning is the same.

Esoteric note

* **The Portal of Grace:** Lips enclose speech. Their deep red color signifies Her overflowing compassion (*karuṇā*). Before Her speech transforms into spoken words, it sits behind the red barrier of Her lips as pure, unmanifest grace. The lips mock coral because coral is dead mineral material, whereas Her lips glow with the pulsing, vibrant life of supreme consciousness.

Nāma 25

शुद्धविद्याङ्कुराकारद्विजपङ्क्तिद्वयोज्ज्वला

Samāsa-vigraha

शुद्धविद्यायाः अङ्कुराणाम् इव आकारः यस्य द्विजपङ्क्तिद्वयस्य, तेन द्विजपङ्क्तिद्वयेन उज्ज्वला।

Word by word

शुद्धविद्या - Shuddha Vidya, superior Shodashakshari Mantra / Sree Vidya.

अङ्कुर - sprout, shoot.

आकार - form, shape.

द्विज - twice-born; also tooth.

पङ्क्तिद्वय - two rows.

उज्ज्वला - shining, resplendent.

शुद्धविद्याङ्कुराकारद्विजपङ्क्तिद्वयोज्ज्वला - She who shines with two rows of teeth resembling sprouts of Shuddha Vidya.

Meaning

(i) One whose rows of teeth shine like sprouts of Shuddha Vidya.

(ii) The word Dvija means twice born. This term is used to describe three different things: a. Brahmin - First birth from the mother and the second when the Upanayanam is performed (when the sacred thread is first worn). b. Birds - First birth as egg and the second when the chick comes out of the egg. c. Tooth - First as milk teeth and second when the tooth sprouts in place of fallen teeth.

(iii) Shuddha Vidya refers to the superior Shodasakshari Mantra. It consists of 16 letters or beejas. Beejas also mean seeds. The teeth look like the two sprouts from the seeds - the upper and lower rows.

(iv) Dattatreya Samhita and other texts state that Shuddha Vidya is the same as Sree Vidya. Hence the 16 letters of Shodasi Vidya are hidden in this name.

(v) Brahmins learn and propagate Vedas. Hence they are called Vidyankuras that is sprout of Vidya. Sreedevee’s two rows of teeth are compared to two rows of Brahmins, the sprout of Vidya.

(vi) In the Tantra text 32 types of initiations are mentioned - starting from Shuddha Vidya, Bala, Dwadasantha, Matangin and ending with Anutthara. These 32 types form the two rows of teeth of Sreedevee - another interpretation of this name.

(vii) It is indicated only the Dvijas (Brahmins) purified by these 32 initiations can reach Sreedevee’s feet.

(viii) Sreedevee’s Triakshari Mantra is also called as Shuddha Vidya. One becomes eligible for the 32 initiations (Deekshas) only after he is inducted into Triakshari. Shuddha Vidya is the base for the two rows of teeth which sprout from Shuddha Vidya.

(ix) In the Paribhasha Sloakas in the Nama Vibhaga part of this book, it is stated that the 1000 names begin only with 32 letters out of 51 letters in the Sanskrit alphabet, omitting 19 letters. It is also indicated that entire Sahasranama Stoora is structured on these 32 letters.

Esoteric note

* **The Smile of Realization:** *Śuddha-vidyā* is the state of cosmic realization where the thought "I am the universe" sparkles clearly. Her teeth are the white, sprouting shoots of this realization. When She smiles, She unleashes the light of pure knowledge that destroys the dark illusion of cosmic separation in the mind of the disciple.

Nāma 26

कर्पूरवीटिकामोदसमाकर्षिदिगन्तरा

Samāsa-vigraha

कर्पूरेण (करुपूरादिभिः) युक्ता वीटिका (ताम्बूलः)। तस्याः आमोदं याः समाकर्षन्ति। ताः एव दिशः अन्तं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

कर्पूर — camphor

वीटिका — betel packet; tamboola

आमोद — pleasant aroma

समाकर्षि — attracting; drawing towards

दिगन्तरा — the quarters and the intervening spaces

कर्पूरवीटिकामोदसमाकर्षिदिगन्तरा — She who attracts the quarters by the aroma of the camphor-scented betel from Her mouth

Meaning

i. One who attracts the four directions towards Her by the pleasant aroma of the betel (tamboola) emanating from Her lotus-like mouth, or one who spreads that aroma in all directions. Veetika is a small pack (folded inside a betel leaf) with proper mixture of aromatic spices such as camphor, cardamom, cloves, musk, saffron, nutmeg, betelnut, lime, etc. The aroma emanating from Sreedevee’s mouth when She chews the Veetika spreads in all directions. It is symbolically described as if the directions compete with each other in surrounding Sreedevee to have a scent of this aroma. Dik refers to the four directions and Digambara is the intervening space between the four directions such as Southeast, Southwest, etc.

ii. In the latter part of this Stotra, there is another name Tamboolapooritamukhi (559th name), which describes Sreedevee chewing betel leaves.

iii. The name Samakarshadigantara is also mentioned as Samakarshidigantara in some editions. There is no difference in meaning between these two versions.

iv. The 14th name in Sree Lalita Trishati, namely, Karpooraveetisaurabhya Kallolitakaguptata, also states the same idea. Sree Adi Sankara in his commentary has stated that the whole world is drenched with this aroma emanating from Sreedevee’s mouth and Sreedevee is thus Maharajabhogavathi (one who enjoys the comforts of an empress).

v. It is told that there were legendary poets, who were Upasakas of Sreedevee, viz. Kalidasa and Mooka Kavi, got their excellent capacity to write poems by consuming the juice of Sreedevee’s tamboola.

vi. It is implied that the Dikpalas — the regents of the eight cardinal points — encircle Sreedevee to offer their prayers.

Esoteric note

* **The Diffusion of Wisdom:** Camphor (*karpūra*) burns completely without leaving any residue, symbolizing the total dissolution of the ego. The betel roll (*vīṭikā*) contains spices that stimulate and sweeten. The fragrance of Her chewing this *vīṭikā* is the diffusion of spiritual wisdom (*Vidyā*) that spreads in all directions to attract and awaken dormant souls everywhere.

Nāma 27

निजसल्लापमाधुर्यविनिर्भर्त्सितकच्छपी

Samāsa-vigraha

नीजस्य (स्वीयस्य) सल्लापस्य माधुर्येण विनिर्भर्त्सिता कच्छपी यया सा।

Word by word

निज — own

सल्लाप — speech; conversation

माधुर्य — sweetness

विनिर्भर्त्सित — humbled; put to shame

कच्छपी — the Veena of Saraswathi

निजसल्लापमाधुर्यविनिर्भर्त्सितकच्छपी — She whose own sweet speech humbles the Kacchapi Veena

Meaning

i. One whose sweet voice humbles the Veena (a string instrument) called Kacchapi in the hands of Sree Saraswathi (goddess of learning).

ii. Kacchapi is the name of Sree Saraswathi’s Veena. Normally, in any string instrument like Veena, only the musical notes will be heard and not the lyrics of a song. But since Sree Saraswathi is the embodiment of sound and music, the musical notes as well as the words in the lyrics are heard from her Veena. However, the words would not be explicit, but resemble the utterances of parrot and infants. Sreedevee’s voice is so sweet, that it wins over the sweetness of Sree Saraswathi’s Veena.

iii. There is one verse in Soundaryalaharee (66th verse beginning with Vipanchya Gayanthi). It is stated that when Sree Saraswathi played her Veena in the presence of Sreedevee, She admired its sweetness and uttered the word “awesome”. On hearing this Sree Saraswathi was ashamed by the sweetness of Sreedevee’s voice which surpassed the sound of her Veena and kept it inside its cover.

Esoteric note

* **The Primal Sound (Nāda):** The lute *Kacchapī* produces the highest form of instrumental music. However, Her sweet conversation represents the primordial, unmanifest sound (**नाद** — *Nāda* or *Parā-vāk*) from which all music and languages emerge. The copy (instrumental music) is naturally shamed and humbled before the sweet, original source (Her voice).

Nāma 28

मन्दस्मितप्रभापूरमज्जत्कामेशमानसा

Samāsa-vigraha

मन्दस्य स्मितस्य (ईशद्धासस्य) प्रभापूरे मज्जतीति मन्दस्मितप्रभापूरमज्जत्। तदेव कामस्य ईशस्य मानसं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

मन्द — soft; gentle

स्मित — smile

प्रभापूर — flood of light

मज्जत् — sinking; immersed

कामेश — Sree Kameshwara

मानस — mind

मन्दस्मितप्रभापूरमज्जत्कामेशमानसा — She whose soft smile floods and immerses the mind of Kameshwara

Meaning

i. One who overwhelms Sree Kameshwara’s mind in the inundate of Her smile.

ii. Smita means smile — without the teeth being visible. Especially Mandasmita means a very soft smile.

iii. Majjat means sinking. Sree Kameshwara does not want to come out of the flood of light that is Sreedevee’s smile. At the same time He does not want to miss the opportunity of enjoying the beauty of the other parts; hence the use of the expression “sinking”.

iv. In Kamakala, Kama means bindu. Kala means Sun, Moon and fire. Bindu denotes ahankara. Kama and kala denote Kamakala. Kameshwara means both Rajarajeshwara and the embodiment of Kamakala.

v. When Sreedevee emerged out of the fire of knowledge (Chidagnikunda), before crowning Her as empress, the question arose as who can be made as Her consort. The only eligible candidate was Sree Kameshwara. But the Devas were perplexed as His physical appearance — with knotted locks, covered with an elephant skin or wearing nothing at all, with snakes as jewels and with ash smeared all over the body — was in no way a match to Her bewitching beauty. Immediately Sree Parameshwara took a beautiful form of Kameshwara. Sreedevee swung a garland declaring that he on whose neck the garland falls would be Her consort; it fell on Sree Kameshwara’s neck and brought forth a smile in Sreedevee’s lips. Sree Kameshwara was drowned in the beauty of Her smile. This is narrated in Sree Lalithopakhyana.

Esoteric note

* **The Dissolution of Transcendent Mind:** Kāmeśvara represents the supreme, unmoving, detached observer (*Prakāśa*). Even Her gentle, subtle smile (*mandasmita*) possesses such immense kinetic power (*Vimarśa*) that it completely dissolves and sweeps away Shiva's detached stillness, bringing Him into a state of ecstatic, non-dual union. It represents the perfect fusion of Shiva and Shakti.

Nāma 29

अनाकलितसादृश्यचिबुकश्रीविराजिता

Samāsa-vigraha

अनाकलितं (न कल्पितं) यत् सादृश्यं यस्याः चिबुकश्रियाः तादृश्या चिबुकश्रिया विराजिता।

Word by word

अनाकलित — not imagined; not conceived

सादृश्य — similarity; comparison

चिबुक — chin

श्री — beauty; splendour

विराजिता — shining

अनाकलितसादृश्यचिबुकश्रीविराजिता — She who shines by the incomparable beauty of Her chin

Meaning

i. One who shines by virtue of the incomparable beauty of Her chin.

ii. Even the Vagdevatas (the goddess of words) could not find similes to describe the beauty of Her chin.

iii. Sree Adi Sankara also opines the same, in his Soundaryalaharee, as Kathankaram Bhruma; tavasubukam oupamya rahitam (67th verse).

iv. Chubuka or Chibuka mean the same.

v. The 85th name Sreemadvagbhava Kootika Swrupa Mukha Pankaja, states the part of Sreedevee’s body above the neck denotes the first part of Sree Vidya Panchadasakshareemantra viz. Vagbhavakoota. The description of this part of the body starts from the 13th name, Champakashokapunnaga-sougandhikalasatkacha and ends here.

Esoteric note

* **The Incomparable Point of Non-Duality:** In aesthetic descriptions, every facial feature has a standard poetic parallel (e.g., eyes like lotus petals, forehead like the crescent moon). However, the chin has no poetic parallel in nature. Bhāskararāya points out that this chin represents the absolute, incomparable uniqueness of the *Nirguṇa* (unconditioned) state. Because She is the non-dual absolute, any comparison (*sādṛśya*) with worldly objects is fundamentally impossible (*anākalita*).

Nāma 30

कामेशबद्धमाङ्गल्यसूत्रशोभितकन्धरा

Samāsa-vigraha

कामेशेन (परमशिवेन) बद्धं यत् माङ्गल्यसूत्रं तेन शोभिता कन्धरा यस्याः सा।

Word by word

कामेश — Sree Kameshwara

बद्ध — tied

माङ्गल्यसूत्र — auspicious marriage string

शोभित — beautified

कन्धरा — neck

कामेशबद्धमाङ्गल्यसूत्रशोभितकन्धरा — She whose neck is beautified by the auspicious string tied by Kamesha

Meaning

i. One whose neck is so beautiful by the auspicious string tied by Sree Kameshwara at the time of wedding.

ii. Sreedevee is a Nitya Sumangali, who is always a Sumangali, wearing the mangala Sutra. Although She emerged out of Chidagni Kunda, already wearing the mangala Sutra, the Devas wanted to see the wedding ceremony of the Holy couple and made Him tie the string again on Sreedevee.

iii. Sree Parameshwara acquired the name Kamari after he reduced Cupid to ashes. Yet on seeing Sreedevee, it appears that He gave life to Cupid and subjected Himself as the aim for the arrows by Cupid so that love would arise in Him upon Sreedevee, that too through the grace of Sreedevee. (84th name — Haranetragni Sandagdha Kama sanjeevanoushadhi may be compared). Hence He becomes the lord of Cupid — Kameesan.

iv. Induced by His desire to marry Sreedevee, Eshwara made friendship with Cupid and was worshipped by him as “Thou art my Lord”.

v. This mangala Sutra tied by Kamesha showered blessings to the entire world. The first such beneficiary of this shower was Rathi-Manmatha (Cupid) couple and that too for the upliftment of the whole world.

Esoteric note

* **The Unbroken Thread of Cosmic Order:** The *māṅgalyasūtra* represents the eternal, indissoluble bond between *Prakāśa* (Shiva) and *Vimarśa* (Shakti). Because Shiva is immortal, Her state of auspiciousness is eternal (*Nitya-Sumaṅgalī*). Esoterically, the thread around Her neck represents the *Sūtrātman*—the singular, thread-like cosmic consciousness that runs through and holds together all individual souls (*jīvas*) in the universe.

भुजा — arms

अन्विता — endowed with

कनकाङ्गदकेयूरकमनीयभुजान्विता — She whose beautiful arms are adorned with golden armlets and Keyuras

Meaning

i. One whose shoulders are adorned by golden shoulder bangles.

ii. Angada and Keyura are the two ornaments worn on the hands. Keyura is for beautification whereas Angada acts as a shield for shoulders and arms of warriors. As Sreedevee is a queen, She wears both the ornaments.

Esoteric note

* **The Pillars of Action:** Her arms represent the active, protective powers of the cosmos. The armlets (*aṅgada* and *keyūra*) symbolize the cosmic laws (*Dharma*) that decorate and guide Her infinite power of action (**क्रियाशक्ति** — *Kriyā-śakti*). Gold (*kanaka*) represents the immutable, eternal truth of consciousness that remains unchanged regardless of the forms it takes.

Nāma 32

रत्नग्रैवेयचिन्ताकलोलमुक्ताफलान्विता

Samāsa-vigraha

रत्नखचितेन ग्रैवेयेण चिन्ताकेन च लोलैः मुक्ताफलैः च अन्विता।

Word by word

रत्न — gemstone

ग्रैवेय — neck pendant or necklace ornament

चिन्ताक — neck ornament/pendant

लोल — swinging

मुक्ताफल — pearls

अन्विता — endowed with; adorned

रत्नग्रैवेयचिन्ताकलोलमुक्ताफलान्विता — She who is adorned with a gem-studded neck ornament and swinging pearls

Meaning

i. One who wears a necklace with a pendant studded with gemstones and garland of Pearls.

ii. Griva means neck. Graiveya means the pendant in the necklace which adorns the neck and the string of Pearls aligning the necklace.

iii. The necklace, the pendant and the string of pearls represent the three types of devotees. Some will be chanting the names of Sreedevee (doing Japa), but their minds will be wandering somewhere else. Their thoughts of Sreedevee stop with the neck. They are Graiveya Chintakas, limiting their thought of Sreedevee above the neck. They hang and swing from the necklace of Sreedevee, hence they are called Loolas. For some others, the thoughts and actions will be oscillating between Sreedevee and other extraneous thoughts, like a pendant hanging from the necklace. The third type is the Muktas — the detached. They have got rid of their extraneous thoughts and action and think of Sreedevee only. Thus, this name classifies the devotees into three types.

iv. The fruits of actions of these three types of devotees are also different. For the Graiveya Chintaka and Loola the benefits are few — A-phala. For the Muktas A-phalam — full benefits. Two meanings are indicated for A-phala — few and full. For those who just utter the names (of Sreedevee) without concentration of mind, the benefits are few. For those whose minds oscillate between material things (Loolas) the benefits are still less. Those whose mind, word and action act in unison derive full benefits. All the three types of devotees are blessed with the gems like benefits they deserve.

Esoteric note

* **The Medallion of Pure Thought:** The neck-ornament (*graiveya*) rests over the throat, the center of speech (*Viśuddhi*). The pendant is called **चिन्ताक** (*cintāka*), derived from the root *cint* (to meditate or think). This represents that the focus of Her meditative thought is the welfare of Her devotees. The dangling pearls (*muktāphala*) represent the individual souls who have achieved liberation (*mukti*), clustered close to Her throat, bathing in the sound of Her grace.

Nāma 33

कामेश्वरप्रेमरत्नमणिप्रतिपणस्तनी

Samāsa-vigraha

कामेश्वरस्य प्रेम एव रत्नमणिः। रत्नमणौ प्रतिपणभूतौ स्तनौ यस्याः सा।

Word by word

कामेश्वर — Sree Kameshwara

प्रेम — love

रत्नमणि — gem; jewel

प्रतिपण — price; exchange

स्तनी — having breasts

कामेश्वरप्रेमरत्नमणिप्रतिपणस्तनी — She who offers Her breasts as the price for the gem of Kameshwara’s love

Meaning

i. One who offers Her breasts as price (or in exchange) for the gem of love of Sree Kameshwara.

ii. Sreedevee has purchased Sree Kameshwara’s invaluable love for Her, with her breasts.

iii. Sreedevee has offered twice the price or price like (two jewels of breasts) for a single jewel of Sree Kameshwara’s love. (Refer 4th verse of Soundaryalaharee — Phalamapicha Vanchasamadhikam).

Esoteric note

* **The Great Cosmic Transaction:** Bhāskararāya interprets this highly esoteric play. The "wager" (*pratipaṇa*) refers to a cosmic game of dice played between Shiva and Shakti. Her breasts represent the dual polarities of creation—**प्रकाश** (*Prakāśa*) and **विमर्श** (*Vimarśa*). To obtain Her supreme, dual-natured manifestation, Shiva wagers His entire undivided, silent love. This represents the absolute, reciprocal self-surrender between the divine couple.

Nāma 34

नाभ्यालवालरोमालिलताफलकुचद्वयी

Samāsa-vigraha

नाभिः एव आलवालः यस्याः रोमालवल्याः लतायाः तस्याः फलभूता कुचद्वयी यस्याः सा।

Word by word

नाभि — navel

आलवाल — trench; basin at the root

रोमाली — line of hair

लता — creeper

फल — fruit

कुचद्वयी — two breasts

नाभ्यालवालरोमालिलताफलकुचद्वयी — She whose two breasts are fruits of the creeper-like hair-line rising from the navel-trench

Meaning

i. Sreedevee’s two breasts are like fruits in a creeper (line of hair) climbing from the trench (the naval).

ii. The deep naval is like a trench. The narrow line of hair grown upwards from the naval is like a creeper. The two breasts appear as if they are hanging from the creeper (an excellent metaphor).

iii. 78th verse of Soundaryalaharee may be referred; Stanamukula Romavali lata.

Esoteric note

* **The Root of Vital Force:** The navel (*nābhi*) represents the **मणिपूर चक्र** (*Maṇipūra Cakra*), the seat of fire and metabolic origin. The upward-climbing hairline (*romāli*) represents the movement of the ascending lifeforce (*Prāṇa*) traveling up the central channel. The twin breasts produced as "fruits" represent the nourishing wisdom and bliss (*Sarasvatī* and *Lakṣmī* potencies) that blossom when the energy rises to the heart center (*Anāhata*).

Nāma 35

लक्ष्यरोमलताधारतासमुन्नेयमध्यमा

Samāsa-vigraha

लक्ष्यितुं योग्या या रोमलताधारता तया सम्यगुन्नेयं मध्यमं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

लक्ष्य — to be inferred; to be noticed

रोमलता — creeper-like line of hair

आधारता — state of being the support/base

समुन्नेय — to be presumed; inferred

मध्यमा — waist; middle

लक्ष्यरोमलताधारतासमुन्नेयमध्यमा — She whose waist is inferred as the base of the creeper-like hair-line

Meaning

i. One for whom, the existence of a waist base for the climbing creeper of line of hair is to be presumed.

ii. The creeper of hair line mentioned in the previous name is visible. But the base where the root of the creeper is located is not to be seen. The existence of a limb as waist is to be presumed.

iii. As per Samudrika Sastra, the waist of upper classes of women will be so small as to be presumed as non-existent.

Esoteric note

* **The Inferred Reality of Brahman:** In Sanskrit poetics, an incredibly slender waist represents beauty. Esoterically, Bhāskararāya aligns this with the philosophical concept of **अनुमान** (*Anumāna* — logical inference). The waist (representing the supreme, unmanifest *Brahman*) cannot be seen directly by the physical senses. However, its existence is masterfully inferred by looking at the manifest world of name and form (the hairline).

Nāma 36

स्तनभारदलन्मध्यपट्टबन्धवलित्रया

Samāsa-vigraha

स्तनयोः भारेण दलत इव मध्यस्य पट्टबन्धः एव वलित्रयं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

स्तनभार — weight of the breasts

दलत् — breaking; cracking as if

मध्य — middle; waist

पट्टबन्ध — bandage; belt-like binding

वलित्रय — three folds

स्तनभारदलन्मध्यपट्टबन्धवलित्रया — She whose three abdominal folds appear as bandages around a waist breaking under the weight of Her breasts

Meaning

i. One whose three folds in the abdominal area appear to be three bandages worn on the waist to prevent it from breaking due to the weight of the breasts.

ii. Samudrika Sastra specifies that higher class men and women will have three lines (folds) on their forehead, neck and abdomen. They are signs of extremely good fortune.

iii. Refer 80th verse of Soundaryalaharee — Thridhanaddham Deveetrivalee lavaleevaleebhiriva.

Esoteric note

* **The Three Folds of Space-Time:** The three folds (*vali-traya*) represent the three cosmic boundaries: the three *Guṇas* (Sattva, Rajas, Tamas), the three worlds, and the three divisions of time (past, present, future). These boundaries act as the "protective binding strap" (*paṭṭabandha*) that stabilizes and holds the weight of manifest creation, preventing the absolute unmanifest consciousness from collapsing.

Nāma 37

अरुणारुणकौसुम्भवस्त्रभास्वत्कटीतटी

Samāsa-vigraha

अरुणारुणेन (अतिशयेन अरुणेन अरुणवद् अरुणं वा) कौसुम्भं यद् वस्त्रं तेन भास्वती कट्याः तटी यस्याः सा।

Word by word

अरुणारुण — deep red; crimson

कौसुम्भ — red silk dyed with Kusumbha

वस्त्र — cloth

भास्वत् — shining

कटीतटी — slope/region of the waist

अरुणारुणकौसुम्भवस्त्रभास्वत्कटीतटी — She whose waist shines with crimson-red silk cloth

Meaning

i. One whose waist shines with the crimson silk worn on it.

ii. The dual expression Aruna-Aruna means dark red or Crimson.

iii. The Red here is like that of Aruna, the charioteer of the Sun God, who rises before Sun rises.

iv. Kausumbha Vastra means Red silk cloth. The juice of Kausumbha herb is used to dye cloths in Red; hence Kausumbha Vastra.

v. Sreedevee has worn Kausumbha Vastra on Her waist.

vi. It appears as though Aruna Vagdevata’s name is indirectly stated here.

Esoteric note

* **The Garment of Pure Desire:** Safflower (*kusumbha*) yields a vibrant, glowing red dye. The hip region corresponds to the **स्वाधिष्ठान** (*Svādhiṣṭhāna*) and **मूलाधार** (*Mūlādhāra*) cakras, which govern primal energy and stability. Her intensely red garment represents the covering of **इच्छाशक्ति** (*Icchā-śakti* — pure will and creative desire) that wraps around the root of cosmic manifestation.

Nāma 38
