रत्नैः (रत्नमयीभिः) किङ्किणिकाभिः रम्येण रशनया एव दाम्या भूषिता।

Word by word

रत्न — gem

किङ्किणिका — small tinkling bell

रम्य — beautiful

रशना — girdle; waist-string

दाम — garland/string

भूषिता — adorned

रत्नकिङ्किणिकारम्यरशनादामभूषिता — She adorned with a beautiful girdle-string lined with gem-bells

Meaning

i. One who wears a girdle string (Meekala Sutra) lined with tinkling gems.

ii. The golden girdle string is lined with small tinkle bells. The small gems inside the bells make a soft pleasant sound.

iii. The part of Sreedevee’s body below the neck and above the thigh represents the central portion of Pancha Dasaksharee Mantra consisting of six letters. These are indirectly stated from 30th till 38th names.

Esoteric note

* **The Rhythms of the Cosmos:** The belt is tied around the waist, stabilizing the center of gravity. The jingling of the tiny bells (*kiṅkiṇikā*) represents the subtle, rhythmic vibrations of the unmanifest sound (*Aṇu-nāda* or *Nāda-bindu*) that continuously hums at the base of creation, driving the cycles of nature.

Nāma 39

कामेशज्ञातसौभाग्यमार्दवोरुद्वयान्विता

Samāsa-vigraha

कामेशेन एव ज्ञाते सौभाग्यमार्दवे ययोः ऊर्वोः तयोः द्वयेन अन्विता।

Word by word

कामेश — Sree Kameshwara

ज्ञात — known

सौभाग्य — exquisiteness; beauty

मार्दव — softness

ऊरुद्वय — two thighs

अन्विता — endowed with

कामेशज्ञातसौभाग्यमार्दवोरुद्वयान्विता — She endowed with two thighs whose beauty and softness are known only to Kameshwara

Meaning

i. One who has two beautiful and soft thighs known only to Sree Kameshwara.

ii. The softness and the smoothness of Her thighs are known only to Sree Kameshwara.

iii. Soubhagya here means exquisiteness or beauty.

Esoteric note

* **The Unknowable Essence of Bliss:** The thighs are kept covered, symbolizing that which is secret and deeply private. Bhāskararāya explains that Her deepest bliss (*saubhāgya*) and tenderness (*mārdava*) are completely inaccessible to the external, dualistic mind. Only when the individual consciousness completely dissolves into Kāmeśvara (pure, non-dual subjective awareness) can this supreme, intimate state of divine bliss be realized.

Nāma 40

माणिक्यमकुटाकारजानुद्वयविराजिता

Samāsa-vigraha

माणिक्येन निर्मितस्य मकुटस्य इव आकारः ययोः जानुद्वययोः तयोः विराजिता।

Word by word

माणिक्य — ruby

मकुट — crown; hard cap

आकार — form; shape

जानुद्वय — two knees

विराजिता — shining

माणिक्यमकुटाकारजानुद्वयविराजिता — She whose two knees resemble ruby crowns

Meaning

i. One whose knees resemble hard, Red caps made of rubies.

ii. The knees are so Red and seem to be like a hard cap.

iii. The softness of the thighs mentioned in the previous name is contrasted with the hardness of the knees.

iv. The reason for hardness of Sreedevee’s knees is stated in the 82nd verse of Soundaryalaharee.

v. Mukuta and Makuta — both have the same meaning.

Esoteric note

* **The Kneeling of Cosmic Powers:** The knees provide the structural pivot for bowing and kneeling. By comparing Her knees to ruby crowns (*makuṭa*), Bhāskararāya hints at a profound cosmic inversion: the highest crowns of all the cosmic deities (Indra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu) bow down and rest in absolute surrender at Her feet, reflecting their crowns upon Her knees.

Nāma 41

इंद्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तस्मरतूणाभजंघिका

Samāsa-vigraha

इंद्रगोपैः परितः क्षिप्तौ यौ स्मरस्य तूणौ तयोः तुल्ये जङ्घिके यस्याः सा।

Word by word

इन्द्रगोप — firefly/red insect

परिक्षिप्त — surrounded

स्मर — Cupid

तूण — quiver

जंघिका — shanks

इंद्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तस्मरतूणाभजंघिका — She whose shanks resemble Cupid’s quiver surrounded by fireflies

Meaning

i. One whose shanks resemble Cupid’s quiver surrounded by fireflies.

ii. A quiver is a case for carrying arrows, carried by the warriors, with a broad mouth and tapered at the bottom.

iii. The two shanks of Sreedevee are firm and reddish. This resembles Cupid’s quiver surrounded by insects sparkling at night. The brightness of the ankles is enhanced by the sparkling insects. The reddish legs are glowing naturally, but as a metaphor this is compared to the fireflies shining in the night.

iv. Sree Adi Sankara says in 83rd verse of Soundaryalaharee, that Cupid, who was burnt down by Lord Shiva was waiting for an opportunity to seek revenge on Him, and when He was attracted by Sreedevee’s beauty, Cupid made Sreedevee’s shanks his quiver and Her toes his arrows; Parajethum RudhramadhvigunaCharagarbhau Girisute Nishangou Janghete Vishama Vichikho Badhamakrta.

Esoteric note

* **The Quivers of Creative Force:** The quivers of Cupid hold the arrows of desire. The *Indragopa* insect is famous in Sanskrit literature for its deep, velvety crimson color. This indicates that Her lower limbs hold the concentrated, velvet-red potential of all creative forces, ready to be deployed to guide and capture the minds of seekers, turning them away from worldly pursuits.

Nāma 42

गूढगुल्फा

Samāsa-vigraha

गूढौ गुल्फौ यस्याः सा।

Word by word

गूढ — hidden; covered

गुल्फ — ankle

गूढगुल्फा — She whose ankles are covered/hidden by firm muscles

Meaning

i. One whose shanks are covered by firm muscles.

ii. Gulpha refers to the calf muscles above the ankles; it means firm and beautiful ankles.

Esoteric note

* **The Veiled Path of Yoga:** *Gūḍha* means hidden or secret. In *Aṣṭāṅga-yoga*, the ankles represent the physical structural transition to the feet (contact with the earth). Her hidden ankles represent that the path of transitioning from material existence (*Samsāra*) to spiritual elevation is deeply hidden and must be approached through secret, internal contemplation rather than ostentatious external display.

Nāma 43

कूर्मपृष्ठजयिष्णुप्रपदान्विता

Samāsa-vigraha

कूर्मयोः पृष्ठे जयिष्णुनी (जयतः इति) ये प्रपदे (पादाग्रे) ताभ्याम् अन्विता।

Word by word

कूर्म — turtle

पृष्ठ — back

जयिष्णु — excelling; surpassing

प्रपद — forepart of foot; foot front

अन्विता — endowed with

कूर्मपृष्ठजयिष्णुप्रपदान्विता — She whose feet surpass the back of a turtle

Meaning

i. One whose foot resembles a turtle’s back.

ii. The back of the feet of higher class women would be pyramid like. In the absence of any other suitable comparison, turtle’s back (though of an inferior class) is used as a simile.

iii. The 88th verse of Soundaryalaharee also explicitly states that this simile is not the most appropriate one; Padam Tekeertteenam Prapadam Apadam Devee Vipadam Ktham Neetam Sadbhih Katina Kamateekarprara Tulam.

Esoteric note

* **The Base of Cosmic Stability:** The tortoise (*Kūrma*) is the classic symbol of ultimate stability and withdrawal of the senses. By having feet that conquer the tortoise shell, She is identified as the supreme foundation of the entire universe, holding the pristine, unshakeable stability (**कूर्म-नाडी** — the channel of complete physical and mental stillness).

Nāma 44

नखदीधितिसंछन्ननमज्जनतमोगुणा

Samāsa-vigraha

नखानां दीधितिभिः (किरणैः) सम्यक् छन्नो नमतां जनानां तमोगुणः यस्याः सा।

Word by word

नख — nail

दीधिति — ray; lustre

संछन्न — covered; enveloped

नमज्जन — people who bow/prostrate

तमोगुण — darkness; ignorance

नखदीधितिसंछन्ननमज्जनतमोगुणा — She whose toenail rays cover and remove the darkness of those who bow to Her

Meaning

i. One who removes the darkness of ignorance of those who prostrate (Tamo Guna) before Her by the lustre of Her toe nails.

ii. When Brahma, Vishnu and other Devas prostrate before Sreedevee’s feet, the lustre of their crown face the lustre of Sreedevee’s toe nails, and unable to stand, their brightness go back inside them and remove the darkness of ignorance.

iii. Or, just by contact, the lustre of the toe nails removes the darkness of ignorance.

iv. Not only for the Devas, but also for all those who worship Sreedevee, the same benefit i.e. the removal of ignorance — is obtained.

Esoteric note

* **The Dawn of Inner Light:** *Tamas* is the dark quality of inertia, sleep, and spiritual blindness. When a devotee bows their head to Her feet, their crown (*Sahasrāra*) comes into contact with the light rays emanating from Her toe-nails. These ten toe-nails act like ten miniature suns, instantly dissolving the deep-seated darkness of spiritual ignorance (*Avidyā*) and replacing it with the light of self-realization.

Nāma 45

पदद्वयप्रभाजालपराकृतसरोरुहा

Samāsa-vigraha

पदद्वयस्य प्रभाजालेन पराकृते सरोरुहे यस्याः सा।

Word by word

पदद्वय — two feet

प्रभाजाल — net/mass of lustre

पराकृत — surpassed; defeated

सरोरुह — lotus

पदद्वयप्रभाजालपराकृतसरोरुहा — She whose two feet surpass the lotus by their lustre

Meaning

i. One who won over the lotus flower by the lustre of Her two feet.

ii. Generally, it is a literary tradition to take the lotus flower for comparison with the face, feet and eyes of beautiful men and women. Lustre, softness, beautiful structure and a lovely appearance are the special features of a lotus. In the case of Sreedevee’s feet, there is one more special characteristic. Lotus will blossom and shrivel on the same day, whereas Sreedevee’s feet remain permanently lustrous, and thus they win over lotus.

Esoteric note

* **The Transcendent Lotus:** The red lotus (*saroruha*) is the standard symbol of beauty and purity in the material world. However, the lotus grows out of mud and water. Her feet, being pure consciousness, excel the lotus because they are entirely self-luminous (*Svaprakāśa*) and free from any worldly origin. They represent the ultimate sanctuary of absolute purity.

Nāma 46

शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीरमण्डितश्रीपदाम्बुजा

Samāsa-vigraha

सिञ्जानाः मणयः ययोः मञ्जीरयोः ताभ्यां मण्डिता श्रीः ययोः पदाम्बुजयोः तादृशे पदाम्बुजे यस्याः सा।

Word by word

शिञ्जान — tinkling

मणि — gem

मञ्जीर — anklet

मण्डित — decorated

श्री — auspicious beauty

पदाम्बुज — lotus feet

शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीरमण्डितश्रीपदाम्बुजा — She whose lotus feet are decorated with tinkling gem anklets

Meaning

i. One whose Lotus feet are decorated with anklets with tinkling bells.

ii. The anklets worn on Sreedevee’s feet have bells fixed with gems. They make a sweet and soft jingle while oscillating. They add Sreeta Her lotus feet. (Sree is one word which cannot be translated into any other language, to bring forth its entire meaning). Broadly it means “all that is good”.

iii. Chinjana is another expression in some texts. The meaning is the same.

Esoteric note

* **The Melodies of Creation:** The sweet tinkling (*siñjāna*) of Her anklets represents the primordial cosmic sound (**नाद** — *Nāda*). As She walks (manifests and directs cosmic processes), the movement of Her feet unleashes the primary vibrations that organize chaos into ordered space and time. It is the music of the spheres playing at Her feet.

Nāma 47

मरालीमन्दगमना

Samāsa-vigraha

मराली इव मन्दगमनं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

मराली — female swan

मन्द — slow; gentle

गमन — gait; movement

मरालीमन्दगमना — She whose gentle gait is like that of a female swan

Meaning

i. One whose gait is slow and beautiful like a female swan.

ii. The gait of a swan is always soft and beautiful. The gait of a female swan is all the more graceful. Hence the female swan is compared.

iii. Everyone stands spellbound by the beauty of Sreedevee coming out of the sacrificial fire.

iv. The same idea is expressed in Soundaryalaharee and Mooka Panchasati. The swans in Sreedevee’s palace try to learn and copy the gait of Sreedevee. The soft sound of Sreedevee’s anklets seem to teach lessons to the swans. Refer: Padanyasa Krida Parichaya Mivarabhdhu Manasa: Skhalantaste Khelam Bhavanakalohamsa Na Jahati Athastheesham Shikshaam Subhagamanji Manjira Ranjita-Chaladachakshanam Charanakamalam Charucharitare (91st verse of Soundaryalaharee). Maralinam Yamabhyasanakalana Moolagurave (Mookapanchasati — Padaravinda Satakam - 3).

v. That part of Sreedevee’s body below the waist represents the Shaktikuta of Sreedevee’s Mantra consisting of four syllables.

Esoteric note

* **The Gait of Ultimate Discrimination:** The swan (*marālī* or *haṃsa*) is the ultimate symbol of spiritual discrimination (*Viveka*), possessing the legendary ability to separate milk from water. Her slow, majestic gait (*manda-gamana*) represents the steady, deliberate process of divine discrimination that separates the eternal reality (*Nitya*) from the transient illusion (*Anitya*) in the cosmos.

Esoteric note

The Axis of the Subtle Body: Mount Sumeru is the cosmic golden mountain at the center of the universe. The "middle peak" (madhya-śṛṅga) is the topmost point of this axis—the Sahasrāra at the crown of the head. Therefore, She is Sumerumadhyaśṛṅgasthā because Her ultimate, supreme station of rest is the crown center of non-dual union.

The Resurrection of Divine Desire: When Shiva's eye of pure transcendence burned Cupid (worldly desire), the universe was threatened with absolute, cold stasis. Esoteric note

She is the giver of this fortune because She transforms the dry life of a seeker into a rich, nectarine experience of self-realization, which is the ultimate prosperity.

Esoteric note

The Destruction of Dualistic Fear: As the Upaniṣads explicitly declare: "Verily, fear arises only when there is a second entity" (Dvitīyād vai bhayaṃ bhavati). Fear is a natural consequence of duality—the fear of loss, death, or judgment by another. She is Bhayāpahā because She dissolves the very illusion of a "second entity." By revealing that the entire universe is Her own self-projection, She establishes the practitioner in the fearless, non-dual state of absolute safety.

The Mudrā of Silent Awareness: Beyond being the consort of Śiva[cite: 1], Śāmbhavī denotes the highest state of internal yoga—the शाम्भवी मुद्रा (Śāmbhavī Mudrā). In this state, the eyes are physically open, gazing outward, but the entire attention is fixed permanently inward on the non-dual Self, completely unmoved by external modifications. She embodies this mudrā, representing the peak of quiet, stable baseline awareness.

Eight elements of time as per Sreedevee's measurements are as follows; 1, TatvaYuga 2. TatvaVarsho (year - total 36 years) 3. Kala Masa (months - total 16 months) 4. Tatva Dina (day - total 36 days) 5. Dina Nitya (total 15) 6. Thithi Nitya (total 15) 7. Vésara (total 9) 8. Udhaya Ghatika (total six) In Samskrit the numbers are represented by letters through Kotapayadhi method. In this, if the first letters of the day and the Udhaya Katiké are the same, it is called a Parva dayor Sreekaree. In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya explains सुप्ता through both micro-cosmic yoga and macro-cosmic states of consciousness:

The Dormant Power: In the subtle body of living beings, She resides as कुण्डलिनी in the मूलाधार chakra, remaining in a dormant or sleeping state until awakened by spiritual practice.

Cosmic Dissolution: On a cosmic level, सुप्ता refers to the state of प्रलय (cosmic dissolution), where the entire universe rests asleep within Her, waiting for the next cycle of creation.

Supreme Knowledge: The name also breaks down as प्रकृष्टः ज्ञः (prakṛṣṭhaḥ jñaḥ — the highest knower). She is the absolute, omniscient intelligence that remains awake as the ultimate witness even when the individual mind completely shuts down in deep sleep.

She is not a separate state, but the very substratum of pure, non-dual awareness (cit) upon which the other three states appear and disappear.

The Witness Identity: While the first three states are bound by time, space, and causality, the Fourth is unconditioned, self-luminous, and eternal. By realizing Her as Turyā, the practitioner breaks free from cosmic delusion (māyā) and recognizes their own identity as pure Brahman.

Absolute Immutability: States belong to the changing world of matter (prakṛti) and the finite mind. As the immutable, supreme reality (nirguṇa-brahman), She undergoes no transitions. The Imparting of Agency: She is the fundamental kinetic power (Śakti) that activates Brahmā. Without Her presence, the masculine creative principle remains inert and incapable of projecting the universe.

Identity with Brahmā: Bhāskararāya notes that She herself assumes the form of Brahmā (Brahmarūpā) during the cosmic dawn to manifest the name-and-form universe out of Her own being.

The Resolution of Duality: On an internal level, She is the power that dissolves the practitioner's sense of duality, drawing the outward-bound mind back into the heart center.

i. One who is a sister of Vishnu, Padmanabha.

ii. Vishnu created the lotus from his navel and hence is Padmanabha. As per Markandeya Purana, Sreedevee created three pairs of twins as per Her desire: Brahma and Lakshmi in gold colour, Vishnu and Sreedevee in blue colour, and Shiva and Sarasvati in white colour. Their colours indicate the three gunas. As per this mythology, Vishnu and Sreedevee are siblings.

iii. Similarly Brahma Purana says that Parvati, born from the womb of Menaka in a former birth, in the next birth is born as Subhadra, sister of Sreekrishna in the womb of Devaki.

iv. Again we read: Katyayaniti Ya Jata Kamsa Shatroh Sahodari.

v. In another place, Sreedevee along with Her brother Sree Vishnu appeared to Brahma at Kanchi. Sree Bhaskararaya explains in many places that each letter of this Sahasranama is a root letter of a mantra; according to this special interpretation, the three names Padma, Nabha and Sahodari indicate the sacred syllables hidden in this name.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya explores this relationship to illustrate cosmic non-duality and shared function:

The Shared Womb of Nature: Mythologically, She is Narāyaṇī, the sister of Kṛṣṇa/Viṣṇu. Esoterically, Bhāskararāya points out that they emerge from the exact same supreme matrix of unmanifested causal nature (mūlaprakṛti).

Equivalence of Form and Power: Viṣṇu represents the pervasive, protective consciousness, while She is the active energy (śakti) that makes that protection effective. They share identical sattva-guṇa properties during the sustenance phase of the universe, demonstrating that the supreme dynamic power and the supreme pervasive consciousness are fundamentally one.

The Scale of Time: While these terms imply a split-second blinking to mortals, on a cosmic scale, a single blink spans the entire lifespan of multiple Brahmās and cosmic systems, showing Her complete transcendence over time.

Bhāskararāya explains that while She assumes all names and forms for the sake of the devotee's worship, Her true, essential nature (Svarūpa) is the attribute-less, unconditioned Brahman (Nirguṇa), completely untouched by any mental definitions or physical shapes.

Meaning

i. One who is in the form of Hrim bija letters.

ii. Hri means modesty, shyness and bashfulness. One who does this is Hrimkari. In Saptashati it is mentioned that we bow to Sreedevee, who is in the form of bashfulness in all souls.

iii. In Swatantra Tantra it is mentioned that since Sreedevee takes care of creation, protection and destruction tasks, She is called Hrimkari.

iv. Hrim itself is one of the names of Sreedevee, the 99th name in Lalita Trishati also. Sree Adi Sankara mentions that all energies are attributes of Sreedevee; by disconnecting them, we get Her liberated form.

v. This is the maya-bija, also called Bhuvaneshvari bija.

vi. This bija is in the Panchadashi mantra at the end of every division. The letters Ka and Ha correspond to Shiva, and the letters A, E, La and Sa correspond to Shakti.

vii. Om in general is called Pranavam. This is also called Shakta Pranavam.

viii. Lalita Trishati has three hundred names, twenty for each letter of the Panchadashi mantra; sixty names correspond to Hrim. The detailed meanings can be seen in the commentary of Sree Adi Sankara.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya unpacks the immense ontological weight of this bīja within Śrīvidyā theology:

The Cosmic Sound Form: ह्रीं is the supreme Lajjā-bīja (syllable of cosmic modesty/containment). Bhāskararāya details that She is both the source and the ultimate reality indicated by this syllable. It represents the unmanifested consciousness containing the seeds of the entire universe, ready to project outward.

The Power of Manifestation: As Hrīṁkārī, She animates the primal vibration that marks the boundary line between the absolute unmanifested Brahman (Nirguṇa) and the manifested, qualified universe (Saguṇa).

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya unpacks the esoteric direction built into this name:

The Guide to Liberation: Beyond Her beautiful eyes, the root nī means to lead. She is Vāmanayanā because She actively leads (nayati) the practitioner toward the highest spiritual beautification (vāma), which is the state of final liberation.

Nāma 333

वारुणीमदविह्वला

Samāsa-vigraha

वारुण्याः मदेन विह्वला।

वरुणस्य इयं वारुणीमान् तस्य इव अविह्वला।

Word by word

वारुण्याः — of Varuni liquor; of Varuna-related power

मदेन — by intoxication; by bliss

विह्वला — overwhelmed; perturbed

अविह्वला — not fatigued or exhausted

Meaning

i. One who is perturbed by the intoxicating liquor, the wine of spiritual bliss.

ii. Varuni is a kind of liquor obtained from the date fruit and is so called because the god Varuna is fond of it. The expression indicates forgetting external objects and simply enjoying; the name Svatmarama may be compared.

iii. According to Taittiriya Upanishad, the Brahma Vidya taught by Varuna to Bhrigu is called Varuni.

iv. The name may also be split as Varunimat and Avihvala: by her grace Adishesha, connected with the region of Varuna, is not fatigued in supporting the universe.

v. Varuni is also a nadi connected with Vayu in the body. One who has conquered it through yoga is called Varuniman. Sreedevee removes weariness and exhaustion from devotees.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya elevates the concept of Vāruṇī:

The Solar Nectar: वारुणी refers to the purifying internal solar energy that flows through the Suṣumṇā channel during high-level yoga. The "intoxication" (mada) is the state of spiritual ecstasy where the outer world is forgotten, and the mind dissolves into pure light, a state that She governs and embodies.

Nāma 334

विश्वाधिका

Samāsa-vigraha

विश्वाधिका। विश्वस्मात् अधिका।

Word by word

विश्वस्मात् — than the universe

अधिका — greater; beyond

विश्वाधिका — she who transcends the universe

Meaning

i. One who transcends the whole world.

ii. She is beyond the thirty-six tattvas from earth up to Shiva. The Veda speaks of the Rudra who is beyond the universe. Since she is the united form of Shiva and Shakti and is in the form of Sadakhya-tattva, she is Vishvadhika.

iii. Sreedevee is beyond waking, dream, and deep sleep states, and even beyond the turiya state. Names from Vishvarupa to Sarvavastha-vivarjita may be referred to.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya clarifies Her concurrent immanence and transcendence:

Surpassing the Manifested: Though the universe is Her own physical projection, She is not limited by it. She is Viśvādhikā because Her essential nature remains completely untouched by cosmic mutations, existing infinitely beyond the boundaries of cosmic space and matter.

Nāma 335

वेदवेद्या

Samāsa-vigraha

वेदैः वेद्या।

Word by word

वेदैः — by the Vedas

वेद्या — to be known; knowable

वेदवेद्या — she who is known through the Vedas

Meaning

i. One who can be known through the Vedas.

ii. She can be realised through the Rig, Yajur, Sama, and Atharva Vedas. In the Bhagavad Gita, Lord Krishna says: by all the Vedas I alone am to be known.

iii. In Sree Nagara, the dwelling place of Sreedevee, the four Vedas are the four entrances. Only by passing through these entrances can one reach Sreedevee.

iv. In the centre of the Sree Chakra, in the Bindu, the Amnaya deities are worshipped. They are goddesses connected with the four Vedas, and since she is recognised by these Vidyas, Sreedevee is Vedavedya.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya connects this directly to the Brahma Sūtra ("शास्त्रयोनित्वात्"):

The Ultimate Subject of Revelation: The four Vedas, along with all their secret Upaniṣads, have only one ultimate subject matter. Though they describe various rituals and lesser deities, their final corporate intent is to reveal Her—the supreme, non-dual consciousness.

Nāma 336

विन्ध्याचलनिवासिनी

Samāsa-vigraha

विन्ध्याख्ये अचले निवासतीति।

Word by word

विन्ध्याख्ये — called Vindhya

अचले — mountain

निवसति — dwells

विन्ध्याचलनिवासिनी — she who dwells in the Vindhya mountain

Meaning

i. One who resides in the Vindhya mountains.

ii. In Saptashati and Pancharatra Lakshmi Tantra it is said that Sreedevee incarnated during Vaivasvata Manvantara in the house of Nandagopa, from the womb of Yashoda, to destroy the demons Shumbha and Nishumbha, and then dwelt in the Vindhya mountains.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya interprets this location across geographical and internal landscapes:

The Historical Abode: Mythologically, She resides in the thick forests of the Vindhya mountain range as the fierce, protective deity.

The Unshakable Base: Esoterically, Acala means that which does not move. The Vindhya range represents the firm, unmoving, grounded station of the Mūladhāra chakra at the base of the spine, where She sits anchored before Her ascent.

Nāma 337

विधात्री

Samāsa-vigraha

विदधातीति।

विधातुः पत्नी वा।

Word by word

विदधाति — supports; arranges; ordains

विधातुः — of Vidhata, Brahma

पत्नी — wife; consort

विधात्री — supporter; ordainer; consort of Brahma

Meaning

i. One who supports this universe.

ii. Since she supports and nourishes the universe, she is Vidhatri. The later name Jagaddhatri conveys the same sense.

iii. Vidhata means Brahma; his consort is Vidhatri.

iv. The word may also be connected with dhatri, myrobalan, because she is fond of myrobalans.

v. Dhatri also means mother, who bears the child in her womb and releases it at the proper time. A great mother is Vidhatri; names such as Sreemata, Mata, Janani, Prasavitri, and Amba may be referred to.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya focuses on Her absolute structural governance:

The Ordainer of Fate: She is the supreme manager who designs, coordinates, and dispenses the individual lines of destiny (karma) for every single living being in the cosmos, performing this function with absolute justice.

Nāma 338

वेदजननी

Samāsa-vigraha

वेदानां जननी।

Word by word

वेदानाम् — of the Vedas

जननी — mother; source

वेदजननी — mother of the Vedas

Meaning

i. One who is the mother of the Vedas.

ii. Since the Vedas themselves arise from her and reveal her, she is the mother of the Vedas. As the source of sacred knowledge and as the one who is known through the Vedas, she is called Vedajanani.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya traces the origin of revelation back to Her breath:

The Source of Revelation: The Vedas are eternal (Apauruṣeya), meaning they are not authored by human minds. Bhāskararāya notes that they emanate effortlessly as Her natural breath at the beginning of each cosmic dawn, proving that She is the parent matrix of all sacred text and sound.

Nāma 339

विष्णुमाया

Samāsa-vigraha

विष्णोः माया।

Word by word

विष्णोः — of Vishnu

माया — power of manifestation; divine power

विष्णुमाया — the Maya of Vishnu

Meaning

i. One who is the Maya of Vishnu.

ii. Vishnu is the all-pervading principle, and Maya is the power through which names, forms, and the universe are projected. Sreedevee, as the power of Vishnu, is called Vishnumaya. This also indicates that the sustaining function of the universe operates through her power.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya clarifies Her role as the grand cosmic veil:

The Projective Illusion: She is that supreme, mysterious power of Viṣṇu mentioned in the Devī Māhātmya ("या देवी सर्वभूतेषु विष्णुमायेति शब्दिता"). She casts the blanket of name and form over the absolute consciousness, making the non-dual appear as dual, while simultaneously holding the key to removing that very illusion.

Nāma 340

विलासिनी

Samāsa-vigraha

विलासः अस्याः अस्तीति।

Word by word

विलासः — sport; graceful play; shining expression

अस्याः — of her

अस्ति — exists

विलासिनी — she who possesses divine sport or graceful play

Meaning

i. One who is sportive and graceful.

ii. Vilasa denotes play, graceful movement, and manifestation. The universe is her divine play, and her beauty, actions, and manifestations are expressions of that play. She is therefore called Vilasini.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, this name defines Her relationship with the world process:

The Universe as Play: The entire projection, maintenance, and collapse of the infinite worlds is not an arduous task for Her; it is Her effortless, joyful play (vilāsa). She is the ultimate actress enjoying the performance of Her own cosmic theater.

Nāma 341

क्षेत्रस्वरूपा

Samāsa-vigraha

क्षेत्रं स्वं रूपं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

क्षेत्रं — field; body; matter

स्वं रूपं — own form

यस्याः — of whom; whose

क्षेत्रस्वरूपा — she whose own form is the field

Meaning

i. One whose body is matter, the body of all beings.

ii. Kshetram is the field ready for cultivation through removal of weeds, ploughing, and watering. Similarly, a place made ready through mantra, tantra, and yantra for attaining godliness is called kshetra.

iii. The thirty-six categories, from earth to Shiva, form her body. That is why Parameshvara is called Kshetrajna. The Bhagavad Gita describes the relation between kshetra and kshetrajna.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya interprets this directly through the 13th chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā:

The Material Field: क्षेत्र represents the entire mutable universe, the physical body, and the field of matter (Prakṛti). She clarifies that the physical universe is not a separate, dirty element to be discarded; it is Her own visible, tangible form.

Nāma 342

क्षेत्रेशी

Samāsa-vigraha

क्षेत्रस्य यः ईशः तस्य इयम्।

Word by word

क्षेत्रस्य — of the field; of matter

ईशः — lord; ruler

तस्य इयम् — she who belongs to him; his power or consort

क्षेत्रेशी — ruler of the field; consort of Kshetesha

Meaning

i. One who is the ruler of matter, or the consort of Kshetesha, Shiva.

ii. There is absolutely no difference between Sreedevee and Parameshvara. The Tripura Upanishad is remembered in this context as saying that Shakti and Bhagavan are one in essence.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya establishes Her governance over matter:

The Owner of the Field: While She manifests as the physical field (Kṣetra), She simultaneously functions as its absolute ruler (Īśvarī). She commands the laws of nature, biology, and chemistry, ensuring that the field operates in perfect synchronization.

Nāma 343

क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञपालिनी

Samāsa-vigraha

क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञं च पालयतीति।

Word by word

क्षेत्रं — field; body; matter

क्षेत्रज्ञं — knower of the field

च — and

पालयति — protects

क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञपालिनी — she who protects both matter and the knower of matter

Meaning

i. One who is the protector of matter and the knower of matter.

ii. Kshetram is the body and Kshetrajna is the soul. She protects both; the Bhagavad Gita may be referred to.

iii. Linga Purana says that the twenty-four tattvas are kshetras and the purusha who enjoys them is the kshetrajna. Sreedevee alone takes the form of all these kshetras and kshetrajnas.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details Her dual protective custody:

Sustaining Matter and Soul: She sustains the objective physical world (kṣetra) so that experiences can occur, and She simultaneously guards the subjective individual soul (kṣetrajña) on its long journey through saṁsāra, ensuring its eventual awakening to its own true nature.

Nāma 344

क्षयवृद्धिविनिर्मुक्ता

Samāsa-vigraha

क्षयवृद्धिभ्यां विनिर्मुक्ता।

Word by word

क्षय — decay; reduction

वृद्धि — growth; increase

विनिर्मुक्ता — completely free from

क्षयवृद्धिविनिर्मुक्ता — she who is free from growth and decay

Meaning

i. One who is free from decay and growth.

ii. Growth and decay belong to kshetra. Though she is related to kshetra and is the ruler and protector of kshetra and kshetrajna, she is free from growth and decay. The Bhagavad Gita says that weapons do not cut the soul, fire does not burn it, water does not wet it, and wind does not dry it.

iii. She is free from those actions which are the result of actions, and she is not connected with actions. Brihadaranyaka Upanishad says that this is the eternal glory of the knower of Brahman: he neither increases by actions nor decreases by bad actions.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya highlights Her immutability (Nirvikāra):

Beyond Material Mutations: Decay (kṣaya) and growth (vṛddhi) are two of the six structural mutations (ṣaḍ-bhāva-vikāra) that apply strictly to material objects and physical bodies. As the eternal, changeless consciousness background, She undergoes no modifications, remaining constant across all time.

Nāma 345

क्षेत्रपालसमर्चिता

Samāsa-vigraha

क्षेत्रं पालयति तेन समयग् अर्चिता।

Word by word

क्षेत्रं — field; sacred precinct; body

पालः — protector

सम्यक् अर्चिता — well worshipped

क्षेत्रपालसमर्चिता — she who is well worshipped by Kshetrapala

Meaning

i. One who is adored by Kshetrapala.

ii. As per Linga and other Puranas, Kali was created by Shiva to slay Darukasura. After killing the demon her wrath did not subside, and Shiva assumed the form of a crying infant. She suckled the child, who drank the fire of her anger with milk. This child is called Kshetrapala, an incarnation of Shiva, and Sreedevee was prayed to by him.

iii. In the results part of this Sahasranamam it is said that Kshetrapala kills anyone who snatches the wealth of those who recite this Sahasranamam. In this way Kshetrapala protects the devotees. She was worshipped by that Kshetrapala.

iv. Literally, kshetra is the precinct of the sacrificial ceremony and pala is the protector. Kshetrapala protects sacrificial ceremonies, and she was worshipped by that Kshetrapala.

v. Kshetra is also the body. The protectors in this body are fire, air, sun, and so on. She is worshipped by them.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya decodes this through both ritual tradition and subtle yoga:

The Guardian's Adoration: Mythologically, Kṣetrapāla is the terrifying Bhairava form assigned to guard the boundaries of Her temples and sacred zones.

The Guardian of the Gate: Esoterically, he represents the structural boundary intelligence guarding the entry to the higher spiritual channels. Even this supreme guardian must worship Her to maintain his office.

Nāma 346

विजया

Samāsa-vigraha

विशिष्टः जयः यस्याः सा।

Word by word

विशिष्टः — special; excellent

जयः — victory

यस्याः — of whom; whose

विजया — she whose victory is special; victorious one

Meaning

i. One who is victorious.

ii. Vijaya means special victory. She is victorious over all obstacles, demons, ignorance, and the forces opposed to dharma. The name also indicates the victory obtained by devotees through her grace.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya interprets Her victorious nature as absolute and unconditioned:

The Triumphant Power: Her victory is not a temporary triumph over a rival; it is Her fundamental state of being. As the supreme reality, She remains forever victorious over the dark forces of ignorance (avidyā), delusion, and death, guaranteeing victory to those who align with Her.

Nāma 347

विमला

Samāsa-vigraha

विगतः मलः यस्याः सा।

Word by word

विगतः — gone; removed

मलः — impurity; blemish

यस्याः — of whom; whose

विमला — she who is free from impurity

Meaning

i. One who is without impurity.

ii. Mala means impurity. Since no impurity belongs to her, she is Vimala. She is pure consciousness, untouched by the impurities that bind the soul.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya defines Mala according to the three structural impurities of the Agamas:

Free from the Three Impurities: She is completely untouched by the three fundamental taints: आणवमल (āṇava-mala — the stain of limitation/ego), मायीयमल (māyīya-mala — the stain of illusion/differentiated perception), and कार्ममल (kārma-mala — the stain of binding action). She remains pure, unblemished awareness.

Nāma 348

वन्द्या

Samāsa-vigraha

वन्दितुं योग्या।

Word by word

वन्दितुम् — to be saluted; to be worshipped

योग्या — worthy

वन्द्या — worthy of worship

Meaning

i. One who is worthy of worship.

ii. She is to be worshipped by all, because she is the source, support, and goal of the universe. Devas, sages, and devotees bow to her.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya notes the absolute necessity of bowing before Her:

The Object of Universal Salutation: She is the baseline source of all life and light. Therefore, She is the natural, ultimate point of adoration for all living beings, from the simple seeker to the highest cosmic deities. Bowing to Her is the method to dissolve the rigid individual ego.

Nāma 349

वन्दारुजनवत्सला

Samāsa-vigraha

वन्दारून् जनान् वत्सवत् लातीति।

Word by word

वन्दारून् — those who bow or worship

जनान् — people

वत्सवत् — like calves; with affection

लाति — protects; nourishes

वन्दारुजनवत्सला — she who loves and protects worshipping people like her children

Meaning

i. One who is affectionate to those who bow to her.

ii. Vatsala is one who shows love like a mother toward her child. Sreedevee shows such tenderness to worshippers and protects those who bow down to her.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya highlights Her overwhelming maternal instinct:

The Maternal Reflex: वत्सला (vatsalā) describes the pure, instinctive love a cow has for her newborn calf, rushing to protect it and feeding it unconditionally. She displays this exact spontaneous, fiercely protective grace toward any devotee who drops their pride and bows before Her.

Nāma 350

वाग्वादिनी

Samāsa-vigraha

वाचं वदतीति।

वाचं वादयतीति।

Word by word

वाचम् — speech; word

वदति — speaks

वादयति — causes to speak; makes speech function

वाग्वादिनी — she who speaks, and who causes speech to arise

Meaning

i. One who speaks, or who causes speech.

ii. She is the power behind speech and the one who enables speech to function. As Vak, she is the source of words, meaning, and expression.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya decodes Her identity as the animator of intelligence:

The Power of Articulation: She is the underlying force that causes speech and language to manifest. Bhāskararāya notes that She does not just speak; She sits as the inner voice that inspires and translates raw thought into articulate speech inside the intellects of poets, scholars, and seers.

Nāma 351

वामकेशी

Samāsa-vigraha

वामाः केशाः यस्याः सा।

वामाः एव वामकाः ये तेषाम् ईशस्य पत्नी।

Word by word

वामाः — beautiful; also left-sided

केशाः — hair

यस्याः — of whom; whose

ईशस्य पत्नी — consort of the Lord

वामकेशी — she with beautiful hair; consort of the Lord of the Vamaka group

Meaning

i. One who has beautiful hair.

ii. The name also admits another interpretation connected with Vamaka and the Lord. In the simple sense, her hair is beautiful and auspicious.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya illuminates Her position within the Agamic divisions:

The Consort of Vāmakeśvara: In the Tantric corporate architecture, She is the primary deity of the Vāmakeśvara Tantra, one of the most core source texts of the Śrīvidyā tradition. Her "hair" represents the infinite, uncoiled rays of cosmic energy that stream out to form the manifest worlds.

Nāma 352

वह्निमण्डलवासिनी

Samāsa-vigraha

वह्नेः यत् मण्डलं तत्र वसतीति।

Word by word

वह्नेः — of fire

मण्डलं — circle; orb

तत्र — there

वसति — dwells

वह्निमण्डलवासिनी — she who dwells in the circle of fire

Meaning

i. One who dwells in the circle of fire.

ii. Fire is a sacred and purifying principle. She is contemplated as dwelling in the fire-orb, and the worship connected with fire and inner radiance is indicated by this name.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya interprets this across structural yogic levels:

The Fire Center: In the internal layout of Kuṇḍalinī Yoga, the वह्निमण्डल represents the Mūladhāra and Maṇipūra regions where the primal digestive and spiritual fire resides. She stays hidden inside this internal fire, functioning as the spark that purifies the practitioner's gross karmic elements during Her ascent.

Nāma 353

भक्तिमत्कल्पलतिका

Samāsa-vigraha

भक्तिमतां कल्पलतिका इव।

Word by word

भक्तिमताम् — of those who possess devotion

कल्पलतिका — wish-fulfilling creeper

इव — like

भक्तिमत्कल्पलतिका — she who is like a wish-fulfilling creeper for devotees

Meaning

i. One who is like a wish-fulfilling creeper to the devotees.

ii. Kalpalatika means a creeper that grants what is desired. She fulfils the true aspirations of devotees. Latika also suggests a fragrant, mind-soothing creeper; Sreedevee is like such a soothing creeper to her devotees.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya uses a celestial botanical metaphor to explain Her responsiveness:

The Wishing Creeper: The mythological Kalpa-latā yields any fruit immediately upon being asked. Similarly, She wraps around the consciousness of those who possess genuine devotion (bhaktimat), effortlessly dropping whatever fruits they require—whether material security or the ultimate fruit of liberation.

Nāma 354

पशुपाशविमोचनी

Samāsa-vigraha

पशोः पाशं विमोचयतीति।

पशूनां पाशे (पिपासाशनाये) विशिष्य मोचयतीति।

पशुपस्य आशा येषां ते पशुपाशाः। तान् विशेषण मोचयतीति।

Word by word

पशोः — of the pashu, the bound soul or ignorant being

पाशं — bondage; fetter

विमोचयति — releases completely

पशूनाम् — of ignorant beings

पिपासा-अशनाये — thirst and hunger

विशिष्य — especially; completely

पशुपाशविमोचनी — she who releases bound souls from their bonds

Meaning

i. One who releases the ignorant from bondage.

ii. Pashus are those who are devoid of the conviction of non-separation. Brihadaranyaka Upanishad says that one who worships another deity thinking that the deity is different and he himself is different does not know; he is like a pashu.

iii. Pa means thirst and asa means hunger. Pasha therefore indicates hunger and thirst. These arise from five afflictions, and these afflictions themselves are bindings. On the whole there are seven bondages. Sreedevee releases ignorant people from these bondages. They are called pashus because they are concerned only with eating and drinking.

iv. The five afflictions are: avidya, the absence of discrimination between the Self and not-Self; asmita, egoism; raga, desire for worldly things; dvesha, anger or hatred when desire is obstructed; and abhinivesha, deep attachment even to what one knows is not beneficial. These are explained in Yoga Sutra and also in Devi Bhagavatam and Linga Purana under different names.

v. Kularnava Tantra mentions eight afflictions such as cruelty, doubt, fear, shame, disgust, race, fame, and caste. Bhaskararaya notes that the divisions become very many and does not expand all sub-divisions further.

vi. According to the Katapayadi method, pasha indicates the number fifty-one, though it may also be taken as fifty-two in some explanations. The point is that she releases the devotees from all these afflictions, whether counted as fifty-one, fifty-two, or otherwise.

vii. The afflictions are also considered as three types: atomic impurity, difference, and action. Those bound by them are classified in different ways in Pratyabhijna Shastra, Shiva Sutra, Nityahridaya, and Svachchanda Tantra. Liberation from these bonds is possible only through the liberating energy of Sreedevee; without that energy Shiva does not act. Thus she is Pashupasha-vimochani.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya provides an extensive breakdown using classical Śaiva/Śākta Agamic terminology:

The Soul and the Tether: पशु (Paśu) refers to the individual soul, bound because it behaves like an animal driven by instinct. पाश (Pāśa) is the rope or tether consisting of ignorance, ego, and karma that keeps the soul tied to the post of saṁsāra.

The Act of Liberation: As Paśupāśavimocanī, She cuts these bindings cleanly, transforming the bound creature (Paśu) into the absolute lord (Pati), granting immediate spiritual freedom.

Nāma 355

संहृताशेषपाषण्डा

Samāsa-vigraha

संहृताः अशेषाः पाषण्डाः यया सा।

Word by word

संहृताः — destroyed; removed

अशेषाः — without remainder; all

पाषण्डाः — heretics; deniers of sacred dharma

यया — by whom

संहृताशेषपाषण्डा — she by whom all heresy is destroyed

Meaning

i. One who is the destroyer of all heretics, those who are averse to spiritual values.

ii. Linga Purana describes heretics as those who observe vows not enjoined in the Vedas and those excluded from ceremonies enjoined by Shruti and Smriti. Such persons are not to mingle with or be spoken to by the twice-born.

iii. Brahma Vaivarta Purana also says that Puranas, Nyaya, Mimamsa, Dharma Shastras, the six Vedangas, and the four Vedas are the seats of righteousness. Whatever is imagined by people beyond these is heresy; she destroys all such pashandas.

iv. In some schools the word is written as Pakhanda, with the same meaning: pa, the Vedas, and khanda, cutting off. She destroys such pakhanda also.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya defines Pāṣaṇḍa through the lens of scriptural integrity:

The Destruction of Delusion: Pāṣaṇḍa refers to systems that distort the truth, promote nihilism, or lead souls away from the realization of the true self. She does not destroy the people, but She completely dismantles their false views, replacing intellectual blindness with the clean, non-dual light of real knowledge.

Nāma 356

सदाचारप्रवर्तिका

Samāsa-vigraha

सदाचारस्य प्रवर्तिका।

Word by word

सत् — good; noble; auspicious

आचारस्य — of conduct; practice

प्रवर्तिका — promoter; one who sets in motion

सदाचारप्रवर्तिका — she who promotes right conduct

Meaning

i. One who inspires right action.

ii. Because she destroys the wicked, she incites people to right action.

iii. Sat means great or auspicious, and achara means conduct. She directs people toward great and auspicious conduct.

iv. She gives the inclination to observe the precepts enjoined in the Karma Kanda of the Vedas and the Advaita Brahman taught in the Jnana Kanda, through the means laid down in the Puranas. In Kurma Purana, Devi says that the eighteen Puranas were promulgated by Vyasa by the command of Brahman and that righteousness is established in them. Thus the supreme dharma coming from Brahma, Manu, Vyasa, and others remains established until dissolution.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya explains Her role as the guardian of practice:

The Instiller of Right Conduct: True spiritual practice requires a clean baseline of ethical and ritual discipline (Sadācāra). She operates as the inner conscience that inspires seekers to perform their daily duties, clean their minds, and maintain the external and internal purity necessary for higher meditation.

Nāma 357

तापत्रयाग्निसंतप्तसमाह्लादनचन्द्रिका

Samāsa-vigraha

तापानां त्रयं यस्य तेन अग्निना सम्यक् तप्तानां सम्यग् आह्लादनेन चन्द्रिका इव।

Word by word

तापत्रय — the three sufferings

अग्नि — fire

संतप्त — scorched; afflicted

समाह्लादन — complete soothing; delighting

चन्द्रिका — moonlight

तापत्रयाग्निसंतप्तसमाह्लादनचन्द्रिका — she who soothes like moonlight those scorched by the fire of the three afflictions

Meaning

i. One who gives, like the moon, soothing relief to those who suffer from the fire of the three kinds of distress.

ii. The sufferings are of three types: adhyatmikam, adhidaivikam, and adhibhautikam.

Adhyatmikam means disturbances stemming from the self and relating to the body, the five sense organs, the five organs of action, mind, intellect, ego, and volition.

Adhibhautikam means disturbances that come from the world and the five basic elements relating to the above organs.

Adhidaivikam means mental disturbances that come from divine or unseen causes beyond human control, such as flood and similar events.

These three are characteristics of the cycle of life. This name indicates that she makes the soul suffering from these disturbances happy by removing suffering through her moon-like compassion.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya identifies the three specific fires that afflict human existence:

The Three Afflictions: The fires are आध्यात्मिक (ādhyātmika — miseries arising from one's own body and mind), आधिभौतिक (ādhibhautika — miseries caused by other living creatures), and आधिदैविक (ādhidaivika — miseries caused by cosmic or supernatural forces).

The Cooling Moonlight: The heat of these three fires makes life a constant burning struggle. Her presence acts as pure, soothing moonlight (Candrikā), which instantly cools the burning distress of the mind, bringing absolute stillness.

Nāma 358

तरुणी

Samāsa-vigraha

नित्यतारुणवत्वात् तरुणी।

Word by word

नित्य — eternal; always

तारुणवत्वात् — because of youthfulness

तरुणी — ever young

Meaning

i. One who is ever young.

ii. Sreedevee does not have growth or reduction. The name Kshaya-vriddhi-vinirmukta may be referred to.

iii. Sreedevee does not have a beginning or an end. If there is a beginning there will be growth; if there is an end there will be reduction. Sreedevee does not have these.

iv. She is eternal, present in all three times. The names Nitya and Purna convey the same sense, and the name Nitya-yauvana may also be referred to.

v. The sense conveyed by the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad - without ageing and immortal - is reflected here.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya clarifies that Her youth is completely free from the decay of linear time:

Eternally Youthful: She is Nitya-tāruṇya-vatī—permanently anchored in a state of fresh, vibrant youthfulness. Unlike material bodies that age, decay, and wrinkle, Her consciousness remains eternally fresh, dynamic, and vital, never suffering the decrepitude of time.

Nāma 359

तापसाराध्या

Samāsa-vigraha

तापसैः आराध्या।

Word by word

तापसैः — by ascetics; by those practising austerity

आराध्या — worshipped; to be adored

तापसाराध्या — she who is worshipped by ascetics

Meaning

i. One who is worshipped by ascetics.

ii. Or, tapa means samsara, the source of misery; sara means essence or depth; and adhya means meditation. Sreedevee, who is the root cause of this samsara life-cycle, is the essential object of meditation.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya describes the level of qualifications required to truly grasp Her nature:

The Object of Deep Penance: She is not easily reached by scattered, superficial minds. She is Tāpasārādhyā because the true method to approach Her is through Tapas—the intense, concentrated burning away of external desires and sensory distractions. She is the ultimate goal sought after by those who have dedicated their entire lives to quiet internal absorption.

Nāma 360

तनुमध्या

Samāsa-vigraha

तनुः मध्यः यस्याः सा।

Word by word

तनुः — slender; thin

मध्यः — waist; middle

यस्याः — of whom; whose

सा — she

तनुमध्या — she whose waist is slender

Meaning

i. One who has a slender waist.

ii. Earlier, in the thirty-fifth name Lakshya-romalata-dharata-samunneya-madhyama, the middle portion of Sreedevee was described. This name again indicates the slenderness and beauty of that middle portion.

iii. Tanumadhya is also the deity worshipped in the country of Kanchi. A verse prays that Sreedevee Tanumadhya, the consort of Bilvesvara and dwelling on the bank of the river Niva, may protect the devotee.

iv. Tanumadhya is also the name of a metre. With six letters in each foot, it has twenty-four letters. The Gayatri metre also has twenty-four letters, and the Bhagavad Gita statement Gayatri chandasam aham may be remembered.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya moves past the physical description to structural cosmology and yoga:

The Cosmic Juncture: Madhya represents the unmanifest state between creation and dissolution. Her waist is tanu (infinitesimally small or non-existent), meaning the boundary line between the manifest universe and the unmanifest absolute is extraordinarily subtle, almost imperceptible.

The Suṣumṇā Channel: In the subtle body, She represents the core energy path, where the central junction (madhya)—the Suṣumṇā channel—is incredibly fine and subtle (tanu).

Nāma 361

तमोपहा

Samāsa-vigraha

तमः अपहन्तीति।

Word by word

तमः — darkness; ignorance

अपहन्ति — removes; destroys

तमोपहा — remover of darkness

Meaning

i. One who removes darkness.

ii. She removes from devotees the darkness called ignorance.

iii. The Ishavasya Upanishad says that those who worship ignorance enter into blind darkness. The same idea is recalled in Lalita Trishati, where the Shruti condemns those who worship ignorance.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya targets the ultimate cause of spiritual bondage:

The Destruction of Ignorance: तमस् (tamas) refers to both physical darkness and the spiritual ignorance (avidyā) that veils the soul's true nature. As Tamopahā, She acts as the spiritual sun that burns away the structural darkness of egoic illusion, instantly granting the clarity of self-realization.

Nāma 362

चितिः

Samāsa-vigraha

चितिः।

Word by word

चितिः — consciousness; knowledge; awareness

Meaning

i. One who is in the form of knowledge.

ii. In Pratyabhijna Hridaya it is said that Chit is independent and is the cause of the establishment of the universe.

iii. In Mahavasishtha, Sreedevee is called Chit because she is the life of those who desire life.

iv. In Saptashati, Chiti is mentioned as the conscious form that pervades the whole universe.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya defines this name as Her absolute, unconditioned foundation:

Pure Awareness: She is not merely an entity that possesses consciousness; She is consciousness itself (Citi). This is the static, eternal background light that illuminates all mental operations, thoughts, and physical movements without undergoing any change itself.

Nāma 363

तत्पदलक्ष्यार्था

Samāsa-vigraha

तत् इति पदेन लक्षणीयः अर्थः यस्याः सा।

Word by word

तत् — that; the word Tat

पदेन — by the word

लक्षणीयः — indicated indirectly; implied

अर्थः — meaning

यस्याः — of whom; whose

तत्पदलक्ष्यार्था — she who is the implied meaning of the word Tat

Meaning

i. One who is the connotation of the word Tat in the Mahavakya.

ii. In the Mahavakya Tat tvam asi, the word Tat indicates Brahman as the cause of creation and other cosmic functions. Its implied meaning is the same Brahman in its taskless, pure form.

iii. She is in the form of Brahman indicated by that implied meaning. The later name Tat may also be referred to.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya applies the standard Vedāntic exegetical method of Lakṣaṇā (indirect indication):

The Transcendent Absolute: In the sentence "Tat Tvam Asi" (That Thou Art), the literal meaning (vācyārtha) of Tat is the omniscient, personal creator God (Īśvara). However, when the structural limitations of cosmic veiling are stripped away, the implied meaning (lakṣyārtha) is the pure, non-dual, infinite consciousness (Parabrahman). She is that ultimate reality.

Nāma 364

चिदेकरसरूपिणी

Samāsa-vigraha

चिदेव रसः येषां तानि रूपाणि अस्याः इति।

Word by word

चित् — consciousness

एव — alone; indeed

रसः — essence

रूपिणी — she whose form is

चिदेकरसरूपिणी — she whose forms have consciousness alone as their essence

Meaning

i. One who is completely in the form of knowledge.

ii. The attributes of bliss, consciousness and intellect are inseparable from her. Though she appears in different forms, her conscious form is full of knowledge, and knowledge itself is to be taken as the single essence.

iii. This is explained in the Panchapadika of Padmapadacharya: bliss, perception of objects and eternity, though inseparable from consciousness, appear as different attributes.

iv. She is never separated from Chit. Though they appear different by attributes, they are really one and the same.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya explains the term एकरस (homogenous flavor):

Homogenous Reality: Just as a vast body of salt water has only one taste throughout, Her entire multi-layered manifestation has only one underlying flavor, substance, and essence: pure consciousness (Cit). Matter and mind are merely dense modifications of this single divine juice.

Nāma 365

स्वात्मानन्दलवीभूतब्रह्माद्यानन्दसन्ततिः

Samāsa-vigraha

स्वस्याः आत्मारूपः यः आनन्दः तस्य लवीभूताः ब्रह्मादीनां सन्ततयः यस्याः सा।

Word by word

स्वस्याः — of her own

आत्मारूपः — in the form of the Self

आनन्दः — bliss

लवीभूताः — become a tiny particle

ब्रह्मादीनाम् — of Brahma and others

सन्ततयः — streams; continuities

स्वात्मानन्दलवीभूतब्रह्माद्यानन्दसन्ततिः — she whose own Self-bliss makes the bliss of Brahma and others only a minute particle

Meaning

i. The totality of the bliss of Brahma and others is only a minute portion of her own bliss.

ii. The three gods who perform creation, protection and destruction, as well as Indra and other devas, enjoy bliss; but this is only a drop when compared with the bliss of Sreedevee.

iii. The Taittiriya Upanishad says that other beings live on a mere part of this bliss. The grades of bliss described there increase up to Brahma, but remain limited. Her bliss is the unlimited bliss of Brahman.

iv. Lava means a particle. The name therefore shows that all other blisses are only small particles of her own Self-bliss.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya anchors this directly in the Taittirīya and Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad evaluations of bliss (Ānanda-mīmāṁsā):

The Ocean and the Drop: The highest imaginable happiness in the relative universe is the bliss of the creator Brahmā. Yet, scriptural revelation states that his bliss is merely a tiny drop leaked from the infinite reservoir of Brahman. She is that ocean; the ultimate spiritual ecstasy of the highest cosmic administrators is just an tiny splash of Her inherent nature.

Nāma 366

परा

Samāsa-vigraha

परानन्दाभिधे तन्त्रे प्रसिद्धत्वाच्च सा परा।

Word by word

परा — supreme; transcendent; the highest form of speech

परानन्द — supreme bliss

प्रसिद्धत्वात् — because of being well known

Meaning

i. One who is in the form of the sound called Para, the transcendent word.

ii. Speech is described in four forms: Para, Pashyanti, Madhyama and Vaikhari. The physical uttered speech expresses only gross form; the pure unconditioned Brahman is indicated through subtler levels of sound.

iii. In the process of manifestation, the causal bindu, nada and bija are discussed as stages of sound and creation. In the bodily aspect, the causal bindu is in the Muladhara and is known as Shakti or Kundalini.

iv. The first motionless sound in the Muladhara is called Para speech. From it arise the later stages: Pashyanti, Madhyama and Vaikhari. The Veda says that speech has four measured quarters; the wise know them, three are hidden, and human beings speak only the fourth.

v. From the name Tatpadalakshyartha up to Vaikhari-rupa, it is described that Sreedevee herself is in all four grades of speech. Tripura-siddhanta also explains Para as the supreme form and the source of grace.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya decodes this name as the highest level of speech (Vāk) within Tantric linguistics:

The Unmanifest Source: परा (Parā) is the first, highest, and most subtle stage of sound manifestation. It resides completely unmanifested in the Mūladhāra chakra as pure, undifferentiated potential energy. It is the silent, flashing seed of consciousness before a single ripple of thought or sound occurs.

Nāma 367

प्रत्यक्चितीरूपा

Samāsa-vigraha

प्रतिकूलम् अञ्चतीति प्रतिची। सा च सा चिती च प्रत्यक्चिती। सा रूपं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

प्रत्यक् — inward; turned toward the Self

चिती — consciousness; knowledge

रूपा — form

प्रत्यक्चितीरूपा — she who is in the form of inner consciousness

Meaning

i. One who is in the form of inner consciousness.

ii. The nature of the sense organs is to move outward. Para, the great subtle form of sound, is recognised only by the mind turned inward. This inward turning is called Pratyak.

iii. With inward attention, the mind recognises the Para-knowledge in the form of Brahman without distinction of matter, energy and qualities. Thus Sreedevee is Pratyak-Chiti, the great inward knowledge.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya highlights the exact direction of self-realization:

The Inward Gaze: Ordinary consciousness moves outward (parāñc) through the senses to perceive material objects. प्रत्यक् (pratyak) describes the exact reverse motion—turning the attention 180 degrees backward, away from the world, directly into the source of awareness. She is that specific internal witness textually realized when the mind rests in the self.

Nāma 368

पश्यन्ती

Samāsa-vigraha

पश्यतीति पश्यन्ती।

Word by word

पश्यति — sees

पश्यन्ती — she who sees; the second subtle stage of speech

Meaning

i. One who is in the form of Pashyanti, speech in the inaudible stage.

ii. Earlier, under the name Para, the four stages of speech were discussed. The second stage is Pashyanti, and she is in that form.

iii. Saubhagya-sudhodaya says that because she sees all and sees all in herself, she is called Pashyanti. Since she rises above the path of action, she is also called Uttirna; the name Kulottirna may be referred to.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya provides the second structural layer of phonic manifestation:

The Visualized Thought: As the cosmic sound descends from the unmanifest Parā state into the Sahasrāra and Maṇipūra regions, it becomes पश्यन्ती (Paśyantī). At this stage, sound is not yet audible speech, but it exists as a luminous, holistic vision or a unified ideation within the cosmic mind. She is the witness of this primal creative vision.

Nāma 369

परदेवता

Samāsa-vigraha

परा च असौ देवता च।

Word by word

परा — supreme

देवता — deity; object of worship

परदेवता — the supreme deity

Meaning

i. One who is the object of supreme devotion.

ii. She is worshipped as the supreme deity and as the ultimate Godhead to be meditated upon.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya clarifies Her ultimate hierarchical position in the universe:

The Sovereign Object of Worship: While there are numerous local, planetary, and functional deities responsible for individual aspects of nature, She is the Paradevatā—the absolute, ultimate divine matrix from whom all other gods draw their authority, existence, and power. She is the final destination of all lines of devotion.

Nāma 370

मध्यमा

Samāsa-vigraha

मध्ये स्थिता।

Word by word

मध्ये — in the middle

स्थिता — situated

मध्यमा — the middle stage of speech

Meaning

i. One who is in the form of Madhyama, speech in the middle stage of its external expression.

ii. This stage is not like Pashyanti, which stops immediately after rising, nor like Vaikhari, in which articulation is fully developed. It is the intermediate stage between the two and is therefore called Madhyama.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya unpacks the third layer of the descent of sound:

The Mental Articulation: Located primarily in the region of the heart (Anāhata), मध्यमा (Madhyamā) is the intermediate stage of speech. Here, the unified vision of Paśyantī breaks down into specific words, sentences, and mental concepts, though it is still internal and silent to the outside world. She is the inner thinker structuring this mental language.

Nāma 371

वैखरीरूपा

Samāsa-vigraha

विशेषेण खरः विखरः। तस्य इयम् एव रूपं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

विशेषेण — specially; distinctly

खरः — hard; audible sound

वैखरी — uttered speech

रूपा — form

वैखरीरूपा — she who is in the form of articulated speech

Meaning

i. One who is in the form of Vaikhari, the uttered audible speech.

ii. The hard and manifest form of letters, issuing as sound through the throat and mouth, is Vaikhari. Scattered sound, carried by air and made dense through articulation, becomes the form of words.

iii. Saubhagya-sudhodaya explains the word as that which clearly enters the cavity of the ear. Yoga texts also connect Vaikhari with the air that brings sound from the heart through the throat.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya completes the magnificent four-fold phonetic sequence (from 366 to 371):

Audible Communication: When sound passes up through the throat and is shaped by the tongue, teeth, and lips, it emerges as वैखरी (Vaikharī)—gross, audible sound waves capable of being heard by the ears of others. Bhāskararāya notes that every spoken word, sentence, and mantra in the universe is Her physical voice in this dense state of material expression.

Nāma 372

भक्तमानसहंसिका

Samāsa-vigraha

भक्तानां मानसे हंसीव हंसिका।

Word by word

भक्तानाम् — of devotees

मानसे — in the mind; in the Manasa lake-like mind

हंसी इव — like a swan

हंसिका — female swan

भक्तमानसहंसिका — she who is like a swan in the minds of devotees

Meaning

i. One who is in the form of a swan in the lake-like minds of devotees.

ii. Brahma created the pure Manasa lake on Kailasha, where swans dwell. The pure minds of devotees are compared to that lake, and Sreedevee is compared to the swan dwelling there.

iii. Soundaryalahari also compares the divine pair to swans moving in the minds of the great. She is invisible to others, that is, to those who are not devotees. The name Muni-manasa-hamsika may also be referred to.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya utilizes this classic aesthetic metaphor to describe Her internal residence:

Sporting in the Heart: A swan will only swim in perfectly clear, clean water, such as the sacred lake Mānasarovara. Similarly, She chooses to manifest Her presence inside the lake of the devotee's mind (mānasa) only when it is cleared of the mud of worldly desire and kept perfectly serene, playing there as the breath of life (Haṁsa).

Nāma 373

कामेश्वरप्राणनाडी

Samāsa-vigraha

कामेश्वरस्य प्राणनाडीव।

Word by word

कामेश्वरस्य — of Kameshvara

प्राणनाडी — life-current; vital nerve

इव — like

कामेश्वरप्राणनाडी — she who is like the life-current of Kameshvara

Meaning

i. One who is like the life-current of Kameshvara.

ii. Prana is the life principle. A nadi carries that vital force. Sreedevee is so inseparably connected with Kameshvara that she is described as his very prana-nadi.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya highlights the absolute, inseparable nature of Shiva and Shakti:

The Vital Breath of Shiva: Shiva (Kāmeśvara) represents the foundational, static consciousness. Without Her presence as the kinetic vital channel (Prāṇa-nāḍī), He remains unmanifest and inert. She is the very pulse, life, and breath that animates Him, demonstrating that they are as inseparable as fire and heat.

Nāma 374

कृतज्ञा

Samāsa-vigraha

कृते जानातीति।

Word by word

कृते — what has been done; action performed

जानाति — knows

कृतज्ञा — she who knows what has been done; grateful one

Meaning

i. One who knows what has been done.

ii. She knows even the smallest service or worship performed by devotees. She is therefore grateful in the highest sense and never ignores the devotion shown to her.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya illuminates Her absolute attentiveness to the devotee's internal efforts:

Remembering Small Devotions: Humans often forget favors done by others. She is Kṛtajñā because She remembers even the smallest, most hidden act of devotion, mental surrender, or ritual offering performed by a seeker. She accounts for every step taken toward Her, returning it with infinite grace.

Nāma 375

कामपूजिता

Samāsa-vigraha

कामेन पूजिता।

Word by word

कामेन — by Kama; by desire; by Kameshvara

पूजिता — worshipped

कामपूजिता — she who is worshipped by Kama

Meaning

i. One who is worshipped by Kama.

ii. Kama may indicate Manmatha or Kameshvara. She is worshipped by him and is also the supreme object sought by desire when desire becomes purified.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya connects this directly to the foundational lineage of Śrīvidyā:

The Kāmarāja Lineage: Kāmadeva is not merely a god of mundane desire; he is one of the twelve great founding seers (kādi-mata) who brought down the premier structural formulation of the fifteen-syllabled Pañcadaśākṣarī Mantra. His worship is sublime and purifies the creative drive, realigning it toward cosmic union.

Nāma 376

शृङ्गाररससम्पूर्णा

Samāsa-vigraha

शृङ्गम् अररं यस्याः सा शृङ्गाररा। सा एव सम्पूर्णेन ब्रह्मणा सह ससम्पूर्णा च।

Word by word

शृङ्गाररस — the rasa of love and beauty

सम्पूर्णा — completely full

ब्रह्मणा सह — together with Brahman

शृङ्गाररससम्पूर्णा — she who is full of the rasa of love and beauty

Meaning

i. One who is filled with the rasa of love and beauty.

ii. Shringara is the rasa of love. Sreedevee is complete in this rasa. The name also admits a deeper interpretation linking her completeness with Brahman.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya defines Śṛṅgāra past its common physical interpretation:

The Sentiment of Union: Śṛṅgāra is the premier aesthetic emotion (Rasa-rāja). In its highest cosmic sense, it represents the absolute attraction and ecstatic love between the individual soul and the universal self, or between Shiva and Shakti. She is the infinite reservoir of this divine love.

Samāsa-vigraha

स्वरूपा — whose nature is

Meaning

i. One who is victory itself.

ii. She is the victorious power, and through her grace the devotee gains victory over inner and outer obstacles.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya tracks Her identity within ritual and historical frameworks:

The Energy of Success: She is the absolute state of victory itself. She functions as the specific energy that enables righteousness to triumph over unrighteousness. Furthermore, in the context of the Śrī Cakra, She represents the specialized protective force executing Her sovereign commands.

i. One who is situated in Jalandhara.

ii. Jalandhara is one of the sacred seats connected with worship. She is present there and is worshipped in that pitha.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details both the geographical seat and the internal yogic lock:

The External Shrine: She is the presiding goddess of the historical Jālandhara Pīṭha, one of the primary sacred locations of the Śākta tradition.

The Throat Lock: In internal Hatha/Kuṇḍalinī Yoga, जालन्धरबन्ध (Jālandhara-bandha) is the precise throat lock performed to contain and redirect the upward-moving vital winds. She is the internal energy awakened and stabilized during this practice.

निलयः — abode

यस्याः — of whom; whose

i. One whose abode is the Odyana pitha.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya explains this premier station within Śrīvidyā geometry:

The Central Throne: Geographically, it refers to the prominent Oḍḍiyāna sacred site. Esoterically, within the Śrī Cakra, the ओड्याणपीठ represents the highly guarded central triangle directly surrounding the Bindu. She sits inside this core sanctuary, radiating Her creative rays into the outer layers.

Nāma 380

Bhāskararāya illuminates the absolute center of meditation:

The Center of the Universe: The बिन्दु (Bindu) is the singular, mathematical point at the absolute center of the Śrī Cakra (the Sarvānandamaya Cakra). It represents the unmanifested, condensed union of Shiva and Shakti before creation explodes outward. She resides inside this point, functioning as the ultimate source of all cosmic dimensions.

Bhāskararāya strips away any external, public ostentation:

Internalized Sacrifice: रहसि (rahasi) denotes absolute interior privacy. This name refers strictly to Antaryāga—the internal, mental sacrifice where the practitioner offers their ego, thoughts, and sensory functions as oblations into the fire of pure consciousness. This is the highest form of Śrīvidyā practice, invisible to the outside world.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya continues the internal mystical methodology:

The Nectar of Absorption: The "libation" (tarpaṇa) offered here is not physical water. It represents the downpour of the nectar of immortality (amṛta) generated when the Kuṇḍalinī unites with Shiva in the crown center. Offering this supreme bliss back to the Devi is what truly satisfies Her cosmic nature.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya contrasts Her with other long, arduous paths:

Instantaneous Grace: While other disciplines require multiple lifetimes of dry, mechanical effort to yield a minor result, Her path of pure devotion and internal surrender (prapatti) is so direct that She clears the practitioner's karmic blockages and illuminates their consciousness instantly (sadyaḥ), the moment sincere connection is made.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya applies the Vedāntic concept of the uninvolved witness (Sākṣī):

The Cosmic Witness: The universe moves through cycles of creation, maintenance, and collapse. She stands as the constant, unmoving lens that witnesses all of these transitions simultaneously. She does not get entangled in the changes; She is the light that makes the perception of the universe possible.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya constructs another profound non-dual paradox by matching 384 and 385:

The Absolute Subject: While She witnesses everything (Viśvasākṣiṇī), there is absolutely no one else back behind Her to witness Her. She is the ultimate, final subjective consciousness (Draṣṭā). There is no second entity above or beyond Her to turn Her into an object, confirming Her status as the final absolute.

The Six Angas: In mantra practice, a text is consecrated across six limbs: heart (Hṛdaya), head (Śiras), crown-lock (Śikhā), armor (Kavaca), eyes (Netra), and weapon (Astra). She is Ṣaḍaṅgadevatāyuktā because Her supreme presence is perfectly protected and expressed through these six secondary guardian forces.

Bhāskararāya enumerates the six absolute attributes (Gunas) that define Lordship:

The Six Virtues: These are ऐश्वर्य (absolute sovereignty), वीर्य (unmatched potency), यशस् (infinite fame), श्री (total prosperity), ज्ञान (omniscience), and वैराग्य (complete dispassion). She contains all six in their absolute peak state, making Her the personal Lord of the cosmos.

Bhāskararāya moves this from standard imagery to specific Śrīvidyā nomenclature:

Perpetual Compassion: To be "moist" means Her heart never dries up into cold indifference. She is perpetually soft and melting with mercy for Her children.

The Nityā Goddess: It also explicitly names Her identity as नित्यक्लिन्ना, the third Nityā goddess governing the structural flow of lunar time and nectar within the Śrī Cakra.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, this states Her absolute uniqueness:

Beyond Comparison: A comparison can only occur if there are two similar things in the universe. Since She is the unique, non-dual, unmatched absolute reality (Advaya), there is absolutely nothing else in existence that can be placed next to Her as an equal or an analogy.

Bhāskararāya distinguishes Her gifts from temporary pleasures:

The Bliss of Extinction: Worldly happiness is brief and followed by fatigue. Nirvāṇa-sukha is the permanent, unshakeable bliss of the extinction of the individual ego. She is the ultimate dispenser of this final spiritual resting state.

The Sixteen Aspects of Time: In Śrīvidyā cosmology, the passage of time and lunar cycles is governed by sixteen specialized rays of energy known as the षोडश नित्याः (Ṣoḍaśa Nityāḥ), running from Kameśvarī to Citra. She is not separate from them; She is the collective matrix that embodies all sixteen phases of time.

The Owner of Splendor: She holds absolute possession over the creative rays of light. Any object, star, or intellect that exhibits illumination or brilliance is merely borrowing a fraction of Her baseline light (Prabhā).

The Most Immediate Intimacy: How is the absolute Devi "famous" or "well-known"? The Ultimate Sovereign: Lesser lords rule specific departments of matter. As Parameśvarī, She is the supreme crown ruler sitting above all primary loops of causality, governing both the physical universes and the spiritual paths with absolute independence (Svātantrya).

The Primordial Womb: मूलप्रकृति (Mūlaprakṛti) is the state where the three guṇas (sattva, rajas, tamas) exist in perfect, unmanifested equilibrium. नामानि ४०१–५००

Nāma 401

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya clarifies that Her single, uniform essence of pure consciousness appears differentiated through the mirror of matter:

The Infinite Manifestation: Since everything in the universe—from gods to elements—is a projection of Her dynamic energy (Śakti), every shape, entity, and configuration in existence is a representation of Her own body.

Beyond Monolithic Limits: This counters any view that limits the divine to a single, static appearance. She plays effortlessly through an infinity of structural variations.
