विद्याऽविद्यास्वरूपिणी — she whose form is knowledge and ignorance

Meaning

i. One who is in the form of knowledge and ignorance.

ii. Vidya leads to liberation, while avidya is the basis of bondage and manifestation. Both function within her power and are forms of her cosmic play.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details a profound, non-dual reconciliation of cosmic forces:

The Power of Liberation: As विद्या (Vidyā), She is the spiritual insight that turns the mind inward, dissolves the ego, and reveals the absolute identity of the Self (Mokṣa-pradā).

The Power of Bondage: As अविद्या (Avidyā), She operates as the cosmic obscuration that project differences, enabling the relative play of the world. Bhāskararāya notes that both are functional shifts of the same singular divine matrix, keeping the cosmic rhythm intact.

Nāma 403

महाकामेशनयनकुमुदाह्लादकौमुदी

Samāsa-vigraha

महाकामेशस्य नयने एव कुमुदे। तयोः आह्लादे कौमुदी इव।

Word by word

महाकामेशस्य — of Mahakamesha

नयने — eyes

कुमुदे — water-lilies

आह्लादे — in delighting

कौमुदी — moonlight

महाकामेशनयनकुमुदाह्लादकौमुदी — she who is moonlight delighting the water-lily eyes of Mahakamesha

Meaning

i. One who is like moonlight that delights the lily-like eyes of Mahakamesha.

ii. The eyes of Mahakamesha are compared to kumuda flowers, which bloom in moonlight. Sreedevee is the moonlight that gives delight to those eyes.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya highlights the intimate, non-dual delight of the absolute couple:

The Radiance of Delight: The night-lotus (kumuda) opens only when struck by the cool rays of the moon. When Mahākāmeśvara looks upon Her supreme beauty, His eyes swell with immediate spiritual ecstasy. She is the source of that bliss, anchoring the baseline union of consciousness and energy.

Nāma 404

भक्तहार्दतमोभेदभानुमद्भानुसंततिः

Samāsa-vigraha

भक्तानां हृदि भावनी यानि तमांसि तेषां भेदे भानुमतः भानुसंततिः।

Word by word

भक्तानाम् — of devotees

हार्द — in the heart

तमः — darkness

भेद — breaking; removing

भानुमत् — sun-like

भानुसंततिः — stream of rays

भक्तहार्दतमोभेदभानुमद्भानुसंततिः — she who is a stream of sun-rays removing the darkness in devotees’ hearts

Meaning

i. One who removes the darkness in the hearts of devotees like the rays of the sun.

ii. The darkness in the heart is ignorance and sorrow. Her grace shines like sunlight and dispels that inner darkness.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya treats this as a formula for the removal of spiritual distress:

The Solar Dispersion: The deep-seated ignorance (avidyā) and accumulated mental impressions (vāsanās) are like pitch darkness inside the heart cavity. Sincere concentration on Her works like a high-noon sun, vaporizing those dense blocks instantly and replacing them with clear light.

Nāma 405

शिवदूती

Samāsa-vigraha

शिवः दूतः यस्याः सा।

शिवस्य दूती।

Word by word

शिवः — Shiva

दूतः — messenger

यस्याः — of whom; whose

शिवदूती — she for whom Shiva is messenger; or the messenger of Shiva

Meaning

i. One whose messenger is Shiva, or who is the messenger of Shiva.

ii. The name recalls the form in which Shiva himself acts as her messenger. It also indicates her inseparable relation with Shiva.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya connects this name directly to the core texts of the Devī Māhātmya:

The Ultimate Sovereign: During the cosmic battle against the demonic forces (specifically Śumbha and Niśumbha), She sent Lord Śiva Himself as Her official emissary to issue the final ultimatum. This demonstrates Her immense absolute authority over even the highest tier of the trinity.

Nāma 406

शिवाराध्या

Samāsa-vigraha

शिवेन आराध्या।

Word by word

शिवेन — by Shiva

आराध्या — worshipped; adored

शिवाराध्या — she who is worshipped by Shiva

Meaning

i. One who is worshipped by Shiva.

ii. Even Shiva worships her. This establishes her supreme status as the power of Shiva himself.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya highlights the profound, reciprocal adoration between the two poles of reality:

The Contemplation of Consciousness: Śiva is the static, pure witness consciousness. To experience His own creative power and bliss, He must contemplate and worship Her—the dynamic energy (Śakti). This confirms that She is the ultimate object of adoration even for the lord of ascetics.

Nāma 407

शिवमूर्तिः

Samāsa-vigraha

शिवः एव मूर्तिः यस्याः सा।

Word by word

शिवः — Shiva; auspiciousness

एव — itself

मूर्तिः — form

यस्याः — of whom; whose

शिवमूर्तिः — she whose form is Shiva

Meaning

i. One whose form is Shiva.

ii. She is not different from Shiva. Her form is auspiciousness itself and is identical with Shiva-consciousness.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya removes any remaining concept of separation between the two:

Non-Dual Identity: Lest a practitioner think that Śiva and Śakti are separate entities competing for status, this name states that Her very body is Śiva. They are the structural twin aspects of a single, indivisible absolute, like the word and its meaning.

Nāma 408

शिवङ्करी

Samāsa-vigraha

शिवं करोतीति।

Word by word

शिवम् — auspiciousness; welfare

करोति — makes; does

शिवङ्करी — she who causes auspiciousness

Meaning

i. One who does good and makes all auspicious.

ii. She confers welfare and auspiciousness on devotees and turns life toward the good.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya defines Śivam as the highest welfare:

The Dispenser of Peace: She transforms the chaotic, turbulent life of the practitioner into a state of deep, tranquil harmony. By dissolving negative karmic tendencies, She naturally generates peace, ultimately converting the individual soul into the status of Śiva Himself.

Nāma 409

शिवप्रिया

Samāsa-vigraha

शिवस्य प्रिया।

शिवः प्रियः यस्याः सा।

Word by word

शिवस्य — of Shiva

प्रिया — beloved

शिवः — Shiva

प्रियः — dear

शिवप्रिया — beloved of Shiva; she to whom Shiva is dear

Meaning

i. One who is dear to Shiva.

ii. She is beloved of Shiva, and Shiva is dear to her. The name expresses the mutual unity and love of Shiva and Shakti.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya explores this mutual, cosmic love:

The Inseparable Bond: She is the eternal consort of Śiva. This intense love signifies that energy cannot exist without a consciousness background, and consciousness cannot manifest without energy. Their deep mutual attraction holds the structure of the cosmos together.

Nāma 410

शिवपरा

Samāsa-vigraha

शिवः एव परः यस्याः सा।

Word by word

शिवः — Shiva

एव — alone

परः — supreme goal

यस्याः — of whom; whose

शिवपरा — she whose supreme object is Shiva

Meaning

i. One for whom Shiva is the supreme.

ii. She is established in Shiva as the supreme reality. The name also shows her non-difference from Shiva.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya defines this through the lens of absolute devotion to the source:

Perpetual Orientation: As the active, kinetic power, Her entire operational intent is to lead everything back into the peaceful, unmoving baseline of static consciousness (Śiva). She remains completely absorbed in Him, demonstrating the model of perfect internal surrender.

Nāma 411

शिष्टेष्टा

Samāsa-vigraha

शिष्टैः इष्टा।

शिष्टानि इष्टानि यस्याः सा।

शिष्टानाम् इष्टा।

शिष्टाः इष्टाः यस्याः सा।

Word by word

शिष्टैः — by the cultured and righteous

इष्टा — loved; worshipped; desired

शिष्टानाम् — of the noble

शिष्टेष्टा — she who is loved and worshipped by the noble

Meaning

i. One who is loved and worshipped by the noble and cultured.

ii. Shishta means the righteous, learned and disciplined. She is their chosen deity and object of worship.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the criteria for true alignment with Her:

The Adoration of the Wise: शिष्ट refers to those who strictly follow the structural disciplines of scripture and possess refined, clean intellects. She is the ultimate object of their desire. Concurrently, She holds these virtuous seekers exceptionally dear, protecting their spiritual progress.

Nāma 412

शिष्टपूजिता

Samāsa-vigraha

शिष्टैः पूजिता।

Word by word

शिष्टैः — by the noble; by the disciplined

पूजिता — worshipped

शिष्टपूजिता — worshipped by the noble

Meaning

i. One who is worshipped by noble persons.

ii. The shishtas, those who follow right knowledge and conduct, worship her.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya reinforces the validity of traditional lineages:

The Validated Path: This title emphasizes that Her worship is not an eccentric or lawless practice. The greatest seers, masters of grammar, and realized souls of history have systematically adored Her, confirming that Her path is grounded in absolute truth and moral rectitude.

Nāma 413

अप्रमेया

Samāsa-vigraha

न प्रमेया।

Word by word

न — not

प्रमेया — measurable; knowable as an object of proof

अप्रमेया — immeasurable; not an object of limited knowledge

Meaning

i. One who is immeasurable.

ii. She cannot be measured by the ordinary means of knowledge. Being the very basis of knowledge, she cannot be known as a limited object.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya applies a fundamental rule of epistemology (pramāṇa-śāstra):

Beyond Logic and Proof: An object is understood when it is measured by instruments of knowledge like perception, inference, or logic (pramāṇa). But because She is the foundational subjective consciousness that animates those very instruments, She can never be turned into an external object of proof. She is the knower, never the known.

Nāma 414

स्वप्रकाशा

Samāsa-vigraha

स्वः प्रकाशः यस्याः सा।

Word by word

स्वः — self; own

प्रकाशः — light; illumination

यस्याः — of whom; whose

स्वप्रकाशा — self-luminous one

Meaning

i. One who is self-luminous.

ii. She shines by herself and does not need another light to reveal her. As consciousness, she reveals all things and is self-revealed.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya sets this up as the resolution to the preceding name:

Independent Light: If She cannot be known by ordinary proofs (Aprameyā), does She remain in total darkness? No. She is Svaprakāśā—She requires no external lamp, intellect, or text to illuminate Her. Just as the sun is seen by its own light, She is realized through Her own self-revealing presence.

Nāma 415

मनोवाचामगोचरा

Samāsa-vigraha

मनांसि च वाचश्च तेषां तासां च अगोचरा।

Word by word

मनांसि — minds.

वाचः — words, speech.

तेषाम् / तासाम् — of them.

अगोचरा — beyond the field or range of perception.

मनोवाचामगोचरा — She who is beyond the range of mind and speech.

Meaning

(i) One who is beyond the range of mind and speech.

(ii) That is, She is not comprehensible by mind and speech. Sruti also, in the Taittiriya Upanishad (II-9-2), says: from whence speech and mind turn away unable to reach — Yato Vacho Nivartante Aprapya Manasa Saha.

(iii) In Vishnu Purana, Prahlada says, “I bow down to the supreme Ishvaree who transcends speech and mind and who can be grasped by the wisdom of the wise alone.”

(iv) She is one in whom no object of thought or speech is to be found.

(v) By mentioning mind and speech, all the eleven organs and Para, etc., speeches are indicated.

(vi) These organs have their own ways of understanding objects. Only if the objects to be understood are within some limits can these organs recognise them. But whatever Sreedevee has is limitless, boundless and infinite. Hence She does not have anything which mind and other organs can recognise.

(vii) When read with the previous name, ‘A’ is to be prefixed to this name. Then it can be split as Amano + Vachma + Gochara. That is, She is beyond the reach of those whose mind and speech are immature. Alternatively, She can be reached only by those whose mind and speech are mature.

(viii) Kathopanishad says that by mind alone it should be perceived. This contradiction is removed in the Bhamati by adding “immature and mature” or “not purified and purified” respectively to the word “mind”.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya evokes the definitive Taittirīya Upaniṣad text ("यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते अप्राप्य मनसा सह"):

Transcendence of Conceptions: Ordinary words fail to describe Her, and the finite human mind cracks when trying to compute Her absolute immensity. She cannot be captured by verbal definitions or mental concepts, remaining as the transcendent witness behind them.

Nāma 416

चिच्छक्तिः

Samāsa-vigraha

चित्शक्तिः।

Word by word

चित् — consciousness, knowledge.

शक्तिः — power, energy.

चिच्छक्तिः — the power of consciousness.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of energy called Chit.

(ii) Chitshakti, the power of removing ignorance, is also termed chaitanya. Since Sreedevee is in the form of knowledge, She got this name.

(iii) According to the Svetasvatara Upanishad (V-1), in the imperishable and infinite highest universal absolute, wherein vidya and avidya are hidden, one is imperishable and the other is perishable; She who rules these two is different from either.

(iv) In Devee Bhagavatam it is said that in all beings there is shakti with all its powers. Any being devoid of that shakti becomes like a corpse. That Chit-Shakti is in all beings; that is Her form.

(v) Chit, according to Yaska, means comparison. Panini also uses it in this sense. This method describes an unknown object by comparing it with a known object. The knowledge of comparison is Sreedevee Herself.

(vi) In Saptashatee we read: Chitiroopena Ya Krutsnam Etad Vyapya Sthita Jagat.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya outlines the primary engine of creation:

The Kinetic Consciousness: She is not a blind, unconscious energy matter (prakṛti). She is the supreme dynamic power operating in absolute synchronization with pure awareness. She is the capacity of Brahman to know, experience, and manifest realities without losing its baseline purity.

Nāma 417

चेतनारूपा

Samāsa-vigraha

चेतना रूपं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

चेतना — consciousness, sentience, inner awareness.

रूपम् — form.

यस्याः सा — whose; she whose.

चेतनारूपा — She whose form is consciousness.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of consciousness, chaitanya.

(ii) The chetana energy in all beings is Sreedevee only. In Saptashatee this has been prayed as Chetana. Chetana means inner sense. Only because of this can we recognise the objects shown by eye, ear and mind. Only through its action can we recognise its availability, not by any other means.

(iii) Kenopanishad says: Srotrasya Srotram Manaso Mano.

(iv) Samkshepa Sareerakam says that the pure chit shakti of the supreme lord is called chaitanya.

(v) In Gaudapada’s Sree Vidya Ratna Sutra also it is mentioned that Shakti is chaitanya itself.

(vi) The first verse of Devee Bhagavatam says that we meditate upon that Primeval Vidya which is the chaitanya of all and which guides our senses.

(vii) In the Taittiriya Upanishad commentary tradition, the letter ‘Sa’ is explained as being in the form of Chitshakti.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya tracks Her presence across all living organisms:

The Animating Pulse: Cetanā is the visible spark of life and intelligence that differentiates a living body from a dead corpse. She is that very pulse of vitality. Every thought, movement, and perception occurring in any biological form is Her direct physical signature.

Nāma 418

जडशक्तिः

Samāsa-vigraha

जडाशक्तिः।

Word by word

जडा — inert, insentient, mechanical.

शक्तिः — power, energy.

जडशक्तिः — the power operating in inert creation.

Meaning

(i) One who manifests as the mechanical forces of the inanimate creation.

(ii) A certain modification of maya, correlative to the power which creates the animate world, simply denotes the creative energy.

(iii) The Vishnu Purana says that the energies of all beings are not grasped by our intellects. The creative energies of Brahman are a hundred times more difficult to grasp; they are in Him as heat is in fire. Brahman is only the instrumental cause of the creation of the world. The creative energies are the material cause. Except for the instrumental cause, the creative energies depend on nothing. An object becomes itself by its own energy.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya introduces a key philosophical transition to prevent cosmic exclusion:

The Matrix of Matter: Lest a practitioner think that the material, unconscious elements of the universe (like rocks, elements, and mechanical forces) belong to an evil or separate category, this name states She is Jaḍaśakti. She assumes the form of inert matter to build the physical staging ground of the cosmos.

Nāma 419

जडात्मिका

Samāsa-vigraha

जडं दृश्यमत्रम् आत्मा यस्याः मायायाः सा।

Word by word

जडम् — inert, insentient.

दृश्यमात्रम् — mere visible object, object of perception.

आत्मा — inner essence, nature.

माया — maya.

जडात्मिका — She who is the inner essence of inert manifestation.

Meaning

(i) One who is the innermost essence of all mechanical forces.

(ii) It has been mentioned above that this static universe is the specialty of cosmic manifestation.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya clarifies Her identity with the objective world:

The Object Universe: जड refers to the entire grid of dṛśya (the seen/perceivable objects). She embodies this dense, material layer through Her power of Māyā. She is the substance out of which the objective, tangible landscape of creation is spun.

Nāma 420

गायत्री

Samāsa-vigraha

छन्दसां चतुर्विंशत्यक्षरं गायत्री।

गायन्तं त्रायते यस्मादिति।

गायनाद् गमनाद् वा।

गायति च त्रायते च।

गायनात्मत्वात्।

गोपकन्या ब्रह्मणः कनिष्ठपत्नी।

Word by word

छन्दसाम् — among metres.

चतुर्विंशत्यक्षरम् — having twenty-four syllables.

गायन्तम् — the one who sings or recites.

त्रायते — protects.

गायनात् — from singing.

गमनात् — from going or movement.

गायति — sings.

त्रायते — protects.

गोपकन्या — daughter of a cowherd / guardian of Veda.

ब्रह्मणः कनिष्ठपत्नी — the junior wife of Brahma.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of Gayatree.

(ii) Veda says, Gayatreem Chandasam Mata: Gayatree mantra is the mother of all mantras. The Gayatree metre has 24 characters. In Sreemad Bhagavat Geeta (X-35), Lord Sreekrishna says: Gayatree Chandasam Aham. In Koorma Purana also the same is conveyed.

(iii) According to Padma Purana, Gayatree is a daughter of a shepherd and a junior wife of Brahma. When Brahma was performing a sacrificial fire, he called his wife Savitri. As she delayed, Brahma brought a daughter of a shepherd from Shakti and, with Vishnu’s consent, married her by the Gandharva method. For the word Gopakanya, Go has several meanings; one of them is Veda, and those who guard Veda are Gopas.

(iv) Gayatree protects those who recite her mantra. Gayatree Kalpa says: Gayantam Trayate Yasmat Gayatree Tena Gadyate. Other reasons are also given: Devee Purana says that Devas worship Gayatree by singing and hearing; Chhandogya Upanishad says Gayatree Cha Trayate Cha; Mahavashishta Ramayana says that because She is in the form of songs, She is called Gayatree.

(v) Padma Purana says that Sreedevee is in the form of Gayatree.

(vi) The ordinarily recited Gayatree mantra has three groups and the complete Gayatree mantra has four. The first three are said to be capsule forms of Rig, Yajur and Sama Vedas; the fourth is a gist of Atharvana Veda. It is said that Sree Bhaskara Raya also had Upanayana again and learnt Atharvana Veda.

(vii) It is well known that Sreemad Ramayana includes Gayatree mantra and that 24 verses are read as Gayatree Ramayana.

(viii) Tripura Tapini Upanishad advises that Panchadasi mantra has the meaning of Gayatree mantra in every group. This has also been explained by Sree Bhaskara Raya.

(ix) In Mahashodha Nyasa, it has been mentioned that She is in the form of three Gunas.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya unpacks the absolute premier status of this identity:

The Mother of Mantras: She is non-different from the sacred Gāyatrī Mantra, the foundational core of Vedic revelation. Bhāskararāya details the semantic root: गायन्तं त्रायते — She extends an immediate shield of spiritual protection over any seeker who sings or chants Her name, transforming their intellect into pure light.

Nāma 421

व्याहृतिः

Samāsa-vigraha

उच्चारणरूपा।

मन्त्रविशेषणरूपा।

Word by word

उच्चारण — utterance, pronunciation.

रूपा — form.

मन्त्रविशेषण — qualifying or special mantra-expression.

व्याहृतिः — sacred utterance/invocation.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of Vyahrutis, invocations.

(ii) Some special mantras are called Vyahrutis. Before creating this world, Brahma chanted the Pranava mantra Om by joining the first letters of the three Vedas, A, U and M. Then he chanted Bhooh, Bhuvah and Suvah and created the world. It expanded to the words Mahah, Janah, Tapah and Satyam and as seven worlds. Hence the Pranava and the names of these seven worlds are called Vyahrutis. She is in this form.

(iii) According to Vayu Purana, She is in the form of Vyaharanam, that is pronunciation. “You were addressed by me and hence you approached me. Hence you are the Vyahruti.”

(iv) It can be said that this and the next two names respectively indicate the waking, dream and deep sleep states.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya connects this directly to the structural framework of Vedic ritual:

The Sacred Utterance: व्याहृति (Vyāhṛti) refers specifically to the cosmic prefixes—भूः, भुवः, स्वः (Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ)—that anchor and unlock the Gāyatrī Mantra. She is the phonic reality of these syllables, representing the three foundational worlds of experience projected by Her sound.

Nāma 422

संध्या

Samāsa-vigraha

सम्यग् ध्यायन्ति अस्याम्।

सम्यग्ध्येयत्वात्।

Word by word

सम्यक् — properly, completely.

ध्यायन्ति — they meditate.

अस्याम् — in her, upon her.

ध्येयत्वात् — because she is fit to be meditated upon.

संध्या — Sandhya, junction, twilight meditation.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of Sandhya Devee, the deity of twilight.

(ii) Sandhya means sound meditation. She is worshipped with the idea of the non-separation of ourselves.

(iii) Sandhya means junction, the time of night and day, or meditation. The meeting of day and night occurs in the morning and evening; similar junctions occur at noon and midnight also. These junctions are worshipped by Brahmins with the integrated thought of chaitanya in the Sun. That kind of worship is the real meaning of Sandhya. In that way, worshipped Gayatree and Brahman are one and the same.

Madhava says that this word indicates the Devee to be worshipped during the junction of day and night.

Note: As per Tantra Sastras, during Sandhya period arghya has to be given aiming at the mainly worshipped deities, after the Vedic Sandhyavandanam. In this fashion, Sreevidyopasakas give arghya in all four Sandhyas. This is called Sree Vidya Sandhyavandanam according to Sakta Tantra Sastra.

(iv) Sandhya is the mind-born daughter of Brahma. When Brahma was meditating, a beautiful girl originated and was called Sandhya. She did penance and, by giving up her body, became Arundhati, wife of sage Vasishta.

(v) In Renuka Purana it is said that the three pulses Ida, Pingala and Susumna are integrated in the body. Similarly Sandhya is an integrated form of the three Devis Mahakalee, Mahalakshmee and Ekaveera.

(vi) According to Dhoumya, a one-year-old girl is called Sandhya. Sreedevee is in that form also.

(vii) The three names Vyahruti, Sandhya and Dvija Brunda Nishevita respectively indicate the awakened, dream and deep sleep states.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details both the ritual hour and the internal yogic junction:

The Hour of Union: Saṁdhyā represents the transitional junctions of the day (dawn, noon, and dusk) where the mind naturally settles into quietude.

The Internal Junction: In the subtle body, She is the junction point where the dual flows of Iḍā and Piṅgalā dissolve into the central Suṣumṇā, marking the state of absolute meditative absorption.

Nāma 423

द्विजवृन्दनिषेविता

Samāsa-vigraha

द्विजानां वृन्दम्। तैः निषेविता उपास्या।

Word by word

द्विजानाम् — of the twice-born.

वृन्दम् — group, assembly.

तैः — by them.

निषेविता — served, worshipped.

उपास्या — to be worshipped.

Meaning

(i) One who is well worshipped by groups of the twice born.

(ii) She has been well meditated upon by all the twice born: Brahmins, Kshatriyas and Vyasyas. One birth is from the mother and the other is during Upanayanam to understand Gayatree mantra.

(iii) She is so worshipped because She is Sandhya. The Renuka Purana says that this Sandhya is to be worshipped by Devas, by the twice born and by great souls, in sitting down, lying down, moving about and eating, and that She is Renuka Herself.

A Brahmin who does not worship Sandhya is no more a Brahmin. He is unfit to do any other religious actions. Sastra says that even if he does any actions, they will be fruitless. The importance of worshipping Gayatree has been described in detail in Devee Bhagavatam.

(iv) It can be said that the three names Vyahruti, Sandhya and Dvija Brunda Nishevita respectively indicate waking, dream and deep sleep states. Vyahruti is the operation of speech and indicates waking. Sandhya, being between the two, indicates dream. Dvija also means birds; birds fly in the sky and return to their nests, just as tired jivas, quitting waking and dream states, are absorbed in the supreme Brahman in deep sleep.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya clarifies the functional meaning of Dvija:

The Double Birth: Dvija means twice-born—first biologically from the mother's womb, and second spiritually through the reception of the Gāyatrī and Agamic initiation. She is the central deity sought after by all those who have dedicated their corporate lives to the maintenance of scriptural order and daily contemplative practices.

Nāma 424

(i) One who has a seat constituted by the Cosmic Elements, the 36 tatvas.

The details can be seen in Sreemad Bhagavatam. Saiva Sastras and Sakta Sastras unanimously accept that there are 36 tatvas from Shiva till Prithvee. She has these 36 tatvas as Her yoga seat.

(iii) One other meaning is that She pushes out the tatvas, i.e. She is beyond all these tatvas. For the 906th name Tatvadhika it has been interpreted that She continues even when these tatvas are destroyed.

Bhāskararāya maps this across the complete taxonomy of the Agamas:

The Throne of Thirty-Six Principles: In the Śākta/Śaiva systems, reality is stratified into thirty-six progressive principles (tattvas), running from the grossest element earth (pṛthivī) up to pure Śiva-tattva. She sits on top of this entire evolutionary ladder, controlling it as its sovereign source and ruler.

The Direct Designation: In Vedic syntax, तत् (Tat) points directly to the unmanifested, omnipresent, transcendent cause of the universe. By declaring Her name to be Tat, the text removes any anthropomorphic limitations, confirming Her identity as the absolute, non-dual Brahman beyond time and space.

(ii) In the 36 tatvas mentioned above, the Shiva tatva is called Para Samvit. This is the Supreme Being without any quality or blemish. Hence, the Shiva Tatva without any dispositions and the Shakti Tatva, the cause of the dispositions on account of creation, are one and the same in the Para Samvit. Hence when Sreedevee is in the form of Parabrahmam, She is referred to as Prakasha Vimarsha Samarasya Roopinee. Kameshwaree is in the form of brightness. This form of knowledge is integrated with Aham, Idam, Etat and Tat.

(vi) Since it is said as Tatvamayee later in the 907th name, these 425th, 426th and 427th names are split into Tat, Tvam and Ayee.

(vii) In usage of namavali, this name appears as Tubhyam Nama.

The Immediate Presence: If She were only Tat ("That"), She might seem like a cold, distant galactic absolute. Therefore, the text immediately names Her त्वम् ("Thou"). She is the immediate, close, internal reality residing inside the seeker as their own subjective spark of life, completing the equation of realization.

पञ्चकोशांतरस्थिता

Samāsa-vigraha

Meaning

(i) One who dwells amidst the five koshas, the psychological sheaths of the personality.

(ii) In Navavarna Pooja, after the ninth avarana above the bindu, Pancha Panchika Pooja is performed by imagining five thrones. These five Panchikas are respectively the five Lakshmis, five sheaths, five kalpalatas, five kamadhenus, and five gems. The five sheaths are named Sree Vidya, Paramjyoti, Paranishkala Shambhavi, Ajapadanda, and Matruka. These details are available in Jnanarnava Tantra.

(iii) Sree Vidya sheath is worshipped in the bindu. The other four are worshipped outside, differentiating the individual and the combined forms. Since Sree Vidya sheath is worshipped in the bindu amidst these four, this name is given to Sreedevee.

(iv) The results of these five Panchika Poojas are explained in detail in Saparya Paddhati Vasana by Sree Chidananda Natha. He explains the five positions as Samyam, Layam, Vinasham, Adyantabhavam, and Aikyam, corresponding to the five Panchikas.

(v) It has also been said that there are five sheaths in the body: Annamaya, Pranamaya, Manomaya, Vijnanamaya, and Anandamaya. Each is covered by the previous one. Sreedevee is in the integral form with Brahmam as the Anandamaya sheath.

(vi) Sree Adi Sankara states that Anandamaya is not itself the universal absolute Brahmam, but is to be understood as different from Brahmam. Based on this view, the name means that She is in the midst of the five sheaths: Brahmam is beyond Anandamaya, completing it, witnessing all actions, and being of the nature of truth and knowledge.

(vii) Brahma Geeta and the tradition of Durvasa also describe Sreedevee as the supreme light known through the five sheaths.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya aligns this with the psycho-spiritual anatomy detailed in the Taittirīya Upaniṣad:

The Hidden Jewel: The individual soul is covered by five dense layers: Annamaya (food/physical), Prāṇamaya (vital energy), Manomaya (mind/emotion), Vijñānamaya (intellect/discernment), and Ānandamaya (causal bliss). She sits at the absolute center of these five layers as the ultimate, unblemished core—the Ātman.

Bhāskararāya provides the grand capstone identification that seals the entire six-chakra structural layout:

The Master Śakti of the Crown: She explicitly identifies Herself here as याकिणी (Yākiṇī), the absolute, high-level administrative Śakti placed in charge of the supreme Sahasrāra matrix. This name triumphantly concludes the deep internal anatomical tour running from Nāma 475 to 533, anchoring the complete subtle layout directly to Her non-dual person.

Nāma 535

स्वाहा

Samāsa-vigraha

स्वाहार्थरूपा।

सुष्ठु आहूयते अनया इति।

स्वान् आजिहीते (स्वीयत्वेन सम्यग्जानाति) इति।

Word by word

स्वाहार्थरूपा — having the form of the meaning of Svaha.

सुष्ठु — well, properly.

आहूयते — is invoked.

अनया — by this.

इति — thus.

स्वान् — one’s own.

आजिहीते — calls, brings near.

स्वीयत्वेन — as one’s own.

सम्यग्जानाति — knows properly.

स्वाहा — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of Svaha, the sacred exclamation with which oblations are made in the sacrificial fire for gods.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details Her function within the fire sacrifice (Homa):

The Consumer of Oblations: She is the phonic reality of the mantra स्वाहा (Svāhā). Without Her presence, no offering dropped into the physical sacrificial fire can reach the Devas. She acts as the dynamic alchemical bridge that transforms material oblations into subtle cosmic energy.

Nāma 536

स्वधा

Samāsa-vigraha

सुष्ठु आधीयते अनया इति।

सुष्ठु अं (विष्णुं स्वान् वा) दधातीति।

सुष्ठु — well, properly.

आधीयते — is placed or offered.

अनया — by this.

इति — thus.

अं — the syllable/being indicated by am.

विष्णुं — Vishnu.

स्वान् — one’s own.

वा — or.

दधातीति — holds, sustains.

स्वधा — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of Svadha.

(ii) The words Svaha and Svadha are used when oblations are offered: Svaha for the gods in the sacrificial fire and Svadha for the Pitrs, the ancestors. Devee Bhagavatam also states this distinction.

(iii) These names also indicate that She is in the form of the Devis represented by Svaha and Svadha.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya coordinates Her function within the ancestral rites (Tarpaṇa):

Sustenance of the Ancestors: She is the phonic power of the mantra स्वधा (Svadhā), which unlocks the channel to the ancestral planes (Pitrū-loka). She ensures the transmission of offerings to nourish the departed roots of the family line, holding ancestral order in equilibrium.

Nāma 537

Samāsa-vigraha

अविद्या।

[अल्पार्थे नञ् इत्यनेन] वृत्त्यात्मकविद्यारूपा।

अविद्यापूर्वा प्राथमिकी (विद्यापूर्वा च क्रमप्राप्ता) सृष्टिरूपा।

Word by word

अविद्या — ignorance.

अल्पार्थे — in a minor/secondary sense.

नञ् — the negative particle nañ.

इत्यनेन — by this.

वृत्त्यात्मकविद्यारूपा — a form of knowledge as mental modification.

अविद्यापूर्वा — preceded by avidya.

प्राथमिकी — primary, initial.

विद्यापूर्वा — preceded by vidya.

च — and.

क्रमप्राप्ता — arrived in sequence.

सृष्टिरूपा — in the form of creation.

अमतिः — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of ignorance or non-understanding, and also as the primordial movement connected with creation.

(ii) Amati is explained as avidya. It may also indicate a form of knowledge functioning through mental modifications, according to the grammatical and interpretive explanations.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya navigates a deep non-dual philosophical transition:

The Screen of Unconsciousness: As Amati, She represents the temporary suspension of active intellectual modifications—either as the baseline cosmic sleep before creation, or as the state of Avidyā that allows the relative world to appear separate. It confirms that even the absence of active intellect is a corner of Her power.

Nāma 538

मेधा

Samāsa-vigraha

विदिताखिलवेदसारा।

धीर्धारणवती बुद्धिविशेषरूपा।

Word by word

विदिताखिलवेदसारा — one who knows the essence of all the Vedas.

धीर्धारणवती — intelligence that retains.

बुद्धिविशेषरूपा — in the form of a special intellect.

मेधा — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of Medha, retentive intelligence.

(ii) Medha is the power that grasps and retains the essence of all the Vedas.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya defines this refined cognitive faculty:

The Power of Spiritual Retention: Medhā is not simple data memory. It is the highly specialized capacity of the intellect (buddhi) to grasp, hold, and integrate the deepest essence of scriptural truth without forgetting or distorting it. She is that internal steel trap that preserves self-knowledge inside the seeker.

Nāma 539

श्रुतिः

Samāsa-vigraha

वेदरूपा।

Word by word

वेदरूपा — in the form of the Veda.

श्रुतिः — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of the Vedas.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya anchors Her identity with the highest scriptural authority:

The Living Revelation: She is the absolute phonic framework of the श्रुति (Śruti — the four eternal Vedas). They are not human books; they are the uncorrupted sound waves of truth heard by ancient rishis in deep absorption. She is the substance, code, and voice of this baseline divine revelation.

Nāma 540

स्मृतिः

Samāsa-vigraha

स्मरते सर्वकार्याणीति।

Word by word

स्मरते — remembers.

सर्वकार्याणीति — all actions.

स्मृतिः — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of Smritis.

(ii) Sruti means hearing and Smriti means recollection. She is in the form of knowledge obtained through both.

(iii) It is mentioned in many places that the Vedas and Smritis, such as those of Manu, are Her form. Saptashatee and Koorma Purana also convey that the Vedas are the inherent form of Brahmam and the eternal Shakti.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the execution of cosmic and practical law:

The Structural Memory: She is the power of memory (Smṛti) that keeps the laws of human conduct and cosmic history intact. Concurrently, She manifests as the authoritative Smṛti texts (like Manu or Yājñavalkya) that translate the high revelations of the Śruti into practical ethical systems for society.

Nāma 541

अनुत्तमा

Samāsa-vigraha

यदपेक्षयोत्तममन्यद्वस्तु नास्ति सा।

Word by word

यदपेक्षयोत्तममन्यद्वस्तु — a thing superior in comparison with whom.

परप्रेरिता — impelled by another.

मा — measure, knowledge, or power.

बुद्धिरैश्वर्यं — intellect or lordship.

वा — or.

यस्या — whose.

अनुत्तमा — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who has none superior to Her.

(ii) There is nothing higher than Her. She is not dependent on praise, external prompting, or any other authority.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya confirms Her absolute position at the peak of reality:

The Unsurpassed Absolute: If any entity existed above Her, Her sovereignty would be secondary. She is Anuttamā because She stands as the definitive ceiling of existence. There is no higher reality, no superior consciousness, and no master back behind Her station.

Nāma 542

पुण्यकीर्तिः

Samāsa-vigraha

पुण्यप्रदा — bestower of merit.

कीर्तिर्यस्याः — whose fame.

सा — she.

पुण्यकीर्तिः — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One whose fame is holy and meritorious.

(ii) Her praise itself is auspicious and bestows merit.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya details the physics of Her renown:

The Purifying Renown: Ordinary fame feeds vanity. Her fame is Puṇya—it carries a tangible energetic frequency. By simply listening to, repeating, or celebrating Her historical and cosmic triumphs, the heavy karmic impurities inside the listener's mind are dissolved, replaced by automatic merit.

Nāma 543

पुण्यलभ्या

Samāsa-vigraha

पुण्यैः लभ्या।

Word by word

पुण्यैः — through merit.

लभ्या — attainable.

पुण्यलभ्या — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who can be attained only through virtue and righteousness.

(ii) Punya means good actions performed in previous births. Only through such punya can Her blessings be attained.

(iii) Devee Bhagavatam says that only those righteous ascetics devoted to wisdom see the beneficent Devee; men of desire do not. Sree Adi Sankara also conveys the same idea in his commentary on the first verse of Soundaryalahari.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya clarifies the transactional alignment of spiritual access:

The Currency of Merit: She cannot be purchased with money, captured by aggressive egoic intellect, or reached by deceptive minds. The only operational currency that unlocks Her gate is Puṇya—the slow, steady accumulation of virtuous deeds, mental purity, and selfless alignment with dharma over lifetimes.

Nāma 544

पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तना

Samāsa-vigraha

पुण्ये विहितकर्मरूपे श्रवणकीर्तने यस्याः सा।

Word by word

पुण्ये — in merit.

विहितकर्मरूपे — in the form of prescribed action.

श्रवणकीर्तने — hearing and chanting.

यस्याः — whose.

सा — she.

पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तना — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One whose hearing and chanting are meritorious.

(ii) Listening to and reciting Her names are themselves holy acts.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya re-emphasizes the ease of access built into Her path:

The Sonic Purification: One does not need to master complex yoga posture loops or live in isolated caves to start the alignment. By simply using the ears to hear Her text (śravaṇa) and the tongue to recite Her syllables (kīrtana), the practitioner's internal environment is realigned with cosmic order.

Nāma 545

पुलोमजार्चिता

Samāsa-vigraha

पुलोमतो जातया (इन्द्राण्या) अर्चिता

Word by word

पुलोमतो — from Puloma.

जातया — born of.

इन्द्राण्या — by Indrani.

अर्चिता — worshipped.

पुलोमजार्चिता — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is worshipped by Pulomaja, Indrani, the daughter of Puloma.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya highlights Her adoration across the highest levels of celestial sovereignty:

The Worship of the Heavenly Queen: Indrāṇī, the empress of the gods, adores Her to maintain the stability of the heavenly throne. It demonstrates that even those who have attained the absolute peak of celestial pleasure and position must bow before Her to hold their office securely.

Nāma 546

बन्धमोचनी

Samāsa-vigraha

बन्धं मोचयतीति।

Word by word

बन्धं — bondage.

मोचयतीति — releases.

बन्धमोचनी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who releases beings from bondage.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya targets the ultimate human problem:

The Cutter of the Karmic Tether: बन्ध (bandha) is the structural imprisonment of the individual soul inside the cycle of birth and death, forged by ego, attachment, and the illusion of separation. As Bandhamocanī, She snaps these chains cleanly, granting immediate spiritual liberation (Mokṣa).

Nāma 547

बन्धुरालका बर्बरालका

Samāsa-vigraha

बन्धुरा बर्बरा अलकाः यस्याः सा।

बन्धुरा — beautiful.

बर्बरा — curly.

अलकाः — locks of hair.

यस्याः — whose.

सा — she.

बन्धुरालका बर्बरालका — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who has charming, curly tresses.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya moves from the poetic physical decoration to structural cosmology:

The Coiled Waves of Creation: Her hair strands represent the infinite, curled, and interwoven rays of cosmic energy projected from Her head. They appear wavy and complex (bandhura) to the human eye, symbolizing the intricate, multi-layered fabric of the manifest universe that She wears effortlessly.

Nāma 548

विमर्शरूपिणी

Samāsa-vigraha

विमर्शः एव रूपम् अस्याः अस्तीति।

Word by word

विमर्शः — reflective consciousness, self-awareness.

एव — itself, indeed.

अस्याः — of her.

अस्तीति — is.

विमर्शरूपिणी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is of the form of Vimarsha.

(ii) Vimarsha is the self-awareness aspect of consciousness, without which pure Prakasha cannot manifest as experience.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details one of the absolute pillars of Śrīvidyā/Non-dual Śākta theology:

The Dynamic Mirror of Consciousness: Ultimate reality consists of two aspects: प्रकाश (Prakāśa — the static, self-luminous light of pure consciousness, Śiva) and विमर्श (Vimarśa — the dynamic, self-reflective awareness of that light, Śakti). Without Vimarśa, consciousness would remain inert, unable to know its own existence or project worlds. She is that critical cosmic mirror.

Nāma 549

विद्या

Samāsa-vigraha

मोक्षप्रदज्ञानस्वरूपत्वाद्विद्या।

Word by word

मोक्षप्रदज्ञानस्वरूपत्वाद्विद्या — Vidya because she is knowledge that grants liberation.

विद्या — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) She is the Vidya that confers salvation.

(ii) Saptashatee says that the holy supreme Devee is Vidya. Gaudapada also says in Sree Vidya Ratna Sutra that She herself is Vidya.

(iii) Vidya is the supreme knowledge by which the products of Maya are discriminated and the state of wisdom is recognized.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya distinguishes Her from ordinary informational data fields:

The Science of Liberation: She is not Aparā-vidyā (relative worldly information). She is परविद्या (Parā-vidyā)—the direct, experiential non-dual insight that breaks the illusion of cosmic separation and reveals the identity of the Self with Brahman, acting as the immediate engine of Mokṣa.

Nāma 550

वियदादिजगत्प्रसूः

Samāsa-vigraha

वियद्व्योम आदिर्यस्य तज्जगत्प्रसूते इति।

Word by word

वियद्व्योम — ether/space.

आदिर्यस्य — beginning with which.

तज्जगत्प्रसूते — mother/source of that world.

Meaning

(i) One who is the mother of the universe consisting of ether and other elements.

(ii) In Taittiriya Upanishad it is mentioned that ether arose from the Supreme Being, air from ether, fire from air, water from fire and earth from water. These are the primary elements for the creation of this dynamic universe.

(iii) Vyad, or ether, is perceived as close, yet seems farther as one approaches. Similarly the Supreme Being appears to be understood, yet remains beyond grasp. This status is indicated through ether, the first of the elements.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya tracks the systematic cosmic evolution:

The Mother of Elements: The universe evolves in a precise cascade: first space (Ākāśa), then air, fire, water, and earth. She is the primordial matrix (Prasūḥ) that stands before the first element, breathing out the space matrix within which the rest of creation can subsequently unfold.

Nāma 551

सर्वव्याधिप्रशमनी

Samāsa-vigraha

सर्वेषां व्याधीनां प्रशमनी।

सर्वेषां — of all.

व्याधीनां — of diseases.

प्रशमनी — pacifier, remover.

सर्वव्याधिप्रशमनी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who cures or alleviates all illnesses and diseases.

(ii) The same message is conveyed in the 876th name, Niramaya.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details Her healing capacity across both dense and subtle tracks:

The Absolute Physician: Vyādhi operates on two levels: physical biological diseases of the body, and the ultimate subtle disease—भवव्याधि (bhava-vyādhi—the chronic sickness of saṁsāric wandering). She forcefully eradicates both, cooling the fever of the physical organs and curing the spiritual blindness of the soul.

Nāma 552

सर्वमृत्युनिवारिणी

Samāsa-vigraha

सर्वमृत्यून् निवारयतीति।

Word by word

सर्वमृत्यून् — all deaths.

निवारयतीति — wards off.

सर्वमृत्युनिवारिणी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who dispels all forms of death.

(ii) Since all forms of death are mentioned, this includes untimely death and death due to old age. Untimely death may be due to accident or fatal disease; She prevents these.

(iii) Anyone born in this world must face death. Depending on actions during life, future births are decided. The fruits of actions are also called Mrityus. She saves one from these Mrityus by making one realise the Self and reach the nectar stage. The Srutis also advise the same: knowing Him, one breaks the noose of death.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya decodes the prevention of untimely death:

The Shield Against Mortality: Death can occur prematurely (apamṛtyu) due to accidents, planetary shifts, or curses before the full life-term is reached. She acts as the ultimate protective shield, blocking these accidental vectors. In the highest sense, She grants the deathless state of immortality by dissolving the ego before the body falls.

Nāma 553

अग्रगण्या

Samāsa-vigraha

गणयितुम् — to be counted.

गण्या — to be counted.

सा — she.
