(i) One who deserves to be counted first.

(ii) She is foremost among all, and therefore worthy of being placed at the head of any enumeration.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya establishes Her premier position across all evaluation metrics:

The First Principle: When scholars, sages, or scriptures sit down to list the foundational causes, supreme forces, or objects of worship in the cosmos, She must be counted at position number one (Agra). She stands before all dependencies, anchoring the rest of the list.

Nāma 554

अचिन्त्यरूपा

Samāsa-vigraha

चिन्तयितुम् अशक्यं रूपं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

चिन्तयितुम् — to think.

अशक्यं — impossible.

रूपं — form.

यस्याः — whose.

सा — she.

अचिन्त्यरूपा — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One whose form is beyond thought.

(ii) Her nature cannot be grasped by ordinary mental conception.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya clarifies the limits of the ordinary rational intellect:

Beyond Conceptual Computing: The human mind can only think about things that are bound by time, space, and attributes. Because Her essential form is the infinite, non-dual, attribute-less Brahman, the ordinary brain cannot frame Her inside standard concepts. She must be realized through direct absorption, not thought out.

Nāma 555

कलिकल्मषनाशिनी

Samāsa-vigraha

कलियुगे कल्मषानां नाशिनी।

Word by word

कलियुगे — in the Kali age.

कल्मषानां — of impurities/sins.

नाशिनी — destroyer.

कलिकल्मषनाशिनी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who destroys the sins and impurities of the Kali age.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the modern corrective shield:

The Antidote to the Dark Age: The Kali Yuga is characterized by intense mental distraction, decline in moral rectitude (Dharma), and heavy psychological impurities (kalmaṣa). As Kalikalmaṣanāśinī, Her specialized energetic layout acts as a high-velocity filter, clearing these dark age distortions from the mind of any seeker who calls upon Her name.

Nāma 556

कात्यायनी

Samāsa-vigraha

कतो नामर्षिः तस्यापत्यं स्त्री।

Word by word

कतो — from the sage named Kata/Katyayana.

नामर्षिः — the sage so named.

तस्यापत्यं — his descendant/offspring.

स्त्री — female.

कात्यायनी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the daughter of the sage Katyayana.

(ii) The Vamana Purana says that this is the name of the Deity formed from the collective brightness of all the Devas, comparable to the account in Saptashati where the brightness of the Devas combines to form Mahalakshmi, the destroyer of Mahishasura.

(iii) According to Kalika Purana, She is Katyayani in Odyana Peetha, Kamakhya in Kamarupa, Purneshwari in Purnagiri, and Chandi in Jalandhara Peetha.

(iv) According to Devi Purana, She supports and pervades the whole world, and therefore receives the name Katyayani.

(v) The Gopika ladies worshipped Katyayani during Margasirsha month and obtained Krishna as their husband. In the Kavacha of Saptashati, Katyayani is also the sixth of the nine names of Durga.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya unpacks Her alignment within historical and ritual revelation:

The Unified Mass of Light: Mythologically, when the tyrannical demonic forces could not be checked by individual gods, the collective angers and splendors of the entire trinity and deities fused together at the hermitage of Sage Kātyāyana. She emerged out of this unified mountain of blazing light as the ultimate defensive warrior goddess, demonstrating Her status as the collective kinetic matrix of the cosmos.

Nāma 557

कालहन्त्री

Samāsa-vigraha

कालस्य मृत्योर्हन्त्री।

Word by word

कालस्य — of Time/death.

कालहन्त्री — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the destroyer of Time or Death.

(ii) Sruti, in the Svetasvatara Upanishad, says that Brahman is the Time of time and is all-knowing. She is therefore the destroyer even of Kala, the power of death.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya details Her absolute supremacy over the governing dimension of mortality:

The Transcendent Substratum: Time (Kāla) devours all created entities without exception. However, because She is the immutable eternal consciousness existing before the dawn of time, She ultimately devours Time itself during the cosmic collapse (mahāpralaya).

Deliverance from Mortality: For the realized practitioner, She acts as Kālahantrī by slicing away the illusion of temporal change, rescuing the soul from the cyclical fear of death and anchoring it in deathless awareness.

Nāma 558

कमलाक्षनिषेविता

Samāsa-vigraha

कमलाक्षेण विष्णुना नितरां सेविता।

Word by word

कमलाक्षेण — by the lotus-eyed one.

विष्णुना — by Vishnu.

सेविता — worshipped.

कमलाक्षनिषेविता — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is specially worshipped by the lotus-eyed Mahavishnu.

(ii) Padma Purana says that Vishnu always worships the sapphire-like Devi and thereby attains the state of Vishnu.

(iii) The story of Vishnu worshipping with lotuses and offering his own eye when one lotus was short may be remembered. Since Shiva and Shakti are not different, that worship may also be understood as worship of Sreedevee.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya highlights Her supreme position relative to the maintenance phase of the cosmos:

The Source of Pervasive Power: Viṣṇu (Kamalākṣa) is the all-pervading protector of the worlds. Bhāskararāya notes that Viṣṇu can execute his preservation duties strictly because he meditates upon and draws kinetic energy from Her. His continuous adoration at Her feet ensures the structural stability of cosmic Dharma.

Nāma 559

ताम्बूलपूरितमुखी

Samāsa-vigraha

ताम्बूलेन पूरितं मुखं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

ताम्बूलेन — with betel leaf.

पूरितं — filled.

मुखं — mouth/face.

यस्याः — whose.

सा — she.

ताम्बूलपूरितमुखी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One whose mouth is filled with betel leaves.

(ii) This is connected with the earlier description of the fragrance of Her tambula. The aroma from Her mouth is treated as a mark of royal enjoyment and auspicious beauty.

(iii) Legendary poets such as Kalidasa and others are said to have gained poetic excellence by receiving the juice of Sreedevee's tambula.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya strips this aesthetic description of any mundane parameters to reveal the Śrīvidyā ritual indicators:

The Red Flush of Cosmic Activity: The chewing of Tāmbūla colors the mouth bright red and generates a rich fragrance. In Tantric symbolism, the red color represents Rāga—not mundane desire, but the intense, compassionate impetus to project and protect the universe.

The Speech Matrix: The mouth filled with betel ingredients represents the unceasing, fragrant generation of sacred speech (Vāk) and the containment of mantric seeds ready to be dispensed to seers.

Nāma 560

दाडिमीकुसुमप्रभा

Samāsa-vigraha

दाडिमीवृक्षस्य कुसुमस्येव प्रभा यस्याः सा।

Word by word

दाडिमीवृक्षस्य — of the pomegranate tree.

कुसुमस्येव — like the flower.

प्रभा — lustre.

यस्याः — whose.

सा — she.

दाडिमीकुसुमप्रभा — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One whose lustre is like the hue of a pomegranate flower.

(ii) There are varieties of pomegranate trees; the kind referred to here is known for its brilliant red flowers. Her complexion is compared to that vivid red colour.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya maps this color frequency within visual concentration:

The Light of Pure Will: The pomegranate blossom exhibits a unique, intensely bright crimson-red color that stands out sharply in nature. This visual profile represents the pure, concentrated vibration of इच्छाशक्ति (Icchā-śakti — divine will). Meditating on this vibrant crimson light cleanses the practitioner's psychic channels, dispelling intellectual grayness.

Nāma 561

मृगाक्षी

Samāsa-vigraha

मृगस्य अक्षिणी इव अक्षिणी यस्याः सा।

Word by word

मृगस्य — of a deer.

अक्षिणी — eyes.

इव — as if.

यस्याः — whose.

सा — she.

मृगाक्षी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who has eyes like those of a deer.

(ii) The eyes of deer are not fixed in one place but move on all sides. Such wavering eyes add beauty. Sreedevee's eyes move in this manner so that Her compassionate glance may fall upon all devotees on every side.

(iii) The 103rd name of Trishati, Harinekshana, may be compared.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the quality of Her gaze toward creation:

The Gaze of Gentle Compassion: A deer's eyes are exceptionally wide, dark, liquid, and gentle, entirely devoid of predatory intent. Her glance (īkṣaṇa) toward bound souls reflects this exact spontaneous tenderness. Concurrently, in subtle anatomy, it marks Her constant surveillance over the restless, deer-like movements of the individual mind (Manas), working to soothe it into stillness.

Nāma 562

मोहिनी

Samāsa-vigraha

मोहयतीति।

Word by word

मोहयतीति — enchants, deludes.

मोहिनी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who enchants or bewitches.

(ii) Laghu Naradiya Purana says that She deludes the entire universe through Her beauty, and therefore She is called Mohini.

(iii) Vishnu is said to have assumed the Mohini form by meditating upon Sreedevee. Soundaryalahari also indicates that even great sages are enchanted through Her grace.

(iv) Mohini is also connected with certain sacred reckonings of time and with the presiding deity of the temple at Nivasapura on the banks of the river Pravara.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya explains a key functional aspect of Her cosmic veiling power:

The Grand Bewilderment: As Mohinī, She is the mysterious power that throws the blanket of relative difference over consciousness, making the non-dual absolute appear as a fragmented world of objects. This enchantment keeps the cosmic game (Līlā) moving.

The Saver of Gods: Mythologically, She is the enchanting form assumed by Viṣṇu (who is identical with Her energy) to delude the chaotic forces and protect the nectar of immortality.

Nāma 563

मुख्या

Samāsa-vigraha

मुखे सर्वादौ भवा।

Word by word

मुखे — at the beginning / in the face.

सर्वादौ — first of all.

भवा — being, existing.

मुख्या — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the first or principal.

(ii) When a child is born, the face is the first part to appear; therefore what is first is called mukhya.

(iii) She is first among all that has originated and foremost among all deities. Taittiriya Upanishad says, 'I am the first-born of truth.'

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya anchors Her priority across evolutionary logic:

The Primal Cause: She is Mukhyā because She stands at the absolute head of the causal chain (Prāthamikī). Before a single element, word, or dimension is projected, She exists as the primary, uncaused foundation. She is the chief animating principle governing all subsequent secondary forces.

Nāma 564

मृडानी

Samāsa-vigraha

मृडस्य परमशिवस्य पत्नी।

Word by word

मृडस्य — of Mrida, Shiva.

परमशिवस्य — of Paramashiva.

पत्नी — wife, consort.

मृडानी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the consort of Mrida, Paramashiva.

(ii) The word Mrida, as a verbal root, indicates giving happiness. Since Paramashiva gives happiness to all, He is called Mrida, and She is His consort, Mridani.

(iii) Mridani is also indicated in Mahashodanyasa in the form of Paksha.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya explores the etymological root of this title:

The Power of Pure Mercy: मृड (Mṛḍa) signifies the one who melts completely with compassion, pardoning errors and granting joy. She is the dynamic, non-dual power (Śakti) that expresses this mercy. Through Her form as Mṛḍānī, She absorbs the devotee's historical errors and realigns their life with divine order.

Nāma 565

मित्ररूपिणी

Samāsa-vigraha

मित्राणां सूर्याणामिव रूपमस्याः अस्तीति।

Word by word

मित्राणां — of Mitras / Suns / friends.

सूर्याणामिव — like the Suns.

रूपमस्याः — her form.

अस्तीति — is.

मित्ररूपिणी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of the Sun or in the form of a friend.

(ii) Mitra is one of the twelve names of the Sun. She is therefore the illuminating and sustaining principle.

(iii) In Sree Vidya Tantra, fire indicates Shiva, Moon indicates Sreedevee, and Sun indicates the unified form of both. Mitra also means friend; thus She is the friendly Self.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya decodes this name across structural solar frameworks and moral attributes:

The Luminous Solar Matrix: मित्र (Mitra) is a primary Vedic name for the Sun. She is identical with the twelve solar deities (Dvādaśa-āditya) that radiate life-giving light and energy across the planetary grid.

The Universal Friend: On a spiritual path, She functions as the ultimate, non-judgmental friend (Mitra) who stays close to the soul, guiding it out of internal darkness.

Nāma 566

नित्यतृप्ता

Samāsa-vigraha

नित्यं तृप्ता।

नित्येन स्वरूपानन्देन तृप्ता।

Word by word

नित्यं — always, eternally.

तृप्ता — satisfied.

नित्येन — by the eternal.

स्वरूपानन्देन — by the bliss of her own nature.

नित्यतृप्ता — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is eternally content.

(ii) She is complete in every respect and needs nothing. Therefore She is always satisfied.

(iii) She is contented by the eternal bliss of Her own true nature.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya defines Her absolute freedom from desire:

Satiation within the Self: Human satisfaction is brief and dependent on acquiring external objects. She is Nityatṛptā because She experiences absolute fulfillment exclusively through Her own intrinsic self-bliss (Svarūpānanda). Lacking nothing and containing everything, She remains completely full, untouched by the hunger of lack.

Nāma 567

भक्तनिधिः

Samāsa-vigraha

भक्तानां निधिः।

Word by word

भक्तानां — of devotees.

निधिः — treasure.

भक्तनिधिः — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is a treasure for devotees.

(ii) She grants whatever is asked by devotees. The name Vanchitartha Pradayini may be compared.

(iii) Soundaryalahari says that She gives even more than what the devotee asks.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the immense spiritual wealth She represents:

The Ultimate Storehouse: A Nidhi is an inexhaustible, hidden treasure house that permanently eliminates poverty once uncovered. For those who possess real devotion (bhakti), She functions as this absolute treasure. Finding Her terminates all spiritual and mental poverty, granting immediate access to the riches of liberation.

Nāma 568

नियन्त्री

Samāsa-vigraha

जगन्नियामक्त्वात् नियन्त्री।

Word by word

नियन्त्री — controller, governor.

नियन्त्री — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who guides and controls the universe.

(ii) Because She governs and directs the whole universe, She is called Niyantri.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details Her absolute legislative control over the cosmos:

The Cosmic Director: She is जगन्नियामिका (Jaganniyāmikā) — the supreme inner controller who dictates and maintains the laws of nature, physics, karma, and time. Not a single planet rotates and not a single atom vibrates outside Her structural coordination. She holds the entire universe in disciplined order.

Nāma 569

निखिलेश्वरी

Samāsa-vigraha

निखिलस्य ईश्वरी।

Word by word

निखिलस्य — of all.

ईश्वरी — ruler, sovereign.

निखिलेश्वरी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the ruler of all.

(ii) Since She controls the universe, She is the sovereign ruler of everything.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, this confirms Her boundless scope:

Sovereignty without Remainder: A king's rule ends at his border wall. Her sovereignty (Īśvaritva) is Nikhila — it covers the entire multi-dimensional grid of space, matter, souls, and unmanifest potentials. There is absolutely no corner of reality that sits outside Her imperial command.

Nāma 570

मैत्र्यादिवासनालभ्या

Samāsa-vigraha

मैत्र्यादिभिः वासनाभिः लभ्या।

Word by word

मैत्र्यादिभिः — by friendliness and the like.

वासनाभिः — by dispositions/tendencies.

लभ्या — attainable.

मैत्र्यादिवासनालभ्या — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is attained through dispositions such as friendliness.

(ii) Yoga texts teach that bad tendencies should be removed and good dispositions cultivated: friendship towards the happy, compassion towards the suffering, joy in the righteous, and indifference towards the sinful.

(iii) Srimad Bhagavatam and Yoga Sutra describe these four dispositions, namely maitri, karuna, mudita, and upeksha. They purify the mind and make Sreedevee easy to attain.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya links this directly to the foundational psychological purifications noted in the Patañjali Yoga Sūtras (Citta-prasādana):

The Ethical Access Path: The four pure attitudes are मैत्री (friendliness toward the happy), करुणा (compassion toward the suffering), मुदिता (joy toward the virtuous), and उपेक्षा (neutrality toward the vicious). Bhāskararāya notes that She cannot be reached by minds hardened by jealousy or hatred. Cultivating these clean mental impressions clears the internal environment, allowing Her light to emerge.

Nāma 571

महाप्रलयसाक्षिणी

Samāsa-vigraha

महाप्रलये साक्षिणी।

Word by word

महाप्रलये — in the great dissolution.

साक्षिणी — witness.

महाप्रलयसाक्षिणी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the witness of the great dissolution.

(ii) Soundaryalahari describes the dissolution of Brahma and others. Sreedevee alone remains as the witness.

(iii) A witness does not participate in the action and is not affected by its result. She is such a witness of the great pralaya.

(iv) The names Maheshvara Mahakalpa Mahatandava Sakshini and Sakshivargita may also be compared.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details Her position at the absolute end of the cosmic movie:

The Sole Survivor: During the Mahāpralaya, the five elements dissolve, space collapses, time terminates, and even the creator deities (Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra) vanish into unmanifest matter. She stands entirely alone in this absolute darkness, functioning as the silent, unblinking witness (Sākṣiṇī), proving Her status as the eternal, independent reality.

Nāma 572

पराशक्तिः

Samāsa-vigraha

परा शक्तिः।

परायाः (मन्त्रस्य शक्तिः।

Word by word

परा — supreme.

शक्तिः — power, energy.

परायाः — of Para / of the supreme mantra.

मन्त्रस्य — of the mantra.

पराशक्तिः — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the Supreme Power.

(ii) Agamic texts describe certain bodily elements as arising from Shakti and others from Shiva; the tenth principle is called Parashakti.

(iii) Parashakti also means the very great energy. The principle of Shakta doctrine is that Shiva attains manifest greatness only through union with Shakti.

(iv) Sruti says that His supreme Shakti is known in manifold forms. Linga Purana also says that whatever energy is found in any substance is Sreedevee.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya details the operational engine of the absolute:

The Transcendent Energy: She is the Parā-śakti celebrated across all Agamic revelation — the supreme, primordial kinetic power that belongs to Brahman. She is the capacity through which non-dual awareness expresses its will, projects universes, and reveals its own hidden beauty, serving as the master key of the entire Śrīvidyā system.

Nāma 573

परानिष्ठा

Samāsa-vigraha

परा निष्ठा।

परायां निष्ठा यस्याः सा।

Word by word

परा — supreme.

निष्ठा — final state, establishment.

परायां — in the supreme.

यस्याः — whose.

सा — she.

परानिष्ठा — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the final end of speech, action, and thought.

(ii) Bhagavad Gita says that all actions culminate in knowledge.

(iii) Suta Samhita describes the highest state as firm knowledge, based on scripture, teacher, reasoning, and experience, that the Self alone is pure non-dual Brahman. This is the highest culmination of scriptural teaching and direct experience.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya defines the absolute ceiling of spiritual attainment:

The Ultimate Absorption: Niṣṭhā describes a state of unshakeable, permanent fixity where the mind has completely ceased its external wandering. As Parāniṣṭhā, She represents that final, non-dual absorption where all relative states dissolve into pure Brahman awareness, a state that She simultaneously guides the seeker toward.

Nāma 574

प्रज्ञानघनरूपिणी

Samāsa-vigraha

प्रकृष्टेन ज्ञानेन घनं रूपमस्याः इति।

Word by word

प्रकृष्टेन — by supreme, excellent.

ज्ञानेन — knowledge.

घनं — compact, solid mass.

रूपमस्याः — her form.

प्रज्ञानघनरूपिणी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is of the form of pure, concentrated, supreme knowledge.

(ii) Pra means superior and beyond ordinary mental modification. Jnana is eternal wisdom. Ghana means compact, solid, and not contaminated by ignorance.

(iii) Brihadaranyaka Upanishad compares the Self to a lump of salt, full of taste throughout. She is the solidified form of supreme wisdom.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya anchors this directly in the profound declarations of the Māṇḍūkya and Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣads:

The Homogenous Mass: प्रज्ञानघन (Prajñāna-ghana) describes a reality that contains no internal gaps, no differences, and no foreign elements—just like a solid block of salt has only one taste throughout. Her entire body is made of nothing but pure, unadulterated, dense consciousness, completely free from the filters of objective thoughts.

Nāma 575

माध्वीपानालसा

Samāsa-vigraha

माध्व्या पानेनालसा।

Word by word

माध्व्या — by madhvi drink.

माध्वीपानालसा — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is languid after drinking madhvi.

(ii) Madhvi is an alcoholic drink mixed with grapes and honey. Many names describe Sreedevee as connected with divine drink.

(iii) In these contexts madhu or liquor indicates supreme bliss. Therefore this name means that She is immersed in the bliss of the Supreme Self.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya purges this name of any literal, crude intoxication perspectives:

The Ecstasy of Self-Absorption: माध्वी (mādhwī) refers to the supreme nectar of immortality (amṛta) that downpours from the Sahasrāra crown center during high-level internal union. Drinking this celestial essence causes Her active, projective energy to become wonderfully relaxed and languid (alasā), drawing the practitioner's entire internal system into deep, ecstatic Samādhi.

Nāma 576

मत्ता

Samāsa-vigraha

मत्ता इव।

मद्भावः (अहम्भावः)।

Word by word

मत्ता — intoxicated.

इव — as if.

मद्भावः — state of I-ness / self-sense.

अहम्भावः — ego-sense.

मत्ता — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who appears intoxicated or unconscious.

(ii) As in the previous name, this indicates the state caused by divine drink, understood as supreme bliss.

(iii) Mat also indicates the Self and the sense of 'I'. Soundaryalahari describes Her as the ego-form of Paramashiva.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya decodes this state of absolute divine pride:

The Pride of Being: She is Mattā because She is completely filled with the ecstasy of Her own infinite existence. Bhāskararāya also highlights an advanced grammatical extraction: मद्-भाव (Mad-bhāva) represents the absolute, uncorrupted cosmic ego—the pure, non-dual sense of "अहम्" ("I am") that characterizes the supreme absolute before it splits into objects.

Nāma 577

मातृकावर्णरूपिणी

Samāsa-vigraha

मातृका (अकारादिक्षकारान्ताः)। तासां वर्णाः। तान्येव रूपं स्वरूपमस्याः इति।

मातृकावर्णा (एकपञ्चाशत्) एव रूपमस्या इति।

मातृकावर्णा एव रूपा निरूपका वाचका यस्याः इति।

मातृकावर्णान् रूपयति (जनयति) इति।

Word by word

मातृका — letters of the alphabet.

अकारादिक्षकारान्ताः — from a to ksha.

तासां — of them.

वर्णाः — letters/colours.

तान्येव — those very.

स्वरूपमस्याः — her own form.

एव — itself.

यस्याः — whose.

रूपयति — forms, manifests.

जनयति — generates.

मातृकावर्णरूपिणी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of all Sanskrit letters.

(ii) She is in the form of the fifty-one letters. Since letters give form and colour to words, they are called varnas.

(iii) Tantric texts assign colours to the letters in the chakras and identify Her with the Shakti that gives individuality to letters.

(iv) She is also the garland of letters, the sound-Brahman, and the source of the matrika letters. Some traditions connect this name with the Kailasa Prastara form of Sreechakra.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the foundational phonic framework of the cosmos:

The Phonic Matrix of Reality: मातृका (Mātṛkā) represents the fifty-one sacred syllables of the Sanskrit alphabet running from अ to क्ष. These letters are not human tools; they are the "little mothers" — the foundational acoustic blueprints out of which every object, name, and element in the universe is woven. She is this structural phonic grid, acting as the soul of all mantras.

Nāma 578

महाकैलासनिलया

Samāsa-vigraha

महाकैलास एव निलयो यस्याः सा।

Word by word

महाकैलास — great Kailasa.

एव — itself.

यस्याः — whose.

सा — she.

महाकैलासनिलया — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who resides in the great Kailasa.

(ii) Puranas describe Mahakailasa as beyond the ordinary Kailasa, the abode of Paramashiva.

(iii) The word Maha is used by the Vagdevis to indicate very great ideas, things, and deities.

(iv) Kailasa is also interpreted as the Sahasrara in the Brahmarandhra, where Shiva in the form of bindu resides.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya elevates this past the physical mountain range to its highest cosmic coordinate:

The Peak of Non-Dual Union: While the earthly Kailāsa is Śiva's mountain, महाकैलास represents the supreme, unmanifested transcendental space where Shiva and Shakti exist in absolute, unbroken non-dual embrace. It corresponds internally to the luminous white space within the Sahasrāra crown center.

Nāma 579

मृणालमृदुदोर्लता

Samāsa-vigraha

मृणालमिव (बिसतन्तुः इव) मृद्व्यो दोर्लता यस्याः।

Word by word

मृणालमिव — like a lotus fibre/stalk.

बिसतन्तुः — lotus fibre.

इव — as if.

दोर्लता — creeper-like arms.

यस्याः — whose.

मृणालमृदुदोर्लता — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One whose arms are soft and slender like lotus stalks.

(ii) The earlier names Bisatantu Taniyasi and Shatodari may be recalled, where Her subtle fineness and slenderness were similarly praised.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya decodes the structural symbolism of Her limbs:

The Soft Grip of Grace: Her arms hold the cosmic weapons (the bow, arrows, noose, and goad). Though these tools govern creation and alignment, Her limbs are described as soft as a lotus fiber (mṛṇāla), reminding the devotee that Her execution of cosmic law and correction is driven entirely by gentle maternal grace.

Nāma 580

महनीया

Samāsa-vigraha

पूज्यत्वात् महनीया।

Word by word

पूज्यत्वात् — because of being worthy of worship.

महनीया — venerable.

महनीया — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is worthy of worship by all.

(ii) The name Mahapujya may be compared. Vishnu Sahasranama names such as Stavya and Arha similarly indicate one who deserves worship and honour.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya notes the natural response of the intellect to Her presence:

The Object of Supreme Reverence: She is Mahanīyā because Her very presence commands absolute, instinctive reverence from every tier of intelligence in the cosmos. By meditating upon Her adorable status, the practitioner's mind is cleared of superficiality, instilling deep spiritual humility.

Nāma 581

दयामूर्तिः

Samāsa-vigraha

दयैव मूर्तिः स्वरूपं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

दयैव — compassion itself.

मूर्तिः — form, embodiment.

स्वरूपं — nature, form.

यस्याः — whose.

सा — she.

दयामूर्तिः — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the personification of mercy and compassion.

(ii) Earlier names such as Karunarasasagara, Sandrakaruna, and Avyajakarunamurti convey the same sense.

(iii) The dhyana verse of this Sahasranama calls Her Karunatarangitakshi, one whose eyes move with waves of compassion.

(iv) Traditional hymns such as Daya Shatakam and Kshamashodashi describe compassion as the force that protects even those whose faults would otherwise disqualify them.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya removes any misconception regarding the nature of the absolute ruler:

Compassion Incarnate: She does not simply feel pity or perform merciful acts. Her entire energetic and physical manifestation is nothing but compassion itself (Dayā-svarūpa). Every cosmic operation She runs—even dissolution and karmic correction—is structurally designed to evolve souls, demonstrating maternal mercy.

Nāma 582

महासाम्राज्यशालिनी

Samāsa-vigraha

महत् च तत् साम्राज्यं च। तस्य शालिनी।

Word by word

महत् — great.

च — and.

तत् — that.

साम्राज्यं — empire.

शालिनी — possessing.

महासाम्राज्यशालिनी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who possesses a vast empire.

(ii) A Samrat controls many kings; a Mahasamrat controls many Samrats. This name is apt because She is not different from Parameshwara and is the Empress of the dominion of Mahakailasa.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya defines the structural scale of Her throne:

Empress of the Cosmic Order: Her empire (Sāmrājyā) is not a physical territory on Earth. She rules over the entire layout of the multi-dimensional universe. From Her seat on the Śrī Cakra, She directs the laws of nature and the paths of liberation, shining with unmatched imperial authority.

Nāma 583

आत्मविद्या

Samāsa-vigraha

आत्मनः विद्या।

Word by word

आत्मनः — of the Self.

विद्या — knowledge, doctrine.

आत्मविद्या — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the doctrine that helps one understand the Self.

(ii) This Vidya instructs the form of Brahman. The name Shivajnana Pradayini also says that She bestows the knowledge of Brahman.

(iii) The teaching of Brahman to Indra in Kenopanishad may be remembered. Some traditions also take this as the Turiya Gayatri of Mahashodanyasa.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya identifies Her directly with the highest branch of spiritual science:

The Science of Self-Realization: She is not an external object or a distant deity to be analyzed. She is Ātmavidyā — the sacred, internal path of insight that reveals the absolute identity of the individual soul with the universal Self. Realizing Her is identical to recognizing one's own true nature.

Nāma 584

महाविद्या

Samāsa-vigraha

महती (सर्वानर्थनिवारका) च असौ विद्या च।

Word by word

महती — great.

सर्वानर्थनिवारका — remover of all misfortunes.

च — and.

विद्या — knowledge, doctrine.

महाविद्या — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the great doctrine.

(ii) The Atmavidya mentioned in the previous name is great because it teaches Brahman, and is therefore called Mahavidya.

(iii) She is also Mahati, the great one, because She removes all sorrows.

(iv) Navadurga Vidya, or Vanadurga Vidya in some books, and Chandi Navakshari Vidya are also connected with this name.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the protective scale of this identity:

The Destroyer of Miseries: She is the Mahāvidyā because Her path possesses the unique capacity to thoroughly eradicate the ultimate misery—सर्वानर्थ (sarvānartha — the systemic confusion of saṁsāra). It also references Her position as the central matrix behind the ten great Tantric wisdom lineages (Daśa-mahāvidyā).

Nāma 585

श्रीविद्या

Samāsa-vigraha

श्रीश्चासौ विद्या च।

Word by word

श्रीश्चासौ — she who is Sri.

विद्या — knowledge, doctrine.

च — and.

श्रीविद्या — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of Panchadashi Vidya.

(ii) Vidya is explained in four forms: Yajna Vidya, Maha Vidya, Guhya Vidya, and Atma Vidya. Vishnu Purana says that She is all these forms and is the bestower of liberation.

(iii) Tripuratapini Upanishad says that each group of the Panchadashi mantra explains the meaning of the Gayatri mantra.

(iv) It is appropriate to call it Sree Vidya because it gives extraordinary meanings in very few letters. The fruit-section of Trishati says that Sree Vidya alone is the path to liberation.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya states the absolute identity of the system:

The Sovereign Tradition: She is the physical and phonic embodiment of the श्रीविद्या (Śrīvidyā) — the highly revered, fifteen-syllabled (Pañcadaśī) or sixteen-syllabled (Ṣoḍaśī) mantric system that acts as the absolute crown of the Śākta tradition, seamlessly blending material abundance with final liberation.

Nāma 586

कामसेविता

Samāsa-vigraha

कामेन सेविता (उपासिता)।

Word by word

कामेन — by Kama.

सेविता — worshipped.

उपासिता — adored.

कामसेविता — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is adored by Kama.

(ii) Kama here indicates Mahakameshwara, who worshipped Her. In mantra-shastras, Mahakameshwara and Kameshwari are said to have mutually acted as teacher and disciple.

(iii) Kama also indicates the bodiless god of love, the presiding sage of Kadi Vidya, another form of Panchadashi Vidya.

(iv) Soundaryalahari says that Cupid worshipped Sreedevee and received Her blessings; his power succeeds only through Her gracious glance.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya explores this name across the founding lineages of the tradition:

The Kāmarāja Path: Kāmadeva (the deity of love) is one of the premier founding seers who mastered Her mantra, establishing the highly prominent कादि-मत (Kādi-mata) lineage. Concurrently, काम refers to Paramaśiva Himself, who constantly adores Her dynamic energy to initiate cosmic play.

Nāma 587

श्रीषोडशाक्षरीविद्या

Samāsa-vigraha

षोडशानामक्षराणां समाहारः षोडशाक्षरी। श्रीयुक्ता षोडशाक्षरी। सा च असौ विद्या च।

श्रीः इति षोडशमक्षरं यस्यां तादृशी च असौ विद्या च।

Word by word

समाहारः — collection.

षोडशाक्षरी — sixteen-lettered.

श्रीयुक्ता — endowed with Sri.

सा — she.

च — and.

विद्या — knowledge, doctrine.

श्रीषोडशाक्षरीविद्या — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of the sixteen-lettered mantra.

(ii) By adding one seed-letter to the Panchadashi mantra, the sixteen-lettered Vidya is obtained.

(iii) Mahashodashi has different versions in mantra-shastra and must be learnt through a proper teacher.

(iv) The names Atmavidya, Mahavidya, Sreevidya, and this name indicate successive forms of sacred knowledge, including the mantra-form and Parabrahman-form of Sreedevee.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the most guarded mantric formula of the tradition:

The Sixteen-Syllabled Crown: This name explicitly points to the षोडश्यात्मक मन्त्र (Ṣoḍaśī Mantra). By adding the secret, highly potent sixteenth phonic seed—the syllable श्रीं (Śrīṁ)—to the base fifteen-syllabled layout, the mantra reaches its ultimate structural peak. She is that exact phonic formula, which grants absolute liberation.

Nāma 588

त्रिकूटा

Samāsa-vigraha

त्रयाणां (ब्रह्मादीनामवस्थापीठलोकगुणादीनां वा) कूटं (समूहः) यस्यां सा।

वाग्भवादिकूटत्रयाभिन्ना।

Word by word

त्रयाणां — of three.

कूटं — group, section.

समूहः — collection.

सा — she.

वाग्भवादिकूटत्रयाभिन्ना — non-different from the three kutas beginning with Vagbhabha.

त्रिकूटा — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who has three groups or kutas.

(ii) Om has three parts A, U, and M. There are three deities, three worlds, three states of the soul, three bodies, three gunas, three times, and three mantra-kandas.

(iii) In Sree Vidya these are Vagbhabha Kuta, Kamaraja Kuta, and Shakti Kuta. She is the form of all that exists in groups of three.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya decodes the triadic geography of Her mantra and form:

The Three Mantric Peaks: In the Śrīvidyā layout, the mantra is stratified into three distinct peaks or blocks (kūṭas): वाग्भव-कूट (Vāgbhava-kūṭa), कामरौज-कूट (Kāmarāja-kūṭa), and शक्ति-कूट (Śakti-kūṭa). She is non-different from this triadic structure, which maps directly onto the structural states of consciousness.

Nāma 589

कामकोटिका

Samāsa-vigraha

कामः (परशिवः) एव कोटिः (एकदेशः) यस्याः सा।

Word by word

कामः — Kama / desire / Parashiva.

परशिवः — Parashiva.

एव — itself.

कोटिः — limit, point, section.

एकदेशः — one part.

यस्याः — whose.

सा — she.

कामकोटिका — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of Kamakoti.

(ii) Since the Supreme Being is the unified form of Shiva and Shakti, Sreedevee is called Kamakotika.

(iii) She is also identified with the Kamakoti Peetha at Kanchipuram.

(iv) She is the limit or culmination of kama, understood as the highest desire, namely liberation. This is also interpreted as residence in Sreechakra.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya details the non-dual pinnacle:

The Apex of Shiva-Shakti: काम represents Paramaśiva as pure, baseline attraction. कोटि means the absolute pinnacle or matching half. She is Kāmakoṭikā because She sits at the absolute apex where dynamic energy fusions perfectly with static consciousness, anchoring the historical sanctuary at Kāñcī.

Nāma 590

कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूतकमलाकोटिसेविता

Samāsa-vigraha

कटाक्षस्य किङ्करीभूताभिः कमलानां (लक्ष्मीणां) कोटिभिः सेविता।

Word by word

कटाक्षस्य — of the glance.

किङ्करीभूताभिः — made into attendants.

कमलानां — of Lakshmis.

लक्ष्मीणां — of Lakshmis.

कोटिभिः — by crores.

सेविता — worshipped.

कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूतकमलाकोटिसेविता — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One upon whom crores of Lakshmis, made servants by Her mere glance, wait and worship.

(ii) If the glance of Lakshmi for even a moment makes one wealthy, the greatness of Sreedevee, served by crores of Lakshmis, is beyond imagination.

(iii) If Her benign glance falls on a devotee, crores of Lakshmis will attend him. The greatness of Her glance is poetically described in Mooka Panchasati.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya clarifies the hierarchy of prosperity within Her presence:

The Source of Abundance: The goddess of wealth (Lakṣmī) is highly sought after by humans. Yet, Bhāskararāya points out that millions of Lakṣmīs stand ready as humble attendants to a mere fraction of Her side-glance (kaṭākṣa). By simply receiving a glancing ray of Her grace, the practitioner automatically obtains boundless material and spiritual wealth.

BLOCK NOTE: The Five-Station Micro-Cosmic Meditation Array

From Nāma 591 to 597, the text tracks a precise internal meditation layout, mapping Her appearance across the vertical centers of the physical and subtle body as commented upon by Bhāskararāya.

Nāma 591

शिरःस्थिता

Samāsa-vigraha

शिरसि ब्रह्मरन्ध्रे स्थिता।

Word by word

शिरसि — in the head.

ब्रह्मरन्ध्रे — in the Brahmarandhra.

स्थिता — situated.

शिरःस्थिता — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who resides in the head.

(ii) She resides in the Brahmarandhra, assuming the form of a teacher.

(iii) She is also in the form of the final Mahabindu in the sound M of the seed Hrim; this is to be learnt through a teacher.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya initiates the spatial sequence at the crown:

The Station of the Crown Nectar: She resides within the Brahmarandhra at the absolute peak of the head. At this station, She sits as the pure white, unmanifested transcendent light, waiting to pour the nectar of immortality down through the subtle channels.

Nāma 592

चन्द्रनिभा

Samāsa-vigraha

(ब्रह्मरन्ध्रे) चन्द्रस्य निभा (सदृशी)।

Word by word

ब्रह्मरन्ध्रे — in the Brahmarandhra.

चन्द्रस्य — of the Moon.

निभा — similarity, likeness.

सदृशी — similar.

चन्द्रनिभा — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One whose lustre is like the Moon.

(ii) There is a Moon in the lower part of the Brahmarandhra, corresponding to the third division of the Panchadashi Vidya. Therefore She is called Chandranibha.

(iii) The name Chandramandalamadhyaga may also be compared.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya maps the visual quality of the crown deity:

The Soothing Radiance: Her appearance at the head center is a cooling, soothing, unblemished white light, exactly like the full moon. This visual frequency cools the internal fires of stress and karmic friction, spreading deep tranquility through the practitioner.

Nāma 593

भालस्था

Samāsa-vigraha

भाले तिष्ठतीति।

Word by word

भाले — in the forehead.

तिष्ठतीति — abides.

भालस्था — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who resides in the forehead.

(ii) She abides in the Ajna chakra in the forehead in the form of the bindu of the syllable Hrim.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya moves the internal focus down to the forehead junction:

The Station of Command: She positions Her presence at the forehead, aligning with the Ājñā chakra center. Here, She functions as the sharp, inner eye of intuitive vision and intellect, directing the practitioner's internal discernment.

Nāma 594

इन्द्रधनुष्प्रभा

Samāsa-vigraha

इन्द्रधनुः इव प्रकर्षेण भातीति।

Word by word

इन्द्रधनुः — rainbow, Indra’s bow.

इव — as if.

प्रकर्षेण — excellently.

भातीति — shines.

इन्द्रधनुष्प्रभा — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One whose brightness is like a rainbow.

(ii) Indradhanus means the bow of Indra, the rainbow.

(iii) Tantric texts describe the bindu and the crescent in the forehead as forms of light. Bhaskararaya also describes the bindu in the forehead as shining like a lamp, with the crescent above it.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya decodes the chromatic shift at the forehead:

The Multi-Hued Light: While She was pure white at the crown, at the forehead She radiates like a brilliant rainbow (Indradhanus). This signifies the splitting of pure light into the vibrant, functional energy channels (Nāḍīs) that coordinate the intellectual operations of the brain.

Nāma 595

हृदयस्था

Samāsa-vigraha

हृदये तिष्ठतीति।

Word by word

हृदये — in the heart.

तिष्ठतीति — abides.

हृदयस्था — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who resides in the heart.

(ii) She is to be meditated upon in the heart.

(iii) Kalpasutra says that one who knows the heart of the Lord finds happiness at every step. Here the heart indicates the Para-bija.

(iv) Scriptures describe the entire moving and unmoving universe as present in seed-form in the heart.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the third station of internal descent:

The Sanctuary of the Witness: She moves Her focus into the Anāhata heart center. At this junction, She rests as the steady, internal witness light, pulsing gently as the soul of emotional balance and baseline devotion.

Nāma 596

रविप्रख्या

Samāsa-vigraha

रवेः प्रख्या (सदृशा)।

Word by word

रवेः — of the Sun.

प्रख्या — likeness.

रविप्रख्या — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who has brightness like the Sun.

(ii) In the heart there is a solar disc corresponding to the second division of the Panchadashi mantra. Therefore Sreedevee is called Raviprakhya.

(iii) Mooka Panchasati also indicates the same idea.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya notes the solar frequency at the heart:

The Blazing Solar Center: At the heart center, Her radiance shifts to a warm, brilliant, golden-red solar light (Ravi). This intense light operates to burn away internal emotional blocks, fears, and doubts, illuminating the inner cave with clarity.

Nāma 597

त्रिकोणान्तरदीपिका

Samāsa-vigraha

(मूलाधारे) त्रिकोणस्य आन्तरे दीपिका।

Word by word

त्रिकोणस्य — of the triangle.

आन्तरे — inside.

दीपिका — lamp/light.

त्रिकोणान्तरदीपिका — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is like a light within a triangle.

(ii) In the pericarp of the Mooladhara there is a triangle, and within it a disc of fire corresponding to the first division of Panchadashi mantra. Hence She is called Trikonantaradipika.

(iii) Tantraraja Tantra describes fire in Mooladhara, the Sun in the heart, and the Moon below Brahmarandhra; together these form the threefold ancient mantra.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya completes the meditation loop at the subterranean base:

The Lamp of the Root: At the Mūladhāra root center, She sits inside the inverted central triangle. She functions as a steady, unmoving lamp flame (Dīpikā), representing the dormant Kuṇḍalinī energy that holds the baseline vitality of the physical shell intact before its ascent.

Nāma 598

दाक्षायणी

Samāsa-vigraha

दक्षस्य कन्या।

दाक्षायणयज्ञरूपा।

Word by word

दक्षस्य — of Daksha.

कन्या — daughter.

दाक्षायणयज्ञरूपा — in the form of Dakshayana sacrifice.

दाक्षायणी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the daughter of Daksha.

(ii) According to the dictionaries, Dakshayani means the wife of Shiva, and also refers to Rohini and other constellations, daughters of Daksha Prajapati.

(iii) Dakshayana is also a sacrifice involving repetition of Darsha and Purnamasa rites; She is in that form also.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya unpacks Her primary historical incarnation:

The Incarnation of Honor: She historically manifested as Satī, the daughter of King Dakṣa, to execute a critical alignment of cosmic consciousness. Bhāskararāya notes an advanced track: She embodies the structural framework of the sacrifice (yajna) itself, ensuring its moral validity.

Nāma 599

दैत्यहन्त्री

Samāsa-vigraha

दैत्यानां भण्डासुरादीनां हन्त्री।

Word by word

दैत्यानां — of demons.

भण्डासुरादीनां — of Bhandasura and others.

हन्त्री — destroyer.

दैत्यहन्त्री — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who slays demons such as Bhandasura.

(ii) The name Rakshasaghni may also be compared.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya moves this martial title into the internal battlefield:

The Crusher of Inner Chaos: Demons (Daityas), such as Bhaṇḍāsura, represent the dark, chaotic forces of ego and pride that attack the soul. As Daityahantrī, Her active energy tracks and eliminates these internal distortions, restoring the reign of spiritual law (Dharma).

Nāma 600

दक्षयज्ञविनाशिनी

Samāsa-vigraha

दक्षस्य (दक्षयोः) यज्ञं विनाशयितुं शीलमस्याः।

Word by word

दक्षस्य — of Daksha.

यज्ञं — sacrifice.

विनाशयितुं — to destroy.

शीलमस्याः — her nature is.

दक्षयज्ञविनाशिनी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who destroyed the sacrifice of Daksha.

(ii) Daksha, out of ego, did not honour Shiva or give Him His proper offering. Therefore the sacrifice was destroyed.

(iii) Though Shiva and His attendants performed the destruction, Sreedevee was the instrument of that destruction, and hence the name is given to Her.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya decodes the philosophical lesson behind this destruction:

The Dismantling of Egoic Ritualism: King Dakṣa conducted a massive, opulent sacrifice but intentionally excluded Lord Śiva (pure consciousness), driven by pride. She manifested Her terrifying power to systematically tear down that sacrifice. This establishes that any action, ritual, or business performed without honoring the baseline absolute consciousness is an expression of toxic ego that She will dismantle to protect cosmic balance.

Section 7

Names 601–700

नामानि ६०१–७००

Nāma 601

दरान्दोलितदीर्घाक्षी

Samāsa-vigraha

दरम् (ईषद्यथा स्यात्तथा) आन्दोलितानि (चञ्चलानि) दीर्घाणि अक्षीणि यस्याः सा।

दरम् (भयम्) आन्दोलितं (नाशितं) यैः तादृशदीर्घाक्षीणि यस्याः सा।

Word by word

दरम् — slightly / fear.

आन्दोलितानि — moving, wavering.

चञ्चलानि — restless.

दीर्घाणि — long.

अक्षीणि — eyes.

यस्याः — whose.

सा — she.

भयम् — fear.

नाशितं — destroyed.

दरान्दोलितदीर्घाक्षी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One whose long eyes, reaching up to the ears, slightly move.

(ii) Dara means a little; Her eyes gently move on all sides.

(iii) According to physiognomy, eyes extending to the ears are the best. Dara also means fear; Her eyes remove fear.

(iv) Her long wavering eyes allow Her compassionate glance to fall on all devotees.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya unpacks this name across two distinct theological frameworks:

The Movement of Vimarśa: Under the first derivation, the slight, dynamic movement (दर-आन्दोलित) of Her long eyes represents the active pulse of विमर्श (Vimarśa — divine self-awareness) interacting with the static light of consciousness.

The Dissolution of Saṁsāra: Under the second track, दर means fear. Her glance acts as a powerful shield that completely eradicates the baseline existential fear of death, birth, and transience inside the heart of the practitioner.

Nāma 602

दरहासोज्ज्वलन्मुखी

Samāsa-vigraha

दरहासेन उज्ज्वलत् मुखं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

दरहासेन — by a gentle smile.

उज्ज्वलत् — shining.

मुखं — mouth/face.

यस्याः — whose.

सा — she.

दरहासोज्ज्वलन्मुखी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One whose face shines with a smile.

(ii) Darahasa means a gentle smile. Her physical beauty and inner bliss are both indicated by this smile.

(iii) The dhyana verse calls Her Smitamukhi. This name may be compared with Darasmera Mukhambuja and the Trishati name Ishatsmitanana.

(iv) Dara also means fear; in war, Her terrible laughter destroys demons.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the intellectual transformations triggered by Her expression:

The Dawn of Vidyā: The gentle smile (darahāsa) is not a mundane emotional reaction. It represents the soft, luminous dawn of absolute knowledge (विद्या) breaking open. The radiance from Her smile enters the dark, dense blockages of the student's intellect, instantly pacifying spiritual doubt and infusing the consciousness with baseline joy.

Nāma 603

गुरुमूर्तिः

Samāsa-vigraha

गुरुरेव मूर्तिः शरीरं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

गुरुरेव — the Guru himself.

मूर्तिः — form, embodiment.

शरीरं — body.

यस्याः — whose.

सा — she.

गुरुमूर्तिः — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who assumes the form of a teacher.

(ii) Mantra-shastras say that the teacher, the mantra, and the deity are one and should not be seen as different. The Sreechakra and the Self are also to be understood in the same non-different manner.

(iii) Gu means the darkness of ignorance and ru removes it; therefore Guru means one who removes ignorance. Sreedevee comes as the Guru and gives mantra-upadesha.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya defines the core channel of dynamic grace within the Śrīvidyā tradition:

The Human Gateway: The absolute supreme reality is too vast to be conceptualized directly by bound souls. Therefore, She assumes a tangible, human form as the श्रीगुरु (Śrīguru) to execute the transmission of initiatory power (śaktipāta). Bhāskararāya notes that the Guru is never to be viewed as an ordinary mortal; the preceptor is the visible, functional body of the Mother specialized for the liberation of the seeker.

Nāma 604

गुणनिधिः

Samāsa-vigraha

गुणानां निधिः।

गुणा व्यूहरूपा निधिसंख्या यस्याः सा।

गुणो रज्जुः सा चेह नौकाबन्धनी वटीरिकानाम्नी लक्षणया गृह्यते। सा नितरां धीयतेऽस्यामिति गुणनिधिः (मात्स्यकालीपुराणम्)।

Word by word

गुणानां — of qualities.

निधिः — treasure.

यस्याः — whose.

सा — she.

गुणनिधिः — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the treasure-house of qualities.

(ii) Sankhya doctrine speaks of three qualities, sattva, rajas, and tamas, with countless modifications. She is the repository of all such qualities.

(iii) Guna also means aggregate or vyuha; nine such vyuhas are described. Since She is the form of these, She is called Gunanidhi.

(iv) Guna also means rope; Puranic accounts of the rope used at pralaya are connected with Her stabilising power.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya explores this across standard cosmic management and Purāṇic alchemical metaphors:

The Reservoir of Cosmic Virtues: She is the infinite repository (nidhi) of all divine splendors, cosmic qualities, and manifestations.

The Anchor of the Soul: Under the Mātsyakālī Purāṇa track, guṇa denotes the heavy rope used to tie a vessel. She is the secure treasure dock that holds the binding rope of the individual soul's boat, keeping it firmly anchored and safe from capsizing in the turbulent storm waves of material illusion.

Nāma 605

गोमाता

Samāsa-vigraha

गवां धेनूनां माता।

Word by word

गवां — of cows.

धेनूनां — of cows.

माता — mother.

गोमाता — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of Kamadhenu, the divine cow, mother of all cows, or the greatest of cows.

(ii) Dictionaries give many meanings for go, including speech, rays, and heaven. She is the root form of all these.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya elevates this past standard agricultural perspectives to encompass three major linguistic and physical planes:

The Matrix of Words, Earth, and Senses: According to classical lexicon definitions, गो (go) signifies the earth, speech (Vāk), and the human sensory apparatus. As Gomātā, She is the primordial matrix that gives birth to, nourishes, and sustains all three layers, functioning as the ultimate wish-fulfilling cow (Kāmadhenu) for Her children.

Nāma 606

गुहजन्मभूः

Samāsa-vigraha

गुहस्य स्कन्दस्य जन्मभूः।

गुहा जीवाः तेषां जन्मभूः।

Word by word

गुहस्य — of Guha/Subrahmanya.

स्कन्दस्य — of Skanda.

जन्मभूः — birthplace, mother-source.

गुहा — hidden beings, souls.

जीवाः — souls.

तेषां — of them.

गुहजन्मभूः — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the mother of Guha, Lord Muruga or Subrahmanya.

(ii) The root guh means to cover. Souls veiled by ignorance are called guhas. As sparks arise from hot iron, souls arise from the Self; therefore She is also the source of such guhas.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya traces this from mythological history to deep internal coordinates:

The Parent of the Dynamic Power: Mythologically, She is the mother of Skanda (Guha), the lord of intense spiritual action.

The Source of the Cave Dwellers: Esoterically, गुहा (guhā) refers to the hidden, secret cavern of the heart where the individual living souls (जीवाः) reside. She is the primordial baseline space out of which all individual sparks of life are born and projected.

Nāma 607

देवेशी

Samāsa-vigraha

देवानाम् ईशी।

Word by word

देवानाम् — of the gods.

ईशी — ruler.

देवेशी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the ruler of the gods.

(ii) She is the head of all divine powers such as Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, and others.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya defines Her ultimate position over the cosmic administration:

The Sovereign over Light Forces: The Devas represent the cosmic forces of light, law, and balance. She is their absolute Īśī (empress). They draw their specific functional capacities exclusively from Her kinetic field, and they execute their duties strictly under Her supreme governance.

Nāma 608

दण्डनीतिस्था

Samāsa-vigraha

दण्डनीतौ तिष्ठतीति।

Word by word

दण्डनीतौ — in the science of punishment/governance.

तिष्ठतीति — abides.

दण्डनीतिस्था — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who administers justice by punishing the wicked.

(ii) Dandaniti is the science that describes offences and the corresponding punishments. Devi Purana says that because She restrains, corrects, and guides beings along the right path, She is called Dandanitistha.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya details Her alignment with cosmic law:

The Anchor of Moral Law: दण्डनीति represents the absolute metric of governance and corrective justice that maintains moral balance across the universe. She sits at the core of this system, ensuring that the law of cause and effect (Karma) operates with neutral accuracy, returning the exact consequences of actions to maintain universal harmony.

Nāma 609

दहराकाशरूपिणी

Samāsa-vigraha

दहरमाकाशं रूपमस्याः इति।

Word by word

रूपमस्याः — her form.

दहराकाशरूपिणी — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the subtle ether in the cave of the heart.

(ii) In the heart of every being there is a subtle hidden space; She dwells there as the inner ether.

(iii) The Chandogya Upanishad describes the small lotus-house in the city of Brahman and the subtle ether within it. Brahma Sutra identifies this dahara-akasha with Brahman.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya aligns this directly with the premier meditations of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad:

The Sacred Internal Sky: दहराकाश (Daharākāśa) is the tiny, luminous ether chamber hidden deep inside the cavity of the human heart. The Upaniṣad reveals that this internal space contains the entire macrocosm. She is that exact pristine, unblemished inner sky where the absolute can be directly realized when the outward senses are quieted.

Nāma 610

प्रतिपन्मुख्यराकान्ततिथिमण्डलपूजिता

Samāsa-vigraha

प्रतिपत्तिथिः मुख्या यस्मिन्, राकातिथिः अन्ते यस्मिन् तिथिमण्डले तस्मिन् पूजिता।

Word by word

प्रतिपत्तिथिः — the first lunar day.

मुख्या — principal, beginning.

यस्मिन् — in which.

राकातिथिः — the full-moon day.

अन्ते — at the end.

तिथिमण्डले — in the circle of lunar days.

तस्मिन् — in that.

पूजिता — worshipped.

प्रतिपन्मुख्यराकान्ततिथिमण्डलपूजिता — the complete name, understood through the samasa above.

Meaning

(i) One who is worshipped in the circle of lunar days beginning with Pratipat and ending with the full moon.

(ii) Pratipat is the first lunar day and Raka is the full-moon day. She is worshipped through all fifteen days according to tantric rites.

(iii) Each tithi has its presiding Nitya Devi. The sixteen include the fifteen Tithi Nityas and Lalita Mahanitya in the bindu. Tithinitya worship is an important part of Sree Vidya worship.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the integration of time and mantric geometry within this name:

The Mistress of Lunar Time: In Śrīvidyā cosmology, She is non-different from Time itself. The fifteen lunar days are governed by fifteen specific crescent energy deities known as the तिथि-नित्याः (Tithi-Nityāḥ), running from Pratipat to Pūrṇimā. She stands as the sixteenth absolute background light (Ṣoḍaśī) that animates this complete cycle, completely surrounding and permeating the calendar array.

Nāma 611

कलात्मिका

Samāsa-vigraha

कला आत्मा स्वरूपं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

कला — art; kalā; divine digit/power

आत्मा — self; essence

स्वरूपं — own form; essential nature

यस्याः — of whom; whose

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of kalās.

(ii) Kalā indicates several divisions of divine power: the kalās of fire, Sun, Moon, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara and Sadāśiva, as well as the well-known sixty-four arts. All these kalās are forms of Śrīdevī.

(iii) The states such as waking, dream, deep sleep and turīya are also related to different kalās. Their real form is Śrīdevī.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya unpacks the term कला (Kalā) across multiple systematic tracks:

The Manifested Fractions: Kalā represents the digits of the moon, the sixty-four cultural arts, or the functional fractions into which the absolute energy divides itself to construct the material universe. She is the soul of all these diverse expressions, animating the components while remaining internally undivided.

Nāma 612

कलानाथा

Samāsa-vigraha

कलानां नाथा।

Word by word

कलानां — of the kalās

Meaning

(i) She is the head of all kalās.

(ii) The Moon is called the lord of kalās. Since the Śrīcakra itself is contemplated in the form of the lunar sphere, the name Kalānāthā is appropriate for Śrīdevī.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya defines Her operational control over temporal and artistic rays:

The Controller of Time and Expression: As Kalānāthā, She governs the light digits that determine the movement of time and lunar calendars. Concurrently, She rules as the supreme source behind all fine arts and creative intelligence, directing how aesthetic energy is formulated.

Nāma 613

काव्यालापविमोदिनी

Samāsa-vigraha

काव्यानाम् आलापेन मोदिनी।

Word by word

काव्यानाम् — of poems; poetic works

आलापेन — by speech; discourse

Meaning

(i) One who gets delighted with poetical speech, dialogue and description.

(ii) Kāvyas are works of poetry. Their rasa, beautiful speech and figures of speech delight Her.

(iii) A devotee who worships Śrīdevī methodically gains the capacity for poetic expression, as in the examples of Kālidāsa, Mūka and other great devotees.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details Her relationship with high aesthetic culture:

The Muse of Divine Literature: True poetry (Kāvya) is not ordinary wording; it is the harmonious expression of cosmic truth and beauty captured by inspired seers (kavis). She functions as the inner muse behind this literature and is deeply pleased when Her children engage in refined, elevating artistic compositions that mirror divine order.

Nāma 614

सचामररमावाणीसव्यदक्षिणसेविता

Samāsa-vigraha

चामराभ्यां सहिते सचामरे। तादृशीभ्यां रमावाणीभ्यां लक्ष्मीसरस्वतीभ्यां सव्ये दक्षिणे क्रमेण सेविता।

Word by word

चामराभ्यां — by two cāmaras/fans

सहिते — accompanied by

रमावाणीभ्यां — by Ramā/Lakṣmī and Vāṇī/Sarasvatī

सव्ये — on the left

दक्षिणे — on the right

क्रमेण — in order

Meaning

(i) One who is attended on either side by Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī holding cāmaras.

(ii) Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī serve Śrīdevī on both sides. A devotee who becomes merged in devotion to Śrīdevī is also blessed by Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī.

(iii) The reference is also supported by the Soundaryalaharī statement that Brahmā and Hari sport with Sarasvatī and Lakṣmī.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya clarifies the hierarchy of cosmic powers:

Sovereignty over Wealth and Wisdom: Humans spend lifetimes pursuing either material wealth (Lakṣmī) or intellectual learning (Sarasvatī). This name establishes that when a practitioner approaches the absolute center, both cosmic principles stand submissively as entry-level attendants holding fans at Her throne, demonstrating Her absolute status as the supreme source of all capability.

Nāma 615

आदिशक्तिः

Samāsa-vigraha

आदिः कारणभूता च सा शक्तिश्च।

Word by word

आदिः — beginning; primordial cause

कारणभूता — being the cause

सा — she

Meaning

(i) One who is the original power.

(ii) She is the primordial Śakti and the root cause before all later manifestations.

(iii) The later names describe many forms and functions, but this name points to the causal power from which they arise.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya identifies the initial engine behind all physical and subtle operations:

The Uncaused Kinetic Cause: She is Ādi-śakti because She exists prior to the first movement of cosmic manifestation. She is the baseline energy matrix that belongs to the absolute Brahman, acting as the primary source from which all secondary forces (like gravity, light, and electricity) branch out.

Nāma 616

अमेया

Samāsa-vigraha

मातुमशक्या।

मेयं न विद्यते यस्याः सा।

Word by word

मेयं — measurable object

विद्यते — exists

यस्याः — of whom; whose

Meaning

(i) One who cannot be measured.

(ii) She cannot be limited by thought, word, number, place, time or object.

(iii) The name indicates that Her form is beyond the reach of ordinary means of measurement or description.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya applies a fundamental rule of non-dual epistemology:

Beyond Mathematical Quantification: Finite objects can be measured, weighted, and fully computed by human instruments. But because She is the infinite, shoreless background awareness within which space itself exists, She can never be turned into an object to be measured. She remains immeasurable, accessible only through direct absorption.

Nāma 617

आत्मा

Samāsa-vigraha

जीवरूपा।

यच्चाप्नोति यदादत्तेयच्चात्ति विषयानिह। यच्चास्य सततो भावस्तस्मादात्मेति कीर्त्यते॥

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of Ātman or jīva.

(ii) This name indicates the jīvātman, while the following name indicates Paramātman.

(iii) Ātman may mean body, mind, Brahman, nature, firmness and intelligence; as She is present in all these, the name is apt.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya quotes the ancient semantic verses defining the Soul:

The Pervasive Subject: She is Ātmā because She fulfills the four criteria of the Self: She pervades all space (आप्नोति), absorbs all elements into Herself (आदत्ते), experiences and illuminates all objective fields (अत्ति), and exists constantly as the baseline background layer of reality. She is the true inner identity of every living being.

Nāma 618

परमा

Samāsa-vigraha

परब्रह्मरूपा।

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who is supreme and great in all ways.

(ii) She reveals and limits for us the immeasurable Brahman.

(iii) For those without devotion She seems distant; in relation to the previous name as jīvātman, this name points to Paramātman.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya positions this name at the definitive peak of reality:

The Absolute Ceiling: She is Paramā because She marks the absolute ceiling of existence. There is no higher state, no finer consciousness, and no authority back behind Her station, identifying Her directly with the unconditioned Parabrahman.

Nāma 619

पावनाकृतिः

Samāsa-vigraha

पावनी आकृतिः यस्याः सा।

Word by word

पावनी — purifying; sanctifying

आकृतिः — form

यस्याः — of whom; whose

Meaning

(i) One whose body and form are holy and sanctifying.

(ii) The very thought of Śrīdevī washes away sins and makes one pure.

(iii) Kṛti may also mean action; therefore the name may also indicate one whose actions are pure and sanctifying.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the immediate alchemical effect of Her visual geometry:

The Purifying Presence: Her structural form—whether visualized as the anthropomorphic mother or as the geometric framework of the Śrī Cakra—possesses a natural purifying frequency (pāvanī). Simply anchoring the attention upon Her structure cleanses the practitioner's subconscious, burning away mental impurities.

Nāma 620

अनेककोटिब्रह्माण्डजननी

Samāsa-vigraha

अनेका अनन्ताः कोटयो ये ब्रह्माण्डास्तेषां जननी जनयित्री।

अनेककोटयः ब्रह्माण्डाः येषां विराडादीनां ते। तेषां जन

Word by word

अनेका — many

अनन्ताः — endless

जननी — mother

ब्रह्माण्डाः — cosmic eggs; universes

Meaning

(i) One who gave birth to many crores of worlds.

(ii) Virāṭ, Hiraṇyagarbha and Īśvara create crores of worlds, and She is the mother even of them.

(iii) Brahmāṇḍa arises from the gross elements and their modifications; She is the source of all such cosmic spheres.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya strips away any localized planetary limits:

The Architect of the Multiverse: She is not the mother of a single world or an isolated galaxy. Her creative womb projects infinite systems of multiverses (aneka-koṭi-brahmāṇḍa) simultaneously. They float within Her vast space like tiny foam bubbles on an ocean, showcasing Her shoreless creative scale.

Nāma 621

दिव्यविग्रहा

Samāsa-vigraha

दिव्यो रमणीयो विग्रहो देहो यस्याः सा।

दिव अन्तरिक्षे भवो दिव्यो विग्रहो रणो यस्याः सा।

Word by word

यस्याः — of whom; whose

Meaning

(i) One who has a divine and beautiful form.

(ii) The name may also recall the Purāṇic description of Devī appearing in a divine body and fighting even in the sky.

(iii) Her form is not ordinary or material but divya, fit for divine contemplation.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya explores this across visual appearance and martial metaphysics:

The Body of Light: Her form (vigraha) is not composed of dense biological tissue; it is made of pure, self-luminous light energy (aprakṛta).

The High Battlefield: Alternatively, Her cosmic battle (vigraha) against ignorance is conducted in the subtle space of pure consciousness, clearing the internal heavens for the seeker.

Nāma 622

क्लींकारी

Samāsa-vigraha

क्लीं कामं बीजं करोतीति।

कामबीजस्वरूपेति।

क्लींकारस्य शिवकामस्य स्त्रीति।

Word by word

क्लीं — klīṃ bīja

कामं — Kāma; desire

बीजं — seed syllable

Meaning

(i) One who is the personification of the letter klīṃ, the Kāmarāja bīja.

(ii) Klīṃ is the seed connected with Kāma or Manmatha and also with Kāmeśvara.

(iii) The bīja indicates the union of Śiva and Śakti, and Śrīdevī is its living form.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the operational force of this bīja within the tradition:

The Seed of Absolute Attraction: क्लीं is the celebrated Kāmarāja-bīja — the syllable of divine attraction, love, and creative desire. She is Klīṁkārī because She animates the primal vibration that draws elements together to form worlds and calls the individual soul back into non-dual union with Śiva.

Nāma 623

Bhāskararāya details Her absolute ease of operation, removing any concepts of cosmic labor:

Effortless Cosmic Architecture: The creation, structuring, and alignment of infinite planetary grids and universal caskets require no heavy labor, planning committees, or structural fatigue from Her end. It is a spontaneous, effortless overflow of Her playful energy (līlā), projected as easily as a child breathing out soap bubbles.

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

The Invisible Subject: Human eyes and sensory channels are designed strictly to capture external, material objects (dṛśya). Because She is the foundational subjective consciousness that sits behind the eyes, enabling them to see in the first place, She can never be seen as an external object. She is the ultimate seer, permanently invisible to outer sight.

The Resolution of Duality: दृश्य (dṛśya) represents the entire field of changing, objective material appearances. She is Dṛṣyarahitā because in Her ultimate essential state (Svarūpa), the illusion of a separate objective universe completely dissolves. When the practitioner achieves the highest absorption (Nirvikalpa-Samādhi), the movie of the world vanishes, leaving Her to shine alone in Her pristine, non-dual subjective purity.

The Absolute Knower: She is the ultimate subject (draṣṭā) behind all acts of perception. While ordinary intellects analyze separate objects, She is the non-dual baseline awareness that comprehends the entire cosmos comprehensively and distinctively, without error or modification.

In Her essential state of absolute absorption (Samādhi), the triad of knower, knowing, and known dissolves into pure, unified awareness.

Every other material object provides transient distraction, while She represents the ultimate, correct destination of human consciousness.

The Unconnected Absolute: As Ayogā, She possesses no binding contact (saṅga) with material mutations. Alternatively, She leads practitioners to Lord Śiva through pure auspicious pathways (ayena).

The Source of Delight: As Nandā, She manifests as the cleansing current of the Gaṅgā or the ancient protective structural deity born in the Nanda lineage.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya details Her control over linear macrocosmic time:

The Upholder of Time Cycles: The universe passes through the massive cycles of the four eras (yugas — Satya, Tretā, Dvāpara, and Kali). She is Yugandharā because She functions as the absolute background axis that bears the weight of these epochal shifts, ensuring the continuity of cosmic balance across vast expanses of time.

The Triadic Force Matrix: She is the absolute consolidation of the three baseline functional energies that project the universe. As इच्छाशक्ति (Icchā-śakti), She provides the initial divine intent to create. As ज्ञानशक्ति (Jñāna-śakti), She maintains the intellectual blueprint of design. As क्रियाशक्ति (Kriyā-śakti), She executes the actual kinetic movement into dense material elements, proving Her status as the full dynamic expression of reality.

Bhāskararāya unpacks three distinct traditional frameworks mapping Her macrocosmic and psychological design:

The Eight Divine Attributes: She manifests as the eight corporate energies of well-being (Lakṣmī, Medhā, etc.).

The Eight Strata of Soul: She governs the eight layers of internal consciousness running from the individual soul (Jīvātmā) up to the absolute Paramātmā.

The Shiva-Anatomy Grid: She is identical with the Aṣṭamūrti layout of Lord Śiva, where the body consists of the five base elements (earth, water, fire, air, space) along with the Sun, the Moon, and the conscious observer (Jīva), proving Her total immanence in nature.

Conquering the Primordial Veil: अजा (Ajā) is a classical scriptural code for अविद्या (Avidyā — primordial ignorance or cosmic illusion), which has no birth date and veils the true Self. (i) One whose form is immensely great.

(iii) Bṛhat-sāman occurs in the Sāma Veda, and a metre of thirty-six letters is called Bṛhatī. She is in those forms also.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya anchors this in the Upanishadic metrics of scale:

The Boundless Expansion: She is Bṛhatī because Her scale surpasses the highest imaginable metric of greatness (महतो महीयत्वात्). She cannot be contained by any boundary line, expanding infinitely beyond cosmic horizons, serving as the vast space within which multiverses float.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the alignment with pure, uncorrupted knowledge:

The Consort of the Knower: Lord Śiva represents the ultimate, pristine repository of Vedic wisdom—the archetypal Brahman. She is His non-dual dynamic energy (Brāhmaṇī). Concurrently, She represents the refined, highly specialized state of pure internal awareness (Saṁvit-viśeṣa-rūpā) that marks an illumined mind.

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya provides a rigorous logical and mantric insight:

The Non-Dual Substance: Because there is no valid proof (mānābhāva) for the existence of any independent material matter separate from the absolute, the entire universe is fundamentally nothing but Brahman. She is Brāhmī — the expression of this non-dual reality. Concurrently, She is the power of articulation (Vāg-ātmikā) that animates creative sound.

Bhāskararāya defines the quality of Her joy:

The Bliss of the Absolute: She is the living embodiment of that supreme, unconditioned happiness (Ānanda) that defines Brahman. When She assumes a qualified form (Saguṇā) for the sake of the devotee, She radiates this unadulterated cosmic joy, lifting the practitioner out of earthly grief.

The Matrix of Articulation: She manifests directly as the structural architecture of language—including classical Sanskrit, natural Prākṛt, and every linguistic dialect spoken across the planetary grid. Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya details the accessibility of Her devotional path:

Worship Free from Physical Friction: She does not require harsh physical mortification, extreme fasting (upavāsa), or torturous bodily postures (kāya-kleśa). She is Sukhārādhyā because She can be worshipped with ease (sukhena), yielding Her presence to sincere internal devotion and simple love rather than complex mechanical constraints.

The Engine of Auspiciousness: She is Śubhakarī because Her continuous influence automatically transforms the seeker's mental environment, producing auspicious thoughts, moral purity (puṇya), and benign outer circumstances that support spiritual growth.

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who gives all aims of life.

(ii) She grants the four puruṣārthas: dharma, artha, kāma and mokṣa.

(iii) Thus every true human aim is obtained through Her grace.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya outlines Her complete, balanced fulfillment of human aspiration:

The Dispenser of the Four Aims: She handles the complete grid of the four human objectives: धर्म (righteousness), अर्थ (wealth), काम (desire), and मोक्ष (liberation). She ensures that Her devotees do not suffer material lack while seeking spirit, nor get trapped in wealth without spirit, organizing a balanced distribution of all human aims.

Nāma 699

Samāsa-vigraha

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) She is Sāvitrī.

(ii) Savitṛ is the creator or impeller of the world; She is the Śakti of that supreme source.

(iii) The name also recalls the Gāyatrī-Sāvitrī contemplation connected with the Sun and the supreme being.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details Her identity with the absolute source of light:

The Power of the Divine Creator: सवीतृ (Savitā) refers to the supreme generator of the universe—Paramaśiva. She is His non-dual dynamic power (Sāvitrī). This confirms Her absolute identity with the inner essence of the Gāyatrī Mantra, acting as the brilliant light that awakens the spiritual intellect.

Nāma 700

सच्चिदानन्दरूपिणी

Samāsa-vigraha

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One whose form is existence, consciousness and bliss.

(ii) Sat, cit and ānanda together constitute Brahman.

(iii) That Brahman is Śrīdevī; this completes the group of kalās described here.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya concludes this major sequence by stating Her absolute philosophical definition:

The Supreme Definition of Brahman: This name frames Her identity with the unconditioned absolute. She is not a passing manifestation; Her entire essential body is made of nothing but pure, uncorrupted, eternal existence (Sat), infinite, self-luminous awareness (Cit), and boundless, unshakeable bliss (Ānanda), serving as the ultimate refuge of reality.

Section 8

Names 701–800

नामानि ७०१–८००

Nāma 701

देशकालापरिच्छिन्ना

Samāsa-vigraha

देशकालाभ्यामपरिच्छिन्ना।

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who is not limited by space and time.

(ii) Some things are limited by place or time; She is eternal and available at all times, so such distinctions do not apply to Her.

(iii) The meanings of Nityā, Nirnāśā and Vyāpinī are brought together in this name.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya defines Her absolute freedom from spatial and temporal limitations (Pariccheda):

Spatial and Temporal Infinity: Material entities exist at a specific location and endure for a finite duration. She is Deśakālāparicchinnā because She stands completely outside these structural coordinates. She lacks spatial boundaries, meaning She is omnipresent; and She lacks temporal boundaries, meaning She is eternal. She acts as the baseline screen within which space and time themselves unfold.

Nāma 702

सर्वगा

Samāsa-vigraha
