Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who pervades all.

(ii) She reaches all things by non-difference and is present everywhere.

(iii) No place or object is outside Her presence.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the mechanics of Her non-dual pervasiveness:

The Pervasive Substance: She does not simply move from place to place. She is Sarvagā because She reaches and permeates every single objective entity (vastu-mātra) through absolute structural identity (अभेदेन). There is no gap between Her consciousness field and the material forms it animates; She is the essential substance inside every coordinate of the universe.

Nāma 703

सर्वमोहिनी

Samāsa-vigraha

Word by word

मोहयति — bewilders

Meaning

(i) One who bewilders all.

(ii) She bewilders ordinary people who take apparent duality as real and deprives them of the knowledge of unity.

(iii) The apparent difference between Brahman and the universe is illusory; this power of bewilderment is described also in Saptashatī.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya provides a rigorous philosophical analysis of Her veiling power:

The Magic of Duality: As Sarvamohinī, She binds those who view the relative world as an absolute reality (bheda-bhāna). She temporarily veils their non-dual realization (advaita-jñāna-vidhura), causing them to see differences instead of unity. This enchantment is the foundational mechanism that allows the cosmic play (Līlā) to appear real to the individual observer.

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya unpacks this name across three distinct dimensions of wisdom and ritual:

The Shoreless Ocean of Wisdom: She is identical to the supreme goddess of wisdom, Sarasvatī. She represents unconditioned awareness (viṣayānavacchinna-jñāna), flowing like a vast, fluid ocean of insight.

Ritual Maidens: In the liturgical framework of Kumārī-Pūjā defined by Sage Dhaumya, She manifests as the pristine energy of a two-year-old girl, representing pure potential before worldly conditioning.

Nāma 705

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details Her non-differentiation from scriptural truth:

The Body of the Sacred Word: She is Śāstramayī because Her subtle body is woven out of the foundational declarations of non-duality, such as “Sarvaṁ khalvidaṁ Brahma” ("All this is indeed Brahman"). Bhāskararāya notes that every sacred science, text, and structural formula is a limb of Her manifest form, making Her the literal substance of divine revelation.

Meaning

(i) One who dwells in the cave.

(ii) The cave is the heart. The Upaniṣadic idea of shadow and light in the cave of the heart is discussed here.

Bhāskararāya explores this across both historical mythology and deep internal coordinates:

The Guardian of the Secret Cavern: Mythologically, She is the mother of the warrior lord Skanda (Guha). Esoterically, गुहा (guhā) refers to the hidden, secret cavern of the human heart. She is the primordial, protective mother energy (Ambā) that sits inside this internal cave, guarding the individual spark of consciousness.

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One whose form is most secret.

(iii) She is the secret knowledge residing in the secret place, beloved by secret devotees.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya defines the hidden nature of Her ultimate reality:

The Transcendent Secret: Ordinary physical vision is tuned exclusively to capture relative, external material objects. Her true, essential form is Guhya — a supreme secret that cannot be objectified by common, worldly intellects (vyāvahārika-dṛṣṭi-ayogya). She is the unmanifested, mystical core of reality, realized solely through internal absorption.

सर्वैः — by all

Meaning

(i) One who is free from all limitations and adjuncts.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya navigates a critical non-dual philosophical absolute:

Absolute Freedom from Adjuncts: An Upādhi is a conditioning lens—like a piece of red glass that makes a clear crystal appear red. Space, time, names, forms, and elements are all cosmic lenses. She is Sarvopādhivinirmuktā because in Her pristine essential nature as Parabrahman, She stands completely free from all these attributes (धर्मसम्बन्धशून्या), remaining unconditioned and pure.

Word by word

यस्याः — of whom; whose

Meaning

(i) One who is the devoted spouse of Sadāśiva.

(ii) She remains always with Śiva in all three times.

(iii) This name establishes Her equality with, and inseparability from, Brahman while preserving the devotional image of Śiva and Śakti.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya elevations this past mundane human marital configurations to reveal cosmic physics:

The Eternal Fusion of Consciousness and Energy: This names the absolute, unbreakable dynamic law of non-duality. She (Śakti) possesses an unceasing, timeless vow (sada-vrata) to never separate Herself from Sadāśiva (pure, static consciousness). Energy cannot exist without consciousness, and consciousness cannot express itself without energy. They remain in an eternal, unbroken embrace.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya defines the structural transmission of grace:

The Mistress of the Lineage: सम्प्रदाय (Sampradāya) is the uninterrupted chain through which sacred wisdom is correctly and directly transmitted from master to disciple (samyak pradīyate). She is the absolute ruler and animating spirit behind this entire pedagogical pipeline, ensuring that the initiatory power stays alive and uncorrupted across generations.

The Guide to the Highest Goal: She is Sādhvī because Her operations are entirely aligned with uncorrupted cosmic order (Ṛta). For the practitioner, She acts as सद्गतिदायिनी (Sadgati-dāyinī) — the force that safely guides the soul along the upward path, ensuring they reach the ultimate destination of liberation without falling into spiritual deviation.

Bhāskararāya decodes one of the most guarded acoustic coordinates of high Śrīvidyā theology:

The Monosyllable of Kāmakalā: The vowel ई (Ī) is the phonetic seed-syllable that represents कामकला (Kāmakalā) — the primal, creative flash of divine desire where Shiva and Shakti recognize their union. It is the fourth transcendent state (Turya-svarūpa). She is the direct phonic reality of this single syllable, which contains the complete blueprint of creation within its resonance.

The Corporate Chain of Preceptors: The Guru lineage in Śrīvidyā is stratified into three distinct tiers: दिव्यौघ (Divyaugha — celestial masters), सिद्धौघ (Siddhaugha — perfected masters), and मानवौघ (Mānavaugha — human masters), initiating from Paramaśiva Himself. She is Gurumaṇḍalarūpiṇī because She is the continuous light running through this entire corporate chain, proving that every true guru is an execution of Her presence.

Beyond the Sensory Matrix: In internal alignment, कुल (Kula) denotes the network of the senses, the physical elements, and the structured system of the lower chakras. She is Kulottīrṇā because while She animates these systems, She simultaneously stands completely past them (atikrāntā). She represents the shoreless, unmanifested sky of pure consciousness (Akula) that remains untouched by material mechanics.

The Unified Adoration: Alternatively, it denotes that She is correctly approached and adored through a completely undivided, unified state of internal awareness (ekākāra), where the practitioner sheds all sense of fragmented tracking.

(i) One who is the form of māyā.

The Engine of Selective Concealment: Māyā is not a simple hallucination. She commands this operational filter to sustain the cosmic projection.

The Solar Honey: The Chāndogya Upaniṣad celebrates the sun as the divine honey of the cosmos (Adityo vai devamadhu). She is the living essence of this मधुमती विद्या (Madhumatī Vidyā), the high scriptural science that tracks this solar nectar.

The Internal Sweetness: In internal yoga, it represents Her presence within the ultimate sweet fluid that floods the channels during deep concentration.

The Softness of Grace: Her limbs and geometric lines are described as tender (sukumāra), reminding the practitioner that Her interaction with the universe is free from crude, heavy violence. गुरुपत्न्यभिन्ना। जगद्गुरोः शिवस्य पत्नी।

Word by word

गुरुः — guru; teacher

यस्याः — whose; of whom

शिवस्य — of Śiva

Meaning

(i) One who has affection for the Guru.

(ii) She has great love for Parameśvara, the great teacher of the world.

(iii) She is pleased with the teachers who initiate eligible disciples into Śrīvidyā and keep the worshipping tradition unbroken.

(iv) She is also understood as the consort of the Guru of every worshipper. This implies that the Guru's wife is to be treated as Śrīdevī herself; in this worship every lady is to be regarded as Śrīdevī.

(v) Guru can also mean Bṛhaspati, the teacher of the Devas; She has care for him also.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the foundational teacher-consort framework:

The Beloved of the Universal Master: Lord Śiva is the eternal, primordial जगद्गुरु (Jagadguru — teacher of the worlds). She is His beloved non-dual consort (Gurupriyā). Concurrently, this name establishes that She is deeply affectionate toward any true preceptor who correctly preserves and teaches the sacred lineage keys, holding them close to Her grace.

Nāma 723

स्वतन्त्रा

Samāsa-vigraha

स्वस्य तन्त्रं प्राधान्यं यस्यां सा।

स्वान्यात्मीयानि तन्त्राणि यस्याः सा।

कारकपारतन्त्र्यमन्तरेणैव सर्वकर्तृत्वात्।

स्वतन्त्राख्यनित्यातन्त्ररूपा।

स्व आत्मीयः स्वाधीनः परशिवस्तत्तन्त्रा तदधीना।

Word by word

स्वस्य — of herself

तन्त्राणि — tantras

यस्याः — whose; of whom

Meaning

(i) One who acts on Her own, without depending on others.

(ii) She does not require the help of others for any activity. She does not even need instruments; by Her mere will or declaration She acts.

(iii) She owns Her consort Parameśvara, and He owns Her; they mutually belong to each other.

(iv) She is in the form of the Nitya Tantra called Svatantra. This name may also be connected with the Svatantra mentioned in Soundaryalaharī.

(v) All tantras are ultimately Her own, because even worship of other deities is made possible only by the life-energy that is Śrīdevī.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the absolute metaphysical independence (Svātantrya) of the Śakti:

Absolute Sovereignty: She is Svatantrā because She operates with absolute freedom, entirely unconditioned by external factors or causal dependencies (कारकपारतन्त्र्यमन्तरेण सर्वकर्तृत्वात्). She rules Her own systems.

The Mirror of Shiva: Alternatively, स्व refers to Her own non-dual counterpart, Paramaśiva, meaning Her entire operational system is fully synchronized and dependent solely on Him, tracking Her onto the Svatantrā Nityā deity of the lunar calendar.

Nāma 724

सर्वतन्त्रेशी

Samāsa-vigraha

सर्वाणि चतुःषष्टिसंख्याकानि तन्त्राणीष्टे समर्थयतीति।

Word by word

सर्वाणि — all

Meaning

(i) One who is the head of all tantras.

(ii) She establishes and supports the sixty-four tantras and makes them meaningful.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, this confirms Her legislative mastery over all traditions:

The Overlord of the Sixty-Four Lineages: The Agamic universe features sixty-four primary textual systems and lineages (Catuḥṣaṣṭi-tantra). She is Sarvatantreśī because She sits at the absolute peak apex above all sixty-four books. They are merely partial, specialized charts of Her energy, drawing their functional authority exclusively from Her supreme command.

Nāma 725

दक्षिणामूर्तिरूपिणी

Samāsa-vigraha

शिवस्य दक्षिणाभिमुखी मूर्तिर्ब्रह्मनारायणादेरध्यापकत्वेन प्रसिद्धा। यस्या मन्त्रास्तन्त्रेषु प्रसिद्धाः स एव रूपमस्याः अस्तीति।

Word by word

शिवस्य — of Śiva

दक्षिणाभिमुखी — south-facing

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of Dakṣiṇāmūrti.

(ii) Dakṣiṇāmūrti teaches the principle of non-duality.

(iii) Śiva and Śrīdevī appear in individual forms, in the integrated form such as Ardhanārīśvara, and in forms where one is merged in the other. Śrīdevī is also understood as merged in the form of Dakṣiṇāmūrti.

(iv) The Dakṣiṇāmūrti idea continues in the following names.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya reveals a profound, identity equation crossing standard gender definitions:

The Soul of the Silent Teacher: Dakṣiṇāmūrti is Lord Śiva sitting in absolute silence under the banyan tree, instructing the ancient rishis through unuttered resonance. This name reveals that She is non-different from this supreme masculine teaching form. She is the internal illumination, the code, and the processing power that allows that silent instruction to break open inside the disciple's mind.

Nāma 726

सनकादिसमाराध्या

Samāsa-vigraha

सनकसनन्दनादिभिः सम्यगाराध्योपास्या।

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who is worshipped by Sanaka and other sages.

(ii) The four sages Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana and Sanatkumāra contemplated Śrīdevī in the form of Dakṣiṇāmūrti and received instruction from Śiva.

(iii) These sages are the mind-born sons of Brahmā, great yogins and highly knowledgeable disciples.

(iv) They are included in the lineage of teachers and are known in connection with the Samaya method of Śrīvidyā worship.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya tracks Her adoration across the highest levels of internal asceticism:

The Meditation of the Primeval Ascetics: Sages like Sanaka represent the absolute pinnacle of lifelong celibacy, internal detachment, and unshakeable absorption in Brahman. Their intense adoration (samārādhyā) indicates that She is not a deity sought merely for temporary worldly gain, but the ultimate, non-dual absolute targeted by the most advanced ascetics in existence.

Nāma 727

शिवज्ञानप्रदायिनी

Samāsa-vigraha

शिवविषयकं ज्ञानं प्रकर्षेण दत्ते।

शिवो ज्ञानप्रदायी यस्याः सा।

Word by word

प्रकर्षेण — excellently; fully

यस्याः — whose; of whom

Meaning

(i) One who bestows knowledge relating to Śiva.

(ii) Śiva means auspiciousness; She gives the knowledge of Brahman.

(iii) The pure and peaceful Śiva can be known only through Śrīdevī, His vibratory power.

(iv) It may also be understood that Śiva gives knowledge about Śrīdevī. This continues the Dakṣiṇāmūrti meaning of the previous name.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya outlines the ultimate crown of insight:

The Granting of Absolute Awakening: The individual soul can know many relative sciences, but it remains bound until it uncovers the true nature of Śiva (pure consciousness). She acts as Śivajñānapradāyinī, directly delivering this supreme, non-dual realization. She reveals Śiva, vanishing the illusion of separation and initiating final liberation.

Nāma 728

चित्कला

Samāsa-vigraha

चिदेव कला सच्चिदानन्दात्मनो ब्रह्मण एकदेश इव यस्यां सा।

अन्तःकरणोपाधिकं चैतन्यं निरुपाधिकायाश्चितः कला एकदेश इति।

Word by word

कला — part; digit; aspect

Meaning

(i) One who is with divine consciousness.

(ii) Cit means knowledge or consciousness, and kalā means a part.

(iii) Brahman cannot be fully objectified, but Sat, Cit and Ānanda are spoken of as its inseparable aspects. Here She is the Cit aspect.

(iv) The consciousness present in the inner self of the soul is described as a part of Brahman; She is that Cit-kalā.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya defines the relationship between the unconditioned absolute and internal awareness:

The Dynamic Ray of Awareness: While the absolute Brahman is completely unconditioned and still, Citkalā is that specialized, highly kinetic ray of awareness that steps down to illuminate the internal cognitive apparatus (antaḥkaraṇa-upādhika-caitanya). She is the active intelligence that allows living beings to process thought, perceive life, and sense existence.

Nāma 729

आनन्दकलिका

Samāsa-vigraha

आनन्द एव कलैकदेश इव यस्याः सा।

जीवगतानन्दैकदेशरूपा।

(स्वार्थे कः)।

Word by word

यस्याः — whose; of whom

Meaning

(i) One who is the bud of divine bliss.

(ii) As the consciousness of the soul is a part of Brahman-consciousness, the bliss of the soul is a part of Brahman-bliss.

(iii) She is the form of supreme bliss, Sat-cit-ānanda.

(iv) Kalikā means a bud. The bliss latent in the soul is like a bud that can, at the proper time, open into supreme bliss.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya maps the internal experience of joy inside bound souls:

The Blossom of Joy: The unconditioned bliss of Brahman is massive and shoreless. Inside individual living beings (Jīvas), this joy is experienced as a tiny, subtle fraction—a delicate bud of happiness (ānanda-aika-deśa-rūpā) that breaks open during moments of deep love or peace. She is that exact internal blossom of joy, waiting to expand into full cosmic realization.

Nāma 730

प्रेमरूपा

Samāsa-vigraha

प्रेम स्नेहो भक्तिरेव स्वरूपं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

प्रेम — love

यस्याः — whose; of whom

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of love.

(ii) The love or devotion of the devotees towards Her is indicated as Śrīdevī herself.

(iii) Love takes different names according to its object: devotion towards elders, love towards equals, affection towards children. She is present in all these forms.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya concludes this major sequence by defining the emotional essence of the absolute:

Pure Devotion Incarnate: She does not simply feel affection or receive love. Her entire essential substance is nothing but pure, unadulterated divine love itself (Prema-svarūpa). This love is the absolute emotional expression of non-duality—the intense attraction that pulls the fragment back into the whole, comforting the seeker that the heart of reality is pure love.

Nāma 731

प्रियङ्करी

Samāsa-vigraha

प्रियं करोतीति।

Word by word

प्रियं — dear; desired

Meaning

(i) One who grants what is dear to Her devotees.

(ii) She gives what devotees seek, according to their inner disposition, whether enjoyment or liberation.

(iii) As soul-consciousness, She causes interest in worldly objects through the senses, and also gives the knowledge that even this interest arises because of the Self.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya clarifies the cosmic allocation of Her benevolence:

The Engine of Universal Delight: She is Priyaṅkarī because Her dynamic operations are naturally formatted to project what is ultimately beneficial, pleasing, and evolutionary for all living beings. She does not design systemic cruelty; Her baseline nature works to convert the friction of existence into deep, soul-level comfort and alignment.

Nāma 732

नामपारायणप्रीता

Samāsa-vigraha

नामपारायणाभ्यां प्रीता।

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who is pleased with the recitation of Her names.

(ii) Here nāma may indicate this Sahasranāma itself. The fruits of such recitation are explained in the result section.

(iii) Different modes of pārāyaṇa are taught in the tradition and are regarded as secret and powerful means to approach Śrīdevī.

(iv) Laghustuti and Devī Bhāgavatam are cited in connection with the formation and recitation of sacred names.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the physics of acoustic dedication:

The Sonic Alignment: A Pārāyaṇa is not a casual, distracted chanting; it is the highly structured, continuous, and focused verbal layout of divine phonic names from start to finish. She is deeply pleased by this process because the systematic vibration of Her names clears the colored filters of the practitioner's mind, perfectly tuning their internal environment to receive Her light.

Nāma 733

नन्दिविद्या

Samāsa-vigraha

नन्दिनो नन्दिकेश्वरस्य विद्या तदुपासितविद्या।

Word by word

विद्या — knowledge; mantra

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of the mantra taught by Nandikeśvara.

(ii) Among the sages connected with Śrīvidyā, Nandi is also counted along with Manu, Candra, Kubera, Lopāmudrā, Agastya, Agni, Sūrya, Indra, Skanda, Śiva and others.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya tracks Her identity across the founding lineages of the tradition:

The Nandikeśvara Lineage: Within the structural history of Śrīvidyā, Lord Nandi stands as one of the premier master seers who received the core mantra directly from Shiva and formatted a highly revered operational tradition (Nandividyā). She is the literal phonic substance and target of this lineage, ensuring the protection of its initiatory keys.

Nāma 734

नटेश्वरी

Samāsa-vigraha

नटेश्वरस्येयमिति।

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the consort of Naṭeśa.

(ii) This means She is the consort of Naṭarāja, who dances in Chidambara.

(iii) Chidambara may mean the sacred place or the ether of the heart.

(iv) She dances together with Naṭeśa, as indicated in the Soundaryalaharī verse describing the dance of Śiva and Śakti.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya defines Her dynamic role in the dance of creation:

The Rhythm behind the Dancer: Lord Śiva as Naṭeśvara executes the cosmic dance of creation, preservation, and dissolution (Tāṇḍava). She is Naṭeśvarī — His non-dual dynamic energy. She provides the structural rhythm, the stage, and the kinetic power that allows the cosmic dance to unfold, remaining the silent witness to every movement.

Nāma 735

मिथ्याजगदधिष्ठाना

Samāsa-vigraha

मिथ्यारूपस्य जगतोऽधिष्ठानं भानाधिकरणं रजतस्येव शुक्तिः। (गुणत्रयापचयविवक्षया स्त्रीलिङ्गम्।)

जगदधिष्ठानरूपं ब्रह्मैव अनः प्राणो यस्याः सा।

Word by word

यस्याः — whose; of whom

Meaning

(i) One who is the substratum of the falsely appearing world.

(ii) Just as a shell is mistaken for silver until true knowledge arises, the changing universe appears on the real substratum, Śrīdevī as the Supreme Being.

(iii) Scriptural statements are cited to show that duality is ultimately illusory and that the Supreme alone is real.

(iv) This name can also be interpreted as She whose breath is Brahman, the support of the universe.

(v) In the tantric view, the universe is not different from Brahman, just as a pot is not different from clay; perceived difference is only apparent.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya navigates a critical, high-tier Advaita Vedānta non-dual equation:

The Reality behind the Appearance: In classical philosophy, an illusion requires a real base to appear—just as a silver illusion (rajata) requires the actual mother-of-pearl shell (śukti) beneath it. The material universe is mithyā (transient, relative, and non-permanent). She is Mithyājagadadhiṣṭhānā because She is the absolute, unchanging consciousness baseline that supports this entire changing projection, allowing it to be perceived.

Nāma 736

मुक्तिदा

Samāsa-vigraha

मुक्तिं मोक्षं ददातीति मुक्तिदा।

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who gives liberation.

(ii) The Purāṇas say that those desirous of freedom should seek refuge in Parvatī, Parameśvarī, the Self of all beings and of Śiva.

(iii) Those who worship the supreme Śakti, whether by regular or irregular methods, do not remain bound in saṃsāra; they are indeed liberated.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya defines the ultimate termination of individual lack:

The Dispenser of Ultimate Freedom: Worldly achievements provide localized, temporary transitions. She acts as Muktidā, directly bestowing the absolute gift of final spiritual liberation. She forcefully cuts the core ignorance that anchors the soul to the wheel of rebirth, returning the practitioner to their pristine state of baseline consciousness.

Nāma 737

मुक्तिरूपिणी

Samāsa-vigraha

मुक्तिरेव रूपमस्याः अस्तीति।

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the form of liberation itself.

(ii) Liberation is not merely an external result but the manifestation of one's own bliss when ignorance is removed.

(iii) The true nature of the Self is hidden by ignorance; when that ignorance goes, the self-bliss shines forth. She is that true bliss.

(iv) Knowledge does not create liberation; it reveals the Self that was veiled.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya constructs an immediate non-dual refinement to prevent structural duality:

Identity with Freedom: Lest a student think that She is an external entity who simply hands over a reward called liberation, this name establishes that Her very body is nothing but liberation itself (Mukti-svarūpa). Realizing Her person is identical to entering the state of unconditioned, boundless freedom.

Nāma 738

लास्यप्रिया

Samāsa-vigraha

लास्यं नर्तनं प्रियं यस्याः सा।

तालैर्नृत्यगीतयोः समकालपरिच्छेदो वा लयः।

तस्य करी कर्त्री।

Word by word

प्रियं — dear; desired

यस्याः — whose; of whom

Meaning

(i) One who is fond of dance.

(ii) The dance performed by women is called lāsya, while male dance is called tāṇḍava.

(iii) Śrīdevī Herself dances and is also pleased with the dance of others.

(iv) As in royal courts and temples, dance and music are offered before the Empress Śrīdevī. She is pleased by dance performed with rhythm, song and devotion.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the gentle, creative properties of Her energy:

The Joy of Harmonious Expression: While the masculine Tāṇḍava represents fierce, destructive kinetic velocity, लास्य (Lāsya) represents the highly refined, graceful, and harmonizing dance frequency associated with creation and nourishment. She is deeply affectionate toward this gentle expression, reflecting Her mode of uplifting the cosmos through pure grace.

Nāma 739

लयकरी

Samāsa-vigraha

लयश्चित्तावस्थाविशेषः।

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who causes absorption.

(ii) Laya is a special state of mind, greater than ordinary meditation.

(iii) When the mind becomes wholly absorbed in seeing, hearing or contemplation, it forgets everything else. Such absorption in the Supreme Being is granted by Her.

(iv) Laya also refers to the measured time of music and dance; She is that form also.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details three profound operational paths for this title:

Cosmic Dissolution: She safely draws the manifest universe back into its unmanifest source during the grand collapse.

Rhythmic Absorption: She acts as the soul of time-keeping (laya) that binds music and dance into harmony.

Mental Stillness: For the practitioner, She coordinates that unique, quiet state of consciousness (citta-avasthā-viśeṣa) where all cognitive ripples dissolve, leading to deep Samādhi.

Nāma 740

लज्जा

Samāsa-vigraha

या देवी सर्वभूतेषु लज्जारूपेण संस्थितेति स्मरणाल्लज्जा।

हृल्लेखाबीजस्वरूपा।

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of modesty.

(ii) Modesty or shyness is an important quality, especially of devoted women, and is described as a form of Śrīdevī.

(iii) The Saptashatī praises the Goddess abiding in all beings as modesty.

(iv) The word Hrīṃ is connected with modesty and is an important bīja of Śrīdevī. Thus lajjā also points cryptically to that bīja.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya elevates this past basic psychological formatting to reveal high mantric keys:

The Shield of Internal Discernment: As celebrated in the Devī Māhātmya, She resides in all living beings as the natural property of modesty (Lajjā), acting as an internal moral compass that restrains base, animalistic tendencies.

The Core Seed of the Heart: In secret Śrīvidyā grammar, Lajjā is a highly guarded code name for the supreme हृल्लेखा बीज (Hṛllekhā Bīja — the sound ह्रीं / Hrīṁ). She is the direct acoustic reality of this core sound, which serves as the cleansing engine of the heart center.

Nāma 741

रम्भादिवन्दिता

Samāsa-vigraha

रम्भोर्वश्यादिभिरप्सरोभिर्वन्दिता।

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who is adored by Rambhā and other celestial damsels.

(ii) From this name onwards the beautiful form of Śrīdevī is described in a series of names.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the cosmic scaling of Her aesthetic authority:

Sovereignty over Aesthetic Radiance: Celestial nymphs (apsaras) represent the peak expression of sensory attraction, grace, and vital beauty across the heavenly planes. Their continuous adoration at Her feet establishes Her status as the original source of all allure and kinetic charm. She coordinates the parameters of beauty while remaining untouched by sensory delusion.

Nāma 742

भवदावसुधावृष्टिः

Samāsa-vigraha

भवः संसार एव दावो वनवह्निस्तस्य शामकत्वात्सुधावृष्टिः पीयूषवर्षमिव।

भवः संसार एव दावोऽरण्यम्। तस्य पुङ्खानुपुङ्खतया उज्जीवनात्पीयूषवृष्टिरिव।

भवं परशिवं दत्ते वसु रत्नं धनं च धत्ते एतादृशी वृष्टिरिति त्रिपदं नाम वा।

Word by word

भवः — worldly existence

दत्ते — gives

नाम — name

Meaning

(i) One who is the rain of nectar falling on the forest-fire of worldly existence.

(ii) Bhava means worldly existence and dāva means forest fire. She is the nectar-rain that extinguishes that fire.

(iii) The name may also be split to mean She who grants Śiva, wealth and auspicious abundance.

(iv) For the great devotees of Śrīdevī, both enjoyment and liberation are available by Her grace.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya coordinates the alchemical transformations triggered by Her grace:

The Extinguisher of Rebirth: Under the primary track, the cyclical friction of worldly existence (Bhava) is a blazing forest fire (dāva) burning the bound soul. Her downpour of non-dual nectar (sudhā-vṛṣṭi) cools this internal panic.

The Nourisher of Spirit: Alternatively, the world is a parched forest; Her nectar acts as the refreshing irrigation that brings dead spiritual channels back to life. Under the split-word key, She functions as a continuous downpour that systematically delivers the direct realization of Lord Śiva alongside all material assets.

Nāma 743

पापारण्यदवानला

Samāsa-vigraha

पापान्येवारण्यानि दुःखजनकत्वात्। तेषां दवानल इव नाशकत्वात्।

पापारण्यानां दवानलो यस्या नाम सा।

पापारण्यानां ये दवाः दावाग्नयो नाशनोपायभूता उपास्त्यादयस्तेषां अनान् प्राणान् लाति आदत्ते तान् जीवयतीति।

Word by word

नाम — name

Meaning

(i) One who is the forest fire that burns down the forest of sins.

(ii) She destroys sins just as a forest fire consumes a forest.

(iii) Sins such as prārabdha, sañcita and āgāmi cannot be destroyed merely by worldly enjoyment; by Her grace and true knowledge they are ruined.

(iv) Remembering the feet of the supreme Śakti is taught as the highest expiation for sins committed knowingly or unknowingly.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya maps Her aggressive corrective purification:

The Incineration of Accumulated Karmas: Sins (pāpa) resemble a dense, dark, overgrown jungle because they form an interconnected tangle that creates existential blockages and blocks out the light of the Self. She acts as Davānalā—a high-velocity fire that leaves no branch unburned, reducing the seeker's historical load of negative impressions (saṁskāras) to pure ash.

Nāma 744

दौर्भाग्यतूलवातूला

Samāsa-vigraha

दौर्भाग्यमेव तूलं कार्पासं तस्य वातूल इव वात्येव दूरं निरासिकेति।

दौर्भाग्यं तूलं येषां ते दौर्भाग्यतूलाः दौर्भाग्यस्य तूलस्येव निरासका धर्मविशेषाः। अत एव ते धर्मा एव वातूले गौण्यावृत्त्या तेन दौर्भाग्यतूलः वातूला यस्याः सकाशात् सा।

दौर्भाग्यनिरासकानि कर्माणि यस्याः सकाशादुद्भवन्ति यस्याः सम्बन्धीनि वा सा।

Word by word

यस्याः — whose; of whom

Meaning

(i) One who is the cyclone that drives away the cotton-bundles of misfortune.

(ii) Misfortune from actions of previous births may appear huge, like bundles of cotton, but Her force scatters it like a strong wind.

(iii) The actions that remove such misfortune arise from Her and are connected with Her grace.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the immediate shift in internal and external alignment:

The Cyclone of Auspiciousness: Misfortune (daurbhāgya) has no solid ontological reality; it is merely a weightless collection of negative conditions, like cotton flakes (tūla). She acts as a powerful whirlwind (vātūlā), blowing these scattered blocks entirely out of the practitioner's path, replacing structural obstacles with instant alignment.

Nāma 745

जराध्वान्तरविप्रभा

Samāsa-vigraha

जरैव ध्वान्तमन्धकारं तस्य नाशकत्वाद्रवेः प्रभेव।

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who removes the darkness of old age by Her light.

(ii) Childhood, youth and old age belong to the body, not to the eternal Self.

(iii) When the knowledge that body and soul are different arises, the fear of old age and death is removed.

(iv) She is like the sunlight that removes the darkness called old age.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya purges this name of simple superficial external physical formatting:

The Ray of Timeless Vitality: Jarā represents the dark creeping rust of time, decay, mental fog, and biological slowing down that veils the body's internal radiance. She is Raviprabhā — the blinding, rejuvenating morning sun ray that cuts through this internal stagnation, restoring the pristine, timeless vitality of pure consciousness inside the subtle matrix.

Nāma 746

भाग्याब्धिचन्द्रिका

Samāsa-vigraha

भाग्यलक्षणस्याब्धेरुल्लासकत्वाच्चन्द्रिका कौमुदीव।

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the moonlight that illumines the ocean of good fortune.

(ii) Good fortune comes from virtue done in previous births. When others recognise a person's good fortune, the joy swells like the ocean under moonlight.

(iii) By Her compassion, She makes the good fortune of Her devotees expand and become recognised.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya decodes the internal dynamics of spiritual expansion:

The Tidal Surge of Grace: When the full moon shines, the ocean naturally experiences massive gravitational tidal surges. Similarly, when Her moon-like light (Candrikā) rises inside the practitioner's consciousness, the dormant ocean of inner spiritual and material merit (bhāgya) expands dramatically, flooding the entire system with active prosperity.

Nāma 747

भक्तचित्तकेकिघनाघना

Samāsa-vigraha

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the cloud that excites the peacocks which are the minds of Her devotees.

(ii) Just as peacocks dance when they see dark rainclouds, devotees' minds rejoice on seeing Śrīdevī.

(iii) Her continuous life-work nourishes the devotees spiritually, like rainclouds sustaining life.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya tracks the emotional and structural relief of the spiritual heart:

The Relief of the Monsoon: Peacocks suffer during the hot summer months and burst into ecstatic dance the exact moment they hear the first low thunder of a dark monsoon rain-cloud (ghanāghana). The devotee's mind, parched by the anxieties of worldly life, experiences this exact cooling relief upon Her entry, bursting into natural, joyous spiritual alignment.

Nāma 748

रोगपर्वतदम्भोलिः

Samāsa-vigraha

Word by word

पर्वताः — mountains

Meaning

(i) One who is the thunderbolt that strikes the mountain of diseases.

(ii) Diseases are compared to mountains, and Śrīdevī to Indra's thunderbolt that can shatter them.

(iii) This recalls the name Sarvavyādhi-praśamanī, the pacifier of all diseases.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya defines Her absolute therapeutic precision:

The Shattering of Disease Vectors: Chronic physical illnesses and deep-seated subconscious mental complexes behave like massive, unmoving stone mountains (parvata), blocking path progression. She is the piercing, high-voltage diamond thunderbolt (Dambholi — Indra's Vajra) that strikes these structural densities, shattering the root vectors of disease instantly.

Nāma 749

मृत्युदारुकुठारिका

Samāsa-vigraha

मृत्युरूपदारूणां कुठारा इव।

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the axe that cuts down the tree of death.

(ii) Death and related pains grow like a tree rooted in birth and time; She cuts it down like an axe.

(iii) A devotee who firmly thinks, "I worship Śrīdevī and will gain liberation," is freed from the fear of death.

(iv) Therefore death is aptly compared to a tree and Śrīdevī to the axe.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the termination of systemic mortality:

The Cutter of the Rebirth Trunk: Physical death (Mṛtyu) is the heavy, stubborn log framework that keeps the soul trapped in the engine of rebirth. As Kuṭhārikā, She strikes directly at the base root of this wood, slicing the illusion of mortality cleanly away and anchoring the practitioner in non-dual permanence.

Nāma 750

महेश्वरी

Samāsa-vigraha

महती च सेश्वरी च।

Word by word

महती — great

Meaning

(i) One who is the supreme sovereign.

(ii) This name differs from the earlier Māheśvarī by the long and short form of the vowel, and therefore is not a mere repetition.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya concludes this structural sequence by establishing Her premier position over cosmic leadership:

Sovereignty Past the Lesser Gods: A local ruler governs a territory; the secondary deities govern specific cosmic departments. She is Maheśvarī because Her sovereign rule (Īśvaritva) is completely unbounded (Mahat). She stands as the absolute, non-dual empress who formats the laws of nature, directs the motion of universes, and acts as the supreme consort of Maheśvara, sealing all cosmic authority directly to Her person.

Nāma 751

महाकाली

Samāsa-vigraha

महती च सा काली च।

महाकालस्य स्त्री।

Word by word

महती — great

सा — she

काली — Kālī

महाकालस्य — of Mahākāla

Meaning

(i) One who is great and in the form of Kāli.

(ii) Kāli may mean She who determines time; Mahākāli determines even the time of Yama, the deity of death.

(iii) She is worshipped as Mahākāli, the consort of Mahākāla, and as the deity of the first story of Saptashatī.

(iv) In Her fierce form She appears dark. Death itself is explained as an act of compassion that temporarily releases beings from the bondage of action and prepares the way for peace and future growth.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya reveals the non-dual baseline tracking time and energy:

The Devourer of Time: Mahākāla is the supreme aspect of consciousness that dissolves the entire universe at the end of an epoch. She is Mahākālī because She is the dynamic kinetic capacity that acts as the container and consumer of even that ultimate time-principle. She marks the final absolute rest state where all temporal mutations return to stillness.

Nāma 752

महाग्रासा

Samāsa-vigraha

महानपरिमितो ग्रासः कवलो यस्याः सा।

Word by word

ग्रासः — mouthful; devouring

यस्याः — whose; of whom

Meaning

(i) One who is the great devourer.

(ii) The Upaniṣad speaks of Brahmins and Kṣatriyas as food and death as condiment for the Supreme.

(iii) At dissolution She, as the supreme consuming power, swallows the universe and the thirty-six tattvas.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya defines Her absolute ease during cosmic reabsorption:

The Single Morsel of Creation: During the grand dissolution (mahāpralaya), the creation of names, forms, elements, and structural spatial coordinates is not dissolved slowly or with friction. She takes the entire multi-dimensional cosmos as a single, effortless mouthful (grāsa), absorbing it completely back into Her non-dual unmanifested matrix.

Nāma 753

महाशना

Samāsa-vigraha

महच्चराचरकर्मकत्वादशनं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

यस्याः — whose; of whom

Meaning

(i) One who is a great eater.

(ii) Continuing the previous name, She consumes the entire animate and inanimate universe.

(iii) This name differs from the earlier Mahāsanā and should not be confused with it.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, this reinforces Her ultimate consuming authority:

The Absolute Appetite: Complementing Mahāgrāsā, She is Mahāśanā because Her ultimate consumption (aśana) encompasses the entire created universe. Nothing is left over as waste matter outside Her field; every single spark of objective appearance is digested, showing Her status as the unified final terminal for all cosmic properties.

Nāma 754

अपर्णा

Samāsa-vigraha

पर्णं पतनमिति नैरुक्तात्पतनरहितेति।

पर्णमप्यदनीयत्वेन न विद्यते यस्याः सा।

Word by word

यस्याः — whose; of whom

Meaning

(i) One who is without debt, or one who ate not even a leaf.

(ii) She gives more than devotees expect and is therefore not indebted to them.

(iii) As Pārvatī, while performing penance to marry Śiva, She did not eat even a leaf; hence the name Aparṇā.

(iv) The name may also mean one without falling or decline.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the foundational asceticism and non-dual perfection of this name:

The Pinnacle of Tapas: Historically, during Her intense tapas to fuse with Shiva, She abandoned consuming even fallen leaves (parṇa).

The Fallless Substratum: Under the etymological track, parṇa denotes falling (patana); She is entirely free from falling into spatial or temporal degradation.

The Debtless Absolute: She has no outstanding liabilities or cosmic debts (ṛṇa), existing completely secure in Her independent status.

Nāma 755

चण्डिका

Samāsa-vigraha

अभक्तेषु कोपनत्वात् चण्डयतीति।

Word by word

अभक्तेषु — towards non-devotees

Meaning

(i) One who is fierce or angry.

(ii) She is angry with those who lack devotion.

(iii) Anger is also described as a characteristic of Brahman in certain scriptural passages.

(iv) In Saptashatī the combined form of Mahākāli, Mahālakṣmī and Mahāsarasvatī is called Caṇḍikā.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the active mechanics of Her protective wrath:

The Fierce Filter of Justice: Her anger is not a mundane psychological distortion. She is Caṇḍikā because She expresses an intense, high-velocity defensive fury (caṇḍatva) directed specifically at unrighteous entities and stubborn internal blockages (abhaktas). This fierce light tears down the structures of ego, providing the necessary shocks to realign the soul.

Nāma 756

चण्डमुण्डासुरनिषूदिनी

Samāsa-vigraha

चण्डश्च मुण्डश्च, तौ च तावसुरौ च, तौ निषूदयतीति।

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who destroyed the demons Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa.

(ii) In the form of Kālī, She destroyed the demons Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa of the group of Śumbha and Niśumbha; hence She was named Cāmuṇḍā.

(iii) Other Purāṇic explanations also connect the name Cāmuṇḍā with the slaying of demons and the carrying of their heads.

(iv) This name recalls one of the forms among the eight mothers.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya moves this historical battle into internal psychological coordinates:

The Extraction of Passion and Delusion: In the internal battlefield of the mind, चण्ड represents the violent force of aggressive passion (Rajas), and मुण्ड represents the low, stubborn weight of intellectual blindness and delusion (Tamas). As Niṣūdinī, She extracts these twin root distortions from the subconscious channels, freeing the practitioner's path.

Nāma 757

क्षराक्षरात्मिका

Samāsa-vigraha

क्षराण्यनियतसंख्यान्यक्षराणि वर्णानि आत्मा स्वरूपं यस्याः सा।

क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते। तदुभयमात्मा स्वरूपं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

वर्णानि — letters

आत्मा — self; essence

यस्याः — whose; of whom

क्षरः — perishable

सर्वाणि — all

Meaning

(i) One whose form is both the perishable and the imperishable.

(ii) It may mean She is the form of countless letters or syllables, since mantras are formed from letters.

(iii) It may also mean She is the Self of both kṣara, the changing beings, and akṣara, the unchanging principle.

(iv) Thus She is the one and many, the source of mantra and the basis of all beings.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya coordinates this directly with the master taxonomy of the Bhagavad Gītā (Puruṣottama Yoga):

The Encompasser of Perishable and Imperishable: Kṣara represents the changing, material world of moving elements; Akṣara represents the still, changeless, and hidden spiritual witness (Kūṭastha). She is Kṣarākṣarātmikā because both conditions are expressions of Her non-dual body, acting as the bridge that synthesizes form and formlessness.

Nāma 758

सर्वलोकेशी

Samāsa-vigraha

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who is the ruler of all worlds.

(ii) All lokas are under Her authority; She is their sovereign mistress.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya outlines the unbounded scope of Her legislative throne:

Universal Imperial Sovereignty: Her administrative authority is not bounded by a single solar system or isolated dimension. She rules over the complete multi-dimensional network of the fourteen operational worlds (sarva-loka), directing their laws of karma and evolutionary paths with neutral accuracy.

Nāma 759

विश्वधारिणी

Samāsa-vigraha

Meaning

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya details the physics of cosmic suspension:

The Structural Pillar of Existence: The universe does not hang in a vacuum by chance. She is Viśvadhāriṇī because Her dynamic energy field acts as the permanent, invisible structural support that holds planetary spheres, gravity metrics, and spatial dimensions perfectly in place, preventing cosmic collapse.

Nāma 760

त्रिवर्गदात्री

Samāsa-vigraha

त्रयाणां धर्मार्थकामानां वर्गः समूहः। (त्रिवर्गो धर्मकामार्थैश्चतुर्वर्गः समोक्षकैरित्यमरः)। तस्य दात्री।

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

Bhāskararāya outlines Her balanced coordination of earthly life:

The Organization of Earthly Aspiration: Before a soul is ready for final liberation (Mokṣa), it requires balanced evolution across the three mundane planes: धर्म (moral alignment), अर्थ (material stability), and काम (refined desire). She systematically dispenses the resources for this triple framework (trivarga), ensuring Her children do not experience unnatural lack during their earthly journey.

Nāma 761

Samāsa-vigraha

Word by word

Meaning

(i) One who is supremely fortunate and bestows auspicious affluence.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara*, Bhāskararāya defines the internal components of भग (Bhaga):

The Six Divine Splendors: Classical lexicon rules define Bhaga as a corporate set of six attributes: absolute wealth, virtue, fame, beauty, wisdom, and effortless intent. She is Subhagā because She contains these traits in their most refined condition.

The Solar Engine: Alternatively, She is the inner consciousness that gives the sun (Bhaga) its brilliant capacity to illuminate worlds.

Nāma 762

त्र्यम्बका

Samāsa-vigraha

यस्याः — whose; of whom

Meaning

(i) One who is three-eyed.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya decodes the structural vision and parental priority built into this title:

The Vision Past Linear Time: Her three eyes correspond to the Sun, the Moon, and Fire, scanning past, present, and future simultaneously.

The Parent of the Trinity: Under the second precise track, अम्बका means mother. She is Tryambakā because She is the original maternal source (Ambikā) that gives birth to and formats the entire administrative trinity of the cosmos—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra.

Nāma 763

त्रिगुणात्मिका

Samāsa-vigraha

त्रिगुणात्मिका सत्त्वरजस्तमोरूपगुणत्रयसाम्यविग्रहा।

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who is in the form of the three guṇas: sattva, rajas and tamas.

(ii) Since the three deities are connected with these three qualities, She includes them all.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details Her identity with primordial nature (Mūlaprakṛti):

The Matrix of Material Form: Before the universe is structured, energy exists as a perfectly balanced, unmanifested equilibrium of the three qualities (guṇas). She is Triguṇātmikā because Her manifest body forms the very fabric of this triadic matrix, directing how light (Sattva), movement (Rajas), and mass (Tamas) combine to weave the material universe.

Nāma 764

स्वर्गापवर्गदा

Samāsa-vigraha

क्षयिष्णु सुखं वर्गः। नित्यं तु सुखमपवर्गः। तदुभयं दत्ते इति।

Word by word

दत्ते — gives

Meaning

(i) One who bestows heaven and liberation.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya clarifies the transactional alignment of experiences:

Fulfillment of All Degrees of Joy: Svarga represents the temporary, structural rewards achieved through virtuous action in the higher planes. Apavarga represents the permanent, non-dual bliss of final awakening. She acts as the singular portal for both paths, giving the appropriate worldly experience to the relative seeker and absolute liberation to the advanced ascetic.

Nāma 765

शुद्धा

Samāsa-vigraha

Word by word

Word meanings are read directly from the samāsa expression above.

Meaning

(i) One who is ever pure.

(ii) She is free from the impurity called ignorance.

(iii) In truth She is the form of knowledge.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya strips this of simple moral definitions to reveal ontological purity:

Untouched by Cosmic Ignorance: Material entities gather stains and undergo decay due to time and contact. She is Śuddhā because Her essential nature stands completely free from the ultimate stain—आविद्यकमालिन्य (āvidyaka-mālinya — the structural rust of cosmic ignorance or illusion). She remains eternally pristine, clear, and unblemished.

Nāma 766

जपापुष्पनिभाकृतिः

Samāsa-vigraha

जपापुष्पनिभा ओड्रपुष्पेण तुल्या आकृतिः स्वरूपं यस्याः सा।

Word by word

आकृतिः — form

यस्याः — whose; of whom

Meaning

(i) One whose form is like the hibiscus flower.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya maps this vibrant color frequency within high-level visual concentration:

The Effulgence of Kinetic Grace: The hibiscus flower possesses a unique, intensely deep red radiance. This visual profile represents the concentrated energy of विमर्शशक्ति (Vimarśa-śakti — active self-awareness) overflowing with creative compassion. Meditating on this crimson geometry burns away internal dark lethargy, realigning the practitioner's channels with dynamic clarity.

Nāma 767

ओजोवती

Samāsa-vigraha

ओजः अष्टमधातुः इन्द्रियसामर्थ्यं तेजः बलम् दीप्तिः च अस्यां सन्तीति।

Word by word

ओजः — vital energy

बलम् — strength

दीप्तिः — radiance

Meaning

(i) One who possesses ojas, the vitality of the body.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya details the neuro-biological mapping of this title:

It acts as the root of immune resilience, sensory capacity, and mental brilliance. She is the internal structural intelligence that animates this vital reserve, keeping life vibrant.

Bhāskararāya anchors this directly in the profound declarations of the Taittirīya Upaniṣad (Satyaṁ Jñānam Anantaṁ Brahma):

The Absolute Identity of Spirit: Her essential substance consists of the core triad that defines the absolute reality—Existence-Truth (Satya), Luminous Awareness (Jñāna), and Boundless Bliss (Ananda). Bhāskararāya notes the corrective physics: to those who turn away from Her light, reality appears as fragmented friction; to those who recognize Her, She opens the gates of absolute joy.

The Equilibrium of Consciousness and Energy: सामरस्य (Sāmarasya) describes a state of chemical and spiritual equilibrium where two elements fuse so perfectly that they cannot be separated—like water mixed with milk. Shiva (consciousness) and Shakti (energy) exist in this exact condition of balanced, non-dual fusion. She is Parāyaṇā because She is permanently anchored at this peak junction point, serving as the ultimate refuge where the seeker's individual duality is dissolved into the whole.

The Unbroken Chain of Creative Rays: She wears the entire network of the sixty-four cultural arts (catuḥ-ṣaṣṭhi-kalā), the digits of lunar time, and the operational phases of element evolution as a continuous, beautiful garland (mālā). Absolute Morphological Freedom: Alternatively, She is Kāmarūpiṇī because She possesses the absolute freedom to project and assume any physical or geometric form whatsoever (yatheccha-rūpā) to guide and protect Her devotees.

The Reservoir of the Non-Dual Nectar: The word शेवधि (Śevadhi) denotes an inexhaustible, highly guarded divine treasure house. She is Rasaśevadhi because She is the absolute reservoir that holds the infinite, sweet nectar of spiritual immortality (ब्रह्मामृत) generated within the Sahasrāra crown center. Finding Her presence gives the practitioner immediate, permanent access to this source of unconditioned joy, concluding the 800-name milestone with absolute satisfaction.

The Essence of Brahman: Alternatively, She is continually nourished and amplified by absolute virtues, the nectar of Brahman-bliss (brahma-rasa), and the spiritual realizations of realized seers, remaining absolute without decay.

Bhāskararāya constructs an immediate non-dual paradox following Mūrtā:

The Subtle Substratum: While She is the visible object (Mūrtā), She is simultaneously Amūrtā — the formless, invisible sky of air and ether (ākāśa) and the unquintupled, subtle elemental seeds (tanmātras). She confirms that the unmanifest vacuum and the dense world are waves of a single energy field.

Nāma 815

अनित्यतृप्ता

Samāsa-vigraha

अनित्यैरेवोपचारैस्तृप्तेति पञ्चाक्षरं नाम भक्तिमात्रप्रियत्वात्।

अनिति श्वसतीति जीवोऽनितिपदार्थः। तै: अतृप्ता।

इति एवंप्रकारेण अतृप्ता न तृप्ता न भवतीति न। (ईदृशः प्रकारो नास्ति येन तृप्ता न स्यात्। अपि तु सर्वैरपि प्रकारैस्तृप्तैव)।

Word by word

तृप्ता — satisfied

Meaning

(i) One who is satisfied even by impermanent offerings.

(ii) Since She is pleased by devotion alone, even simple and temporary offerings satisfy Her.

(iii) Another interpretation says there is no manner in which She is not satisfied; She is always fulfilled by every sincere mode of worship.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya decodes the transactional dynamics of simple devotion:

Sincerity over Opulence: She does not demand permanent, impossible physical monuments; She is perfectly satisfied by transient, fleeting daily offerings (anitya-upacāra) if driven by pure devotion.

The Double Negation: Under the logical track, it is impossible for Her to experience lack; She remains fully satisfied across every parameter and condition in existence.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya maps the historical and philosophical accuracy of this title:

The Absolute Vow: Her essential code of operation is absolute truth (Satya).

The Power of the Seed-Syllable: Under the historical track, She references a mute Brahmin (Satyavrata) who accidentally vibrated the primary wisdom seed-syllable ऐं (Aiṁ) out of fear, instantly unlocking Her presence and transforming into a master poet, proving the immediate responsiveness of Her sound keys.

Untouched by the Three Tenses: Satya is defined as that reality which can never be contradicted, altered, or negated across the past, present, or future (kālatrayābādhya). Every material object shifts and fails; She is Satyarūpā because Her baseline consciousness remains constant across all universal transitions.

The Perfection of Clever Grace: While the literal grammatical derivation means "thoroughly burned," the philosophical meaning denotes a highly refined, brilliant capacity of mind (चातुर्यशीला). She is Vidagdhā because Her consciousness manages the trillions of structural calculations required to run the multiverse with flawless, sharp, and graceful precision, leaving no room for operational error.

अनर्घ्येति दीर्घान्तपाठे आसमन्ताद्व्याप्तं यत्कैवल्यमिति वा पदम्/फलम्।

न विद्यते कैवल्यं यस्मात्तदकैवल्यमीदृशं यत्पदमिति वा पदम्/फलम्।

(i) One who grants the priceless state or fruit of liberation.

(iii) She bestows the immeasurable fruit of absolute freedom.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya defines the definitive ceiling of spiritual reward:

The Priceless Gift: Worldly gains have price tags and expire over time. She is Padadāyinī of कैवल्य (Kaivalya — absolute, unconditioned non-dual liberation). This state is Anarghya (priceless) because it cannot be bought with material currency, marking the absolute end of all individual lack and limitation.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya clarifies the sound mechanics of praise:

The Resonance of Realignment: She does not seek public praise to satisfy an ego. She is Stotrapriyā because when a practitioner recites a hymn (stotra), the poetic metrics and focused language gather their scattered mental energies. This process realigns their subtle nervous system, making it easy for Her grace to flood their consciousness.

Every word of adoration, every pure intent, and the capacity to praise are expressions of Her own energy field.

Bhāskararāya notes an advanced track where Śruti means the numeral four: Her glory is perfectly distributed across the four foundational levels of speech (Parā, Paśyantī, Madhyamā, Vaikharī).

She is Manasvinī because Her cosmic mind operates with absolute, unrestricted freedom (स्वतन्त्रतया तिष्ठति). Her intent (Icchā-śakti) is independent, directing the laws of nature without being bound by them.

The Geometry of Absolute Benevolence: She is Maṅgalākṛtiḥ because Her very shape is composed of pure auspiciousness. परं प्रकृष्टं मोदमानन्दमासमन्ताद्रातीति।

परमाण्युदानि जलानि यस्मिन्स परमोदः समुद्रः, स च प्रकृते भवसमुद्ररूपः, तस्यारा आयुधविशेषो यस्याः सा।

The Gateway of the Refined Mind: The scripture states, "Manasaivānudraṣṭavyam" ("Through the mind alone is the Self to be realized"). While the absolute absolute is past the senses, it is discovered when the mind becomes perfectly clear, still, and reflective. She is Manomayī because She acts as the very substance of this highly purified, refined intellect, functioning as the direct gateway to non-dual awakening.

This imagery shows Her vast containment of the planets. As the consort of Shiva who bears the matted hair of space, She coordinates the cosmic fields with perfect balance.

विशिष्य माति निष्कृष्य प्रमां जनयतीति विमानो वेदस्तत्र प्रतिपाद्यतया तिष्ठतीति वा।

विशिष्टेषु वेदाविरुद्धेषु मानेषु प्रमाणेषु धर्मब्रह्मरूपेण तिष्ठतीति।

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya delivers a deep Vedāntic analysis:

Established in the Unmeasurable: While human eyes map Her onto a celestial vehicle (vimāna), the high non-dual interpretation reveals that She is Vimānasthā because She stands permanently anchored within that absolute Brahman which is completely free from measurement or limitation (विगतं मानं यस्य). Concurrently, She resides at the core of the Vedas (Vimāna) as the ultimate truth they reveal.

She is Vajriṇī because She is the living embodiment of this unyielding law, holding the ultimate diamond power to shatter egoic deviations.

Under the operational key, She acts as the supreme queen (Īśvarī) governing those radical practitioners who follow the left-hand path (Vāmakas), using intense methods to realign their awareness.

Meaning

(i) One who loves the five kinds of sacrifices.

(ii) Different scriptures list the five sacrifices differently: Vedic sacrifices, Smriti sacrifices, Pancharatra practices, Kulagama forms, Nitya Tantra forms, and the Agnihotra-related five offerings.

(iii) She is fond of all these forms of yajna.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the daily alignment of energy:

The Harmony of Daily Sacrifice: The scripture mandates the Pañca-Mahā-Yajñas (sacrifice to the absolute, to ancestors, to deities, to humans, and to animals) to clear existential debts and balance the earth space. She is Pañcayajñapriyā because this daily practice keeps human activity in harmony with the cosmos, turning routine life into a field of pure devotion.

Nāma 947

पञ्चप्रेतमञ्चाधिशायिनी

Samāsa-vigraha

ब्रह्मादयश्चत्वारः प्रेताः पादाः। सदाशिवाख्यः प्रेतः फलकमेतादृशं मञ्चं पर्यङ्कमधिशेते।

Word by word

प्रेताः — corpses

पञ्चप्रेतमञ्चाधिशायिनी। — component of the name

Meaning

(i) One who reclines on a couch made of five corpses.

(ii) To show that She is greater than the five cosmic functions, the performers of those functions are treated as the legs and plank of Her couch. Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra and Eshvara are the four legs, and Sadashiva is the plank or sheet.

(iii) Without their Shaktis they cannot act; therefore they are described as corpses. This bed is praised in Bhairavayamala, Lalita Stavaratna, Soundaryalahari, Rudrayamala and other texts.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya delivers one of the most celebrated and profound iconographic analyses of the tradition:

The Supreme Throne past the Five Functions: The couch where She rests at the center of the royal chamber is constructed out of the five cosmic administrators: ब्रह्मा (Creation), विष्णु (Preservation), रुद्र (Dissolution), and ईश्वर (Concealment) serve as the four vertical legs, while सदाशिव (Grace) forms the flat seating plank. Without Her dynamic energy field, these five deities are inert like corpses (preta). She sits above them, demonstrating Her status as the supreme, non-dual source that gives life to cosmic functions.

Bhāskararāya details the structural placement of Her energy:

The Power of the Fifth Order: Within the administrative framework, She is Pañcamī because She is the dynamic consort of the absolute fifth principle—Sadāśiva (the Lord of Grace). In the specialized vocabulary of Agamic practice, She represents the critical fifth element—आनन्द (Ananda — supreme non-dual bliss) — which functions as the crown energy that completes the purification process.

She is the absolute Īśvarī (empress) who designs and governs their laws, formatting how gravity, fluid dynamics, heat exchange, atmospheric friction, and spatial containment operate across the macrocosmic grid.

In the internal alignment matrix, they correspond perfectly to the five elements: Earth, Space, Air, Fire, and Water. She is Pañcasaṅkhyopacāriṇī because when a practitioner performs this five-fold worship (pañcopacāra), they are systematically offering the entire element fabric of the cosmos back into Her non-dual light, completing the loop of realization.

बिन्दुतर्पणसन्तुष्टा

Samāsa-vigraha

बिन्दौ सर्वानन्दमये चक्रे ब्राह्मणादिवर्णचतुष्टयकर्तृकेण तर्पणेन सम्यक्तुष्टा।

क्षीराज्यमध्वासवबिन्दुकरणकेन वा तर्पणेन सम्यक्तुष्टा।

Word by word

बिन्दुतर्पणसन्तुष्टा। — component of the name

Meaning

(i) One satisfied by tarpana at the Bindu.

(ii) The Bindu is the Sarvanandamaya Chakra, and offerings there please Her.

(iii) Tarpana with milk, ghee, honey, wine or other prescribed offerings is also indicated.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya unpacks the secret internal and ritual operations of the lineage:

The Alchemy of the Center Point: Externally, this denotes offering drops (bindu) of milk, honey, or consecrated liquids into the central hub of the Yantra. Internally, Bindu refers to the absolute central point of the Sahasrāra crown. When the practitioner drives the internal energy up to this center, it melts the absolute nectar of immortality. Offering this nectar back into the point satisfies Her, stabilizing the system.

Samāsa-vigraha

Word by word

जा — born; manifested

पूर्वजा। — component of the name

Meaning

(i) One who is born or manifested first.

(ii) She is prior to all manifestation.

(iii) She is the first and original principle.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya clarifies Her chronological priority over creation:

The Primordial Manifestation: Before elements consolidate and before the secondary creators take their stations, She is the very first wave of manifestation (Pūrvajā) emerging out of the absolute unmanifest silence. She is the first ray of dawn, setting the template for everything that follows.

त्रिपुराम्बिका। — component of the name

Meaning

(ii) The three cities may be the three states of experience.

(iii) She is the mother of the jiva who identifies with those three states.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya details the structural hierarchy of human experience:

The Parent of the Three States: The "three cities" (tripura) are the three everyday states of human awareness: जाग्रत (Waking), स्वप्न (Dreaming), and सुषुप्ति (Deep Sleep). She is Ambikā (the mother) to this entire triad. She generates and supports these states, serving as the hidden fourth space (Turīya) that anchors them.

Meaning

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya details the geometric and physical locks of the Śrīvidyā tradition:

The Ten Energy Seals: Mudrās are precise physical gestures and internal seals (running from Sarvasaṅkṣobhiṇī up to Sarvatrikhaṇḍā) that match the nine enclosures of the Śrī Yantra. They are not symbolic dances. They act as precise energetic keys that lock the practitioner's nervous system into alignment, opening the channels to receive Her grace.

Command over the Fifth Circle: Within the anatomy of the Śrī Yantra, Tripurāśrī is the specific administrative deity placed in charge of the fifth enclosure. She is the ultimate source back behind this goddess, directing the distribution of wealth and spiritual merit.

The Seal of Awareness: Physically, She manifests as the iconic hand gesture where the index finger touches the thumb, forming a complete circuit that symbols individual soul merging with universal spirit. Internally, She acts as the force that dispenses intense spiritual joy (mudam) the exact moment pure knowledge (jñāna) flashes open inside the mind.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya delivers the definitive epistemological filter for Her presence:

The Gate of Awakening: She cannot be captured by emotional manipulation, mechanical rituals, or dry intellectual logic. She is Jñānagamyā because Her ultimate reality opens its gate exclusively to pure, non-dual realization (Jñāna). Every preliminary practice must eventually transform into direct awareness to step inside Her sanctuary.

Nāma 981

Word by word

ज्ञानज्ञेयस्वरूपिणी। — component of the name

Meaning

(i) One whose form is knowledge and the object known.

(ii) She is both the seer and the seen, knowledge and the knowable.

(iii) The distinction between knower, knowing and known resolves in Her.

Esoteric note

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya presents a master non-dual equation to collapse epistemological duality:

The Fusion of Subject and Object: Human tracking splits reality into a subject who looks (Dṛg / Jñāna) and an object that is looked at (Dṛśya / Jñeya). She is Jñānajñeyasvarūpiṇī because She is the single, non-dual energy field that manifests as both sides of the equation. There is no independent world out there separate from the light that sees it; the knower and the known are one substance.

Bhāskararāya details the ultimate geometric and physical seal of energy conservation:

The Seal of Primordial Source: Yonimudrā is the highly sacred, non-dual hand gesture that represents the matrix of creation. Internally, it refers to the primary inverted triangle enclosure that tightly wraps and protects the central point (Bindu). She is this seal, representing the absolute containment and conservation of spiritual power before it translates into manifestation.

Meaning

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya details the phonetic and physical mastery of this title:

The Master of the Three Blocks: Trikhaṇḍā is the definitive tenth mudrā that seals the entire Śrī Yantra ritual work. Phonetically, it refers to the three distinct blocks (khaṇḍas) of the supreme mantra—the Moon section (Soma), the Sun section (Sūrya), and the Fire section (Anala). She is the absolute Īśvarī (empress) who governs this entire triple structure, binding it into a single power loop.

The Weaver of Form: While She transcends qualities (Guṇātītā), She is simultaneously Triguṇā because She coordinates the three qualities (Sattva, Rajas, Tamas) to build the physical world. She acts as the master weaver who spins light, movement, and mass to construct the material universe.

The Primordial Maternal Source: The entire cosmic system of mantras, elements, and geometries dissolves into a single word—Ambā. She is the direct, unconditional mother of every living soul. She is the ultimate cause (jagat-kāraṇa) that provides love, protection, and the necessary path inputs to guide Her children home.

She remains a pristine, unblemished template of absolute purity, clearing away the errors of anyone who enters Her space.

The Momentum of Realization: She cannot be uncovered by a casual or distracted interest. This continuous momentum clears away the oldest layers of mental habits, revealing the Self.

Transcending the Six Pathways: The entire universe is structured across six major operational pathways (ṣaḍ-adhvā), split into the sound track (Śabda-adhvā: Varṇa, Pada, Mantra) and the object track (Artha-adhvā: Kalā, Tattva, Bhuvana). She is Ṣaḍadhvātītarūpiṇī because Her essential unconditioned nature sits completely above and outside this entire structural framework, serving as the raw consciousness that supports the path grid.

She is an open reality accessible to anyone who approaches with a clean heart.

She is Śrīśivā because She contains both traits simultaneously, ensuring that Her path provides earthly support alongside spiritual freedom.

In the Saubhāgyabhāskara, Bhāskararāya delivers the definitive theological crown of the text:

The Non-Dual Oneness: As the Sahasranāma reaches its penultimate peak, this name removes any remaining dualistic filters. Shiva (pure, still consciousness) and Shakti (dynamic, creative energy) are not two separate entities sitting together. They exist in a state of absolute, perfect fusion (Sāmarasya) — like heat inside fire. She is this exact non-dual unity. Duality is merely Her unity displaying its options, anchoring the seeker in absolute oneness.

Nāma 1000

ललिताम्बिका

Samāsa-vigraha

ललतेऽसौ ललिता च साम्बिका च।

Word by word

ललिता — playful; beautiful

ललिताम्बिका। — component of the name

Meaning

(i) One who is the beautiful Mother called Lalita.

(ii) This is the concluding name of the thousand names. The hymn begins with Sreemata, Mother, and ends with Ambika, Mother.

(iii) Though She is Brahman, devotees can easily approach Her as Mother. Lalita means She who plays, She who is beautiful, and She who, through divine sport, creates and sustains the universe. At the end of this name, Om is to be pronounced.

Esoteric note

Bhāskararāya concludes this thousand-name milestone by anchoring Her identity within playful compassion:

The Ultimate Playful Mother: The word ललिता (Lalitā) defines Her core style: She acts with absolute charm, effortless ease, and playful elegance (Lalita), managing universes without friction. She links this play directly to Her role as अम्बिका (Ambikā — the deeply compassionate mother). She runs the grand play of the cosmos to guide, protect, and love Her children. This name seals the text, confirming that the ultimate absolute is a mother who welcomes the practitioner home with open arms.
